## 3. Decision ledger (forward-looking)

The rest of this file is the locked decision ledger. Every PR must
justify changes against this list. New decisions are appended at the
bottom; old decisions are amended in-place with a dated note when
superseded.

### Source & scope

1. Data source: **Dhan API only** (single-source vendor lock for v1)
2. Universe: **NIFTY 50, BANKNIFTY, SENSEX spot + India VIX volatility index** (was: 8 F&O indices + ~215 stocks; **amended 2026-05-15** from 3 → 4 instruments per user scope expansion, see decisions #71-72). **Amended 2026-05-22 (DEC-P0-063, entry #200):** Track 1 INGEST scope expanded to additionally cover **200 NSE F&O eligible single stocks (spot + options across all 4 Dhan expiryCodes)** — the LAKE grows; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE stays at the 3 brute-force indexes (REFERENCE_ONLY grows from {India VIX} to {India VIX + 200 stocks}, mirroring decision #83). Lake design: de-rolled by absolute strike; zero-data-loss guarantee enforced per quarantine + gap-detection + audit-replay. See entry #200.
3. Tradability: **NONE — signal-only research** (was: F&O execution)
4. Range: **Rolling `2021-01-01 → today`** (**amended 2026-05-15** from fixed 2021-05-15 → 2026-05-15 window per user scope expansion, see decision #75)
5. Range source: `POST /v2/charts/intraday` (1m, 90-day chunks) + `POST /v2/charts/historical` (daily)
6. Native timeframes: 1/5/15/25/60 min + 1d (was: incorrectly claimed 21)
7. Resampled timeframes: **19 derived intraday TFs from 1m base** (**amended 2026-05-15** from 14 derived per user scope expansion to 21 total, see decisions #73-74)
8. Money unit: int64 paisa throughout
9. Exchange segment: `IDX_I` for ALL 4 Track 1 instruments (single Index segment per Dhan annexure verified 2026-05-15; there is no separate `BSE_I`)
10. securityId: never hardcoded; resolved from `api-scrip-master-detailed.csv` at startup

### Indicators (9)

11. EMA 20, EMA 200, Day High, Day Low, PDH, PDL, Daily Pivots (P, R1-R3, S1-S3), Static Daily Fib (12 levels), Candle metadata
12. VWAP dropped (no volume on spot)
13. Day high definition: `day_high[t] = max(day_high[t-1], high[t])` — no resample leak
14. PDH/PDL anchor: previous TRADING day (skips holidays)
15. Fib anchor: yesterday's H→L; extensions in trade direction

### Vocabulary

16. 52 atomic conditions, organised into 9 groups
17. K ∈ {2, 3, 4, 5} ANDed per strategy
18. AND only — no OR / mixed boolean
19. ~2.9M raw patterns → ~1.2-1.5M after conflict-graph pruning
20. Direction parameter (bull/bear) is separate from the 52 bits
21. Tolerances in basis points (bps), NOT absolute points

### Exit modes

22. Mode A (SL/TP-based): ~2.76M params per pattern
23. Mode B (signal-exit): ~500K params per pattern
24. Both modes brute-forced in parallel
25. 10-condition exit vocabulary for Mode B
26. Entry: bar OPEN of (signal_bar + 1)
27. Always candle CLOSE for signal; never bar touch
28. Forced 15:20 IST exit always active

### PnL & cost model

29. paper_pnl_paisa only (single column)
30. Brokerage, STT, GST, stamp duty: REMOVED (spot doesn't trade)
31. Slippage: ZERO
32. Position size: % of notional capital (Phase 2 will lot-round for options)

### Search pipeline

33. 5-stage smart-staged: Stage 1A → 1B → 2 → 3 → 4
34. Stage 1A: pattern discovery on NIFTY 15m only (~90 sec wall)
35. Stage 1B: expand top 50K patterns to all 45 inst-TF (~40 sec wall)
36. Stage 2: full param brute force on top 10K combos (~33B trials)
37. Stage 3: Bayesian CMA-ES refine top 100 (~15-20 min)
38. Stage 4: 4-filter cascade (DSR/CPCV/WFO/Lockbox) → final 3

### Statistical filters

39. DSR with effective-N (Bailey-LdP correlation clustering)
40. CPCV (Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation)
41. WFO (Walk-Forward Optimization)
42. Lockbox: Dec 2025 - May 2026 held-out window

### Throughput & SLA

43. Target sustained throughput: 80-150K trials/sec on 10-core M4 Pro
44. Sweep wall time: **2-4 days on M4 Pro** (was: 10-13 hours, 5-15x optimistic)
45. CPU budget: 10 P-cores used; 4 E-cores reserved for OS + daily apps (14-core M4 Pro)
46. Memory tiling required: by (instrument, TF, day-window) bucket

### Dedup & audit

47. SHA256+Bloom+LMDB dedup
48. Timeframe IS part of the hash (different TF = different combo)
49. Bloom filter: ~5 GB sized for **survivors-only** (~150M-1B post-threshold-filter combos), giving FPR ≈ 1e-12 to 0. NOT sized for raw 33B trials (which would give FPR ≈ 56%). Math sanity-checked 2026-05-15 evening (decision #98)
50. LMDB: stores only result survivors, not every trial
51. Hash-chained JSONL audit with selective material-event logging
52. Audit replay test = the reproducibility oracle

### Storage

53. Result Parquet: ~50-100 GB per sweep (threshold-filtered)
54. failures.parquet: ~500 MB for audit completeness
55. ~80-160 sweeps fit in 8 TB SSD

### Verification (the 99.9% assurance path)

56. 9-layer test pyramid (Unit/Property/Golden/Integration/Bench/Stress/Smoke/Fuzz/Mutation)
57. 24 property invariants (hypothesis + proptest, 500 examples each)
58. 3 oracle tests: audit-log replay, Python-Rust parity, 52-condition spec table
59. O(1) ratio bench gate: `p99(N=1M) / p99(N=1K) ≤ 1.1`
60. Mutation testing: mutmut + cargo-mutants ≥ 85%
61. Coverage gate: 100% line + 100% branch (Python); 100% line + 95% branch (Rust)

### Indian microstructure

62. Pre-open 09:00-09:15 bars dropped at ingest
63. Muhurat dates excluded by hardcoded list (Samvat 2078-2083)
64. NIFTY 50 / SENSEX reconstitution dates flagged in audit
65. Circuit breaker halts: drop full day
66. Half-day sessions (Ram Navami etc.) honoured by calendar

### Engineering

67. Top-level package strategy: fresh `brutex/v2/` subpackage in Phase 2 (Track 1 lives in subpackage; old `brutex/*` modules deprecate progressively)
68. Rust hot kernel: extends existing `rust/fno-math/`
69. 8-12 week build timeline (Phase 0-4)
70. 4-agent hostile-review pattern at each phase end

Probability 4-day claim holds in production: **55-65%** (Agent X worst-case audit). 18 precision risks identified (Agent 5 audit) — 4 CRITICAL (no `bar_hash` in code, no `int64 paisa` columns, resampler UTC-anchor bug, this Bloom math bug — first 3 already in Phase 1/2 plan). 99. **AWS removed from escalation matrix + Metal GPU promoted to Tier 2 required scaling lever** (user-confirmed 2026-05-15 evening). No cloud, no sharding — Track 1 is LOCAL-ONLY. Apple 20-core Metal GPU (already in M4 Pro) is the only hardware escalation path. Updated contingency SLA matrix in TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md §2.1: added new top tier "≥ 300K t/s (CPU + GPU) → 1-2 days" with Phase 3.5 Metal kernel.
100. **Stage 2.5 — Bayesian adaptive early-stop locked** (2026-05-15 evening, Plan-agent design). Hybrid Bayesian posterior (Gaussian conjugate on 95th-percentile Sharpe) + Wald-style decision rule. Empirical-Bayes prior fit from Stage 1B Sharpe distribution. Prune if Pr(true Sharpe ≤ Stage-1B median) ≥ 0.95; promote if Pr(true Sharpe ≥ Stage-1B 99th pctile) ≥ 0.99. Hard floor 50K trials before decision + 10% of param surface. Expected 61% Stage-2 wall reduction (33B → ~13B effective). Verified by **P-25 + P-26 property invariants** (new) AND `tests/integration/test_stage2_5_no_winner_loss.py` A/B oracle (top-3 recall ≥ 95%; rolling 30d miss-rate budget ≤ 5% triggers auto α_prune raise to 0.98). References: Wald 1947 Sequential Analysis (Dover); Gelman BDA3 Ch. 2.5 (CRC 2013); Efron-Hastie 2016 Ch. 6 (Cambridge UP). Phase 2.5 implementation, 1 week effort, sits between Phase 2 and Phase 3 in build plan. Full design at `docs/TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §2`.
101. **Phase 3.5 — Apple Metal GPU offload locked** (2026-05-15 evening, Plan-agent design). Local M4 Pro 20-core GPU only (NO CUDA / NO OpenCL / NO AWS). Workload split: bitmask AND (3-5× projected) + indicator precompute (5-10× projected) on GPU; trade simulation stays on CPU (branchy). Apple unified memory (`MTLResourceStorageModeShared`) = zero PCIe copy. Rust↔Metal via `metal` crate v0.27 + `objc2` v0.5, gated `#[cfg(target_os="macos", target_arch="aarch64")]`. Bitmask kernel threadgroup (32, 8) = 256 threads, batch 8192 strats × 94K bars (~850 KB per batch fits L2). CI gate `tests/bench/test_metal_kernel_speedup.py` asserts ≥ 2× CPU baseline + bit-exact numerical parity + audit-replay byte-identical Parquet. Fallback `BRUTEX_GPU_OFFLOAD=0` env flag → CPU-only path unchanged (no quality impact, just slower). Projected blended speedup ~2× → 33B wall 1-2 days CPU+GPU vs 2-4 days CPU-only. Phase 3.5 implementation, 3-4 weeks effort, sits after Phase 3 in build plan. Full design at `docs/TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §3`.
102. **Combined optimization impact projected (Phase 2.5 + Phase 3.5 stacked)**: effective trials drop 33B → ~13B (Stage 2.5 prune); throughput rises 100K → 200-300K t/s (Phase 3.5 GPU); combined 33B-equivalent wall time drops to **~10-20 hours = 1 overnight session (22:00-07:00 IST) on M4 Pro alone, no cloud**. Subject to Phase 3 + 3.5 + 2.5 canary validation; SLA bands in spec §2.1 self-amend if measurements differ. Updated contingency matrix at `TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §8` shows how Phase 2.5 + Phase 3.5 each shift the published SLA — combined they buy 3 full SLA tiers without hardware escalation.

108. **DEC-RISK-011 — INTRADAY-ONLY LOCK MADE EXPLICIT** (2026-05-16 evening, operator confirmation). Previously implied via Track 1 §7 "forced exit 15:20 IST" but never written as a single rule. Now explicit in `TRACK2_RISK_MGMT.md §2A`: Track 2 is intraday-only, MIS product only, NO NRML, NO overnight positions ever, NO held-to-expiry, NO weekend exposure, NO BTST. Forced exit 15:20:00 IST with no overrides. Three Phase-1 property invariants enforce this: P-INTRA-1 (entry.date == exit.date), P-INTRA-2 (exit_dt = 15:20:00 IST unless circuit-close), P-INTRA-3 (09:16:00 ≤ entry_dt ≤ 15:01:00). Material cost-model simplifications: (a) expiry-day +2% additional ELM is INAPPLICABLE (no position at SOD on expiry); (b) CALCULATOR_SPEC §4.2 `EXPIRY_*` branches are forward-compat stubs only — Track 2 hard-codes `trade_outcome = "NORMAL_CLOSE"`; (c) no overnight margin-funding cost; (d) no T+1 settlement risk. Tax implication: every P&L is realized same-day, audit log emits `held_overnight: false` on every trade.

109. **DEC-RISK-012 — 09:15 candle USED as first signal-eval bar** (2026-05-16 evening, operator decision). Operator wants ALL available market data used; brute-force engine will discover empirically whether 09:16-entry strategies underperform 09:17-entry strategies, rather than prejudging via the auction-bar exclusion rule. Signal evaluation timeline locked in `TRACK2_RISK_MGMT.md §2A.2B`: at 09:16:00 IST (when bar "09:15" closes) signal evaluates using bar "09:15" data; if signal fires, entry executes at bar "09:16" OPEN price = 09:16:00 IST. Earliest possible entry execution = 09:16:00 IST. Latest possible entry execution = 15:01:00 IST (bar "15:00" close triggers signal; bar "15:01" OPEN executes). Forced-exit execution = 15:20:00 IST (bar "15:19" close triggers exit; bar "15:20" OPEN executes). Three additional property invariants P-INTRA-4/5/6 enforce these timestamps. Auction-bar caveat documented but not blocking — operator can revisit if empirical backtests show systematic degradation tied to the 09:15 bar.

110. **Track 2 Execution Simulator spec written** (`docs/track2/TRACK2_EXECUTION_SIMULATOR.md`). Bridges Track 1 brute-force winners to Track 2 real-money option replay. For each top-10 Track 1 combo, the simulator sweeps all 21 strikes (ATM ± 10) per signal, applies the full cost stack (CALCULATOR_SPEC.md), applies slippage (TRACK2_OPTIONS_SPEC §9), applies liquidity filter (TRACK2_RISK_MGMT §4.3), and emits ranked results by Deflated Sharpe Ratio. Pipeline = Stage 5.1 signal replay → 5.2 strike sweep → 5.3 cost+slippage → 5.4 liquidity filter → 5.5 rank+report. Cardinality: ~315K trade candidates per 10-combo batch, ~220K accepted, ~95K rejected by liquidity, total wall time ~11 sec parallelizable. Output schema = one row per (combo_hash × strike_offset × direction × instrument). Seven decision IDs DEC-EXEC-001 through DEC-EXEC-007 covering 21-strike sweep, liquidity filter audit, DSR ranking, MIN_TRADES_THRESHOLD=30, NORMAL_CLOSE hard-code, and post-Track-1 timing.

111. **DEC-EXEC-008 — BUY-ONLY POLICY** (2026-05-16 evening, operator decision). REVISED from earlier draft that had Track 2 sweep BUY+SELL sides per strike. Operator clarified: Track 2 NEVER writes/shorts options. Sides set ∈ {`long_call`, `long_put`} only. Cost calculator's `short_call` / `short_put` branches in CALCULATOR_SPEC §4 are forward-compat stubs that Track 2 hard-codes away. Rationale: (a) retail-intraday focus — option-writing requires SPAN+ELM ₹1-2 lakh margins per lot that don't fit profile; (b) asymmetric risk — short-option max-loss is unbounded; long-option max-loss = premium paid (bounded); (c) STT structure favors buyers (no STT-on-entry for long-side); (d) simplifies risk management — no margin-call risk. Per-signal candidate count drops 42 → 21 (one side only). Total Stage 5 wall time drops ~22 sec → ~11 sec. Property invariant P-EXEC-8 enforces `side in {long_call, long_put}`.

BULL spot signal → BUY CE only. BEAR spot signal → BUY PE only. NOT both CE and PE on the same signal. This is NOT a straddle simulator and NOT a strangle simulator. NO spreads in Track 2 (out of scope per Track 2 master spec). Property invariant P-EXEC-9 enforces (BULL → CE) AND (BEAR → PE).

325. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONCURRENCY-001 — the universe pull now runs TRULY parallel (~8 r/s, not ~3 r/s sequential): drop the whole-call SDK lock (the Groww SDK is thread-safe) + relabel "pending"→"no F&O"** (operator runs 2026-05-30: the two-phase pull crawled at ~3 r/s despite the 8-worker pool + start-8 bucket — "why fetching slow... 8 rps parallel right?"). Two coupled fixes on the Performance + Observability rungs.

    **(A) Root cause + fix — the SDK is thread-safe; the serialization lock was unnecessary.** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319) finding #6 added `_SdkRemintGuard.call` holding a lock around EVERY SDK call, on the assumption the shared `growwapi.GrowwAPI` was not concurrency-safe. **HARD-VERIFIED against growwapi 1.5.0 `groww/client.py` (CLAUDE.md §6):** `_request_get`/`_request_post` call the module-level `requests.get`/`requests.post` directly — each spins up + closes its OWN ephemeral session; there is NO shared `requests.Session` on the client. So concurrent calls on one shared `GrowwAPI` ARE thread-safe, and the whole-call lock pinned all 8 `PoolRunParallel` workers to one-at-a-time (~3 r/s = 1/round-trip-latency, never reaching the 8-r/s bucket cap). The new `brutex/adapters/groww/remint_guard.py::RemintGuard` (pure, 100% line+branch, 14 tests) runs `fn()` LOCK-FREE — the 8 workers fetch truly concurrently under the shared start-8/slow-decrement `AdaptiveTokenBucket` — and locks ONLY the one-shot token re-mint (a long phase outlives one 6 AM-IST token, CLAUDE.md §6): the first auth-failed worker `auth.refresh()` + rebinds both fetchers under the lock (latch-bounded), others retry against the fresh client. `cli._build_remint_guard` is the thin live wiring (coverage-omitted). The tighter auth fingerprints also fix the prior `_is_auth_error` false-positive (it matched bare "invalid"/"token", so an "invalid expiry_date" bad-request needlessly re-minted).

    **(B) Honest coverage label — "pending" → "no F&O".** A cell fetched with 0 expiries (e.g. SENSEX 2020-22: BSE options started ~2023; 360ONE: F&O-eligible ~2025; ABB ~2022) was shown as "… pending", which LOOKS in-progress though it is terminal "fetched, confirmed no F&O for that year" (operator: "should be fetched-but-no-data, not pending"). The `/coverage` row now reads "○ no F&O" (terminal mark + label, not "… pending") + the KPI "no F&O (no data)". The status CONSTANT stays `STATUS_PENDING` (terminal, settled, kept out of `to_repull` for past years) — only the display relabels; the classification is unchanged + correct.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `remint_guard.py` is 100% line+branch (14 tests); `cli._build_remint_guard` + the `coverage.html` relabel are coverage-omitted glue/template. The honest throughput ceiling is **~4-6 r/s sustained (~45-85 min for the ~19k-job contracts phase), NOT a guaranteed 8** — Groww's per-minute backtesting cap is UNVERIFIED (CLAUDE.md §6), so an 8-wide burst likely forces the adaptive slow-decrement to 4; the fix removes the artificial serializer so the shared bucket (start-8, slow-decrement-to-4 on 429s, recover) is the real governor — exactly the operator's model. SDK thread-safety was verified by READING the installed wheel source (growwapi installed in the dev container for introspection ONLY — NOT added to project deps, CLAUDE.md §6; uninstalled after). Hostile review: the per-worker-client-pool design was considered + REJECTED in favour of the simpler lock-drop once the SDK was proven thread-safe; the review's "acquire holds the lock across sleep" concern was checked + found already lock-free (`rate_limiter.py` releases the lock before `self.sleep`). **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-CONCURRENCY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319, the 8-worker pool + bucket) · DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 (#321, the two-phase runners) · DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001 (#320, honest coverage labels) · CLAUDE.md §6 / §9 / §10.

324. **DEC-DASHBOARD-WIPE-001 — dashboard "Delete all ingested data" button: SQL-truncate the lake DATA tables via the OPEN connection (no close/reopen → no DuckDB segfault)** (operator runs 2026-05-30: after `make wipe` the running dashboard still showed the deleted lake because uvicorn held the file open — "next start should run from scratch"; the operator wanted a one-click in-dashboard wipe with no restart). PR-2 of the wipe feature (PR-1 = the `brutex wipe` CLI, DEC-DATA-WIPE-001 #322). **Design A** from the 4-agent hostile review (truncate-via-open-connection), NOT Design B (close/reopen — deferred to a future PR with its own §9 review).

    **Why truncate, not close→reopen (the review's decisive call):** `db_view.sample_rows` issues TWO executes (COUNT then SELECT) and RELEASES the store `RLock` between them; a wipe that `close()`d the connection in that gap would free it under a live cursor → DuckDB native segfault. Truncating instead runs as ONE `InstrumentStore.wipe_lake_tables()` method under the `_StoreMeta` lock, so a concurrent `/db` read sees the full table or the empty table — ACID/MVCC-consistent, never a crash.

    **Pure 100%-tested cores:**
    - `brutex/data/lake_wipe.py` — `LAKE_DATA_TABLES` (the authoritative wipe set: instruments · instrument_runs · expiries · contracts · **coverage_ledger**, EXCLUDING `schema_meta`) + `truncate_lake_tables(execute, *, count, tables)` (per-table `DELETE FROM`, continue-past-failure, `LakeWipeReport(deleted, failed)`). **`coverage_ledger` is included** so `/coverage` doesn't keep showing stale cells (a real correctness bug the review caught — `db_view.KNOWN_TABLES` omits it); `schema_meta` excluded so the version row isn't orphaned.
    - `brutex/dashboard/wipe_view.py` — the HTTP guards: `parse_wipe_confirmation` (typed `WIPE`), `wipe_refusal_reason` (refuse while a pull phase is mid-write), `is_same_origin` (CSRF guard for the destructive POST), `wipe_report_payload`.

    **Glue (coverage-omitted):** `InstrumentStore.wipe_lake_tables()` (one locked method calling the pure core); `POST /api/v1/db/wipe` (same-origin → typed-`WIPE` body → refuse-if-pull-running → truncate → audit-log → JSON report); a "🗑 Delete all ingested data" danger-zone button on `/universe` (prompt → type WIPE → fetch JSON POST; every interpolated value XSS-escaped).

    **Z+ defensive layers:** DETECT (per-table counts in the report) · VERIFY (typed-`WIPE` + same-origin) · RECONCILE (`LakeWipeReport` deleted/failed) · PREVENT (atomic-under-store-lock truncate — no close → no segfault; refuse-while-pulling; CSRF) · AUDIT (`dashboard.wipe.requested`/`.done` structlog) · RECOVER (per-table continue-past-failure) · COOLDOWN (the typed-`WIPE` prompt).

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `lake_wipe.py` + `wipe_view.py` are 100% line+branch (24 tests); the store method + route + button are coverage-omitted glue. This empties ROWS (the operator's 236 / 6,053 / 249,409 → 0, `/db` updates instantly with NO restart); DuckDB does NOT shrink the file on `DELETE`, and credentials / token / audit are NOT touched — a true file-level clean slate is `make wipe` with the server stopped (DEC-DATA-WIPE-001 #322). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-WIPE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-DATA-WIPE-001 (#322) · DEC-STORE-THREADSAFE-001 (#317-A, the `_StoreMeta` lock) · DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 (`db_view`) · CLAUDE.md §9 / §10 / §11.

323. **DEC-PULL-TIMEOUT-DEFER-001 — the hung-SDK-call timeout (DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 finding #5) is DEFERRED, not patched: the watchdog "fix" was hostile-reviewed as actively UNSAFE, and every SDK-free alternative is unverifiable while `growwapi` is not a test dependency** (operator decision 2026-05-30, AskUserQuestion: "Defer + document why"). Closes the open follow-up from entry #321 finding #5 by RECORDING the limitation as a locked, understood decision rather than shipping a worse-than-the-disease mitigation (priority law: Correctness > Reliability > … ; Golden Rule #10 honest limits).

    **Root problem.** The Groww SDK sets no client socket timeout (`build_session=GrowwAPI` is the bare constructor — `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py:233`), so a `get_expiries`/`get_contracts` call against a silently-dead host blocks its `PoolRunParallel` worker until the OS TCP layer eventually errors. Finding #5 tracked "add a session-level timeout so a hang becomes a retryable `VendorSdkError`".

    **Why the obvious fix (a deadline watchdog) was REJECTED — 1-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9 / §12 refactor-tier):**
    - **CRITICAL (single-flight violation).** Python cannot kill a thread blocked in a C-level socket read. A watchdog (`future.result(timeout=…)`) can only ABANDON the in-flight thread, which keeps executing `sdk.get_*` on the SHARED, non-thread-safe SDK object. `retry_call` then issues a SECOND concurrent call on that same `requests.Session` / connection pool — with the `_SdkRemintGuard` lock no longer held — reintroducing the exact race `_SdkRemintGuard` was added to prevent (entry #321 finding #6). That is STRICTLY WORSE than the documented one-wedged-worker limitation.
    - **HIGH (self-saturation).** A bounded guard pool fills with leaked threads from dead hosts; once full, `submit()` itself blocks and the watchdog stops watching.
    - **HIGH (lifecycle).** The guard pool's non-daemon threads + a leaked hung thread block `shutdown(wait=True)` and interpreter exit.

    **Why the SDK-free alternatives are unverifiable (Golden Rule #1 — `growwapi` is deliberately NOT a unit-test dependency, CLAUDE.md §6 + `client.py` docstring, so its HTTP internals cannot be inspected here):** `socket.setdefaulttimeout(T)` reliably bounds the CONNECT phase (`socket.create_connection` honours the global default) but `urllib3` sets its own per-read socket timeout, so when `requests` is called with `timeout=None` the READ phase likely blocks regardless — and the common hang IS a read hang. UNVERIFIABLE without the SDK + its `requests`/`urllib3` versions installed; also process-global (it would touch every blocking socket in the uvicorn process during the pull).

    **The TRUE fix (still tracked, not done here):** pass an explicit `(connect, read)` timeout into the SDK's `requests.Session` at `GrowwAuth.build_session` so a hang surfaces as `requests.exceptions.Timeout` → translated to the retryable neutral `VendorAPITimeoutException`. This requires `growwapi` installed as a (CI-gated, offline-suite-excluded) integration dependency so the wiring + the timeout path can be VERIFIED, not guessed. Re-opens as a dedicated PR when that dependency lands.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10).** The hang case today is MITIGATED, not eliminated: blast radius is one wedged worker, bounded by (a) `retry_call`'s finite `max_attempts=10`, (b) the operator re-click (the O(1) `cells_to_pull` / `contract_jobs_to_pull` skip resumes only genuinely-new work — entry #321), and (c) per-cell failure capture (one dead cell never aborts the run — `PoolRunParallel` captures, never propagates). No code changes in this entry — docs only; the brute-force ENGINE and the adapter are untouched (Golden Rule #3 scope lock). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-TIMEOUT-DEFER-001. **Amends:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 (#321, finding #5). **Builds on:** entry #321 finding #6 (`_SdkRemintGuard`) · DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319, `retry_call`) · CLAUDE.md §6 (growwapi not a unit-test dep) · §9 (hostile review) · §10 (honest limits) · §13 (priority law).

322. **DEC-DATA-WIPE-001 — `brutex wipe` / `make wipe`: one-command total wipe of all persisted BruteX data (lake + credentials + token + audit + logs)** (operator runs 2026-05-30: deleting the repo folder did NOT clear the dashboard's 236 instruments / 6,053 expiries / 249,409 contracts — because ALL state lives under `$HOME/.brutex`, deliberately OUTSIDE the repo so an expensive ingest survives a re-clone; the operator chose to ADD an explicit wiper rather than relocate storage into the repo). PR-1 of 2: the pure core + CLI (the dashboard "Wipe all data" button is the separately-reviewed PR-2, per the hostile review's split).

    **Pure 100%-tested core (`brutex/wipe.py` + `brutex/config/paths.py`, line+branch):**
    - `wipe_targets(env, home, cwd)` enumerates `$HOME/.brutex` + the in-repo `./.brutex-logs` (make-run's default log dir) + any of the EIGHT `BRUTEX_*` overrides (`OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` registry — lake / credentials / token / log-dir / log-file / runtime / **audit** / live-subjects) that resolve OUTSIDE the home dir. ONE registry so a new override can't be silently forgotten by the wiper (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON).
    - `assert_safe(path, home, cwd)` is a strict RESOLVED-path ALLOWLIST (irreversible op → default-deny): it REFUSES a symlinked target, the filesystem root + too-shallow paths, `$HOME` and any ancestor of it, and the repo/cwd and any ancestor of it — so a mis-set `BRUTEX_LAKE_ROOT=$HOME` or a `~/.brutex`→`$HOME` symlink can never become `rm -rf $HOME`. Proven by a hostile override-matrix test (`=$HOME`, `=/`, symlink → all refused).
    - `execute_wipe(..., dry_run, rmtree/unlink/exists/is_dir injected)` re-validates EACH target through `assert_safe` at delete time (defence in depth), continues past per-target failures, and returns `WipeReport(removed, absent, failed, dry_run)`.
    - `config/paths.py` extracts the canonical `brutex_home()` + `resolve_lake_root()`; `cli._resolve_lake_root` + `cmd_run` now DELEGATE to it (de-dups the two pre-existing inline copies — review #11, COMMON).

    **CLI glue (`brutex wipe` / `make wipe` — coverage-omitted):** dry-run by DEFAULT (`brutex wipe` / `make wipe-dry` only PREVIEW the plan); `--execute` (`make wipe`) deletes only after a typed `WIPE` confirmation on an interactive TTY (or `--yes` for non-interactive / CI); REFUSES while a dashboard is running (`server_is_running` via `read_runtime_file` + `is_pid_alive`, so a CLI wipe never rm's the lake out from under a live server); prints + `structlog`-logs the plan before any deletion.

    **Z+ defensive layers:** DETECT (dry-run preview) · VERIFY (`assert_safe` re-check at delete time) · RECONCILE (`WipeReport` removed/absent/failed) · PREVENT (strict allowlist + symlink refusal + server-running guard + typed-`WIPE` + dry-run default) · AUDIT (plan printed + logged pre-delete; the in-home audit chain is itself part of the wipe, so its destruction is logged to stdout/run-log) · RECOVER (continue-past-failure; the `failed` bucket surfaces partial state) · COOLDOWN (the typed-`WIPE` confirm gate).

    **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) — caught + fixed before code (irreversible delete → maximally adversarial):** CRITICAL symlink bypass of the lexical guard (→ refuse symlinks + resolve real paths); CRITICAL override→`$HOME`/`/`/repo deletion (→ strict resolved-path allowlist + hostile override-matrix test); HIGH missed `BRUTEX_AUDIT_PATH` / `BRUTEX_LIVE_SUBJECTS_FILE` (→ added to the registry); MAJOR dry-run-not-default + `--yes` too hot (→ dry-run default + typed-`WIPE` on TTY); MAJOR partial-failure had no bucket (→ `failed` list + continue-on-error); plus the COMMON resolver de-dup (#11). The CRITICAL dashboard close-mid-read crash (#3) + the store holder/lock surgery are DEFERRED to PR-2 (the review's explicit split — they touch the just-merged pull/threading code + can segfault DuckDB, so they earn their own 4-agent review).

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `wipe.py` + `paths.py` are 100% line+branch (real tmp-dir + real-symlink + injected-failure tests); `cli.py` + Makefile are coverage-omitted glue. The CLI wipe DELETES files (a true clean slate when the server is stopped). The dashboard button (PR-2) will REOPEN an empty lake (a fresh tiny `.duckdb`, not bit-for-bit nothing) — it will be labelled "Delete all ingested data", not "total wipe", to avoid overclaiming. **Decision ID:** DEC-DATA-WIPE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (#160, the lean lake) · DEC-AUTO-UNIVERSE-001 · DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 (#321) · CLAUDE.md §11 (COMMON) · §9 (hostile review) · §10 (honest limits).

321. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 — two-phase pull (ALL expiries → ALL contracts) + O(1) incremental skip + manual buttons, replacing the per-cell interleave + auto-pull** (operator decree 2026-05-30: "only pull all the expiries at first, only after the successful pull of these alone then contracts"; "remove the auto pull"; "two buttons under /universe — fetch all expiries / fetch all contracts"; "re-click → only the newly rows … once pulled successfully don't fetch the same again"). Supersedes the per-cell interleave of DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319).

    **Landing in stages on one branch (this entry covers the tested backend foundation; the /universe buttons + route wiring + auto-pull removal are the focused follow-up on the same decision):**

    - **(A) Two-phase core — `brutex/orchestrator/universe_phases.py` (pure, 100% line+branch, 37 tests).** `run_two_phase` runs Phase 1 (every `(exchange, underlying, year)` expiry cell via the injected `run_parallel`) to completion behind a STRUCTURAL barrier — the Phase-1 iterable is fully drained before a single contract job is built — then Phase 2 derives jobs ONLY from discovered expiries (`contract_jobs_from`, O(1) set dedup) and fetches them. The "never jump to contracts early" invariant is asserted directly (`test_no_contract_before_all_expiries`). A failed cell is recorded + skipped for Phase 2 (no expiries ⇒ no jobs) so one dead cell never blocks the run.

    - **(B) O(1) incremental skip (the "don't re-fetch what's already pulled" requirement) — immutability by time, not "pulled once = never".** `cells_to_pull` skips a PAST year already settled (its expiry calendar is immutable) but ALWAYS re-pulls the current year (new expiries appear) + any unsettled/failed cell. `contract_jobs_to_pull` skips an EXPIRED expiry already pulled (its contract set is immutable) but ALWAYS re-pulls a not-yet-expired expiry (new strikes list as the underlying moves). `settled_expiry_cells` builds the skip set from coverage rows (complete/pending = settled; failed excluded so failures retry). Each filter is one `frozenset` membership ⇒ O(1) per item, so a daily re-click issues only genuinely-new API calls (the persisted upsert PK is the second dedup line). Honest: the bulk pull is still O(N) API calls, Groww-rate-bound (Golden Rule #10) — what is O(1) is the per-item skip/dedup.

    - **(C) Production concurrency primitive — `brutex/orchestrator/parallel.py::PoolRunParallel` (100% line+branch, 7 tests).** A bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` (default 8 workers, matching the start-8 r/s budget of #319) mapping a fetcher over a worklist, yielding one `ItemResult` as each future completes; a fetcher exception is CAPTURED (never propagated) so the phase can't abort. Pool torn down per call (no thread leak).

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this entry is the **tested backend foundation** — `universe_phases.py` + `parallel.py` are both 100% line+branch (44 tests), mypy-strict + pyright + ruff clean. It is NOT yet wired to a caller: the two `/universe` buttons ("Fetch all expiries" / "Fetch all contracts"), their POST routes (building the `settled` sets from the store, driving `run_two_phase` in a background thread), and the REMOVAL of the startup auto-pull (`should_auto_pull_universe` + the `cmd_dashboard` background pull) are the focused follow-up PR on this same decision + branch — deliberately separated because that glue spans the 2123-line `/universe` template + the dashboard app (coverage-excluded), and is safest as its own reviewed change. A full 4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9, mandatory for the live-API concurrency wiring) runs on that follow-up. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319, superseded interleave) · DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001 (#320) · DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001.

    **Stage 2 — the wiring + buttons + auto-pull removal (the follow-up promised above, now landed under the same DEC-ID):**

    - **(D) Skip-set builders — `settled_expiry_cells` + `settled_contract_jobs`** (pure, in `universe_phases.py`; the merged Stage-1 had the *consumers* `cells_to_pull`/`contract_jobs_to_pull` but not the *producers*). `settled_expiry_cells` maps coverage `(exchange, underlying, year, status)` rows → the Phase-1 skip frozenset (complete/pending settled; failed excluded). `settled_contract_jobs` maps distinct `(exchange, underlying, expiry)` contract rows → the Phase-2 skip frozenset. Both built in one O(R) pass; downstream membership O(1). 100% line+branch (the module is now 42 tests).

    - **(E) Live two-phase runners — `cli._run_expiries_phase` / `cli._run_contracts_phase`** (`# pragma: no cover` — live creds + SDK + DuckDB + threads). INDEPENDENT (operator's "fully independent buttons" choice): Phase 1 refreshes the master, derives the lake underlyings, applies `cells_to_pull(settled_expiry_cells(list_coverage), current_year)`, fans expiry fetches out via `PoolRunParallel`, persists a coverage row per cell. Phase 2 reads ONLY the persisted expiries (`store.list_expiries`) — so contracts can never precede expiries across clicks — applies `contract_jobs_to_pull(settled_contract_jobs(list_contracts), today)`, fetches via `PoolRunParallel`; with no expiries persisted it returns a `needs_expiries_first` no-op. Shared `_build_universe_fetchers` (8→4 r/s bucket, lean leg→underlying metadata).

    - **(F) Routes + buttons + single-flight — `POST /api/v1/universe/fetch-expiries` · `POST …/fetch-contracts` · `GET …/phase-status`** (app.py, coverage-excluded). Each POST launches its phase in a daemon thread under a `threading.Lock` single-flight guard (a second click while running → `already_running`; the flag clears in `finally` so a crashed phase retries), and requires Groww creds (actionable 400 otherwise). `/universe` gains "① Fetch all expiries" + "② Fetch all contracts" buttons that POST then poll `/phase-status` to enable/disable while running (the two phases independent ⇒ one running never disables the other); all interpolation HTML-escaped; progress read from `/coverage` + `/logs`.

    - **(G) Auto-pull REMOVED — `cmd_dashboard` no longer launches the startup `should_auto_pull_universe` background thread.** Nothing hits Groww until a button is clicked (operator decree "remove the auto pull"); the keyless instrument master still auto-loads so the list + buttons have data. `should_auto_pull_universe` stays as a tested-but-unwired pure helper (vulture-clean via its test).

    **Stage-2 honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the pure additions (`settled_*` builders) are 100% line+branch; the runners + routes + template are coverage-excluded glue (`# pragma: no cover` / `[tool.coverage] omit`) — their *decision* logic is the 100%-tested `universe_phases` + `parallel`. ruff + mypy-strict + pyright + vulture all clean; `app.py` pyright is `1 error, 1 warning` == base (no new findings). The bulk pull stays O(N) API calls (vendor-rate-bound, CLAUDE.md §6); O(1) is the per-item skip + the PK-keyed upsert dedup. **Same Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001.

    **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) — findings + fixes (all addressed before merge).** The mandatory review of the live-API + concurrency wiring caught and the same PR fixed:
    - **CRITICAL — exchange/underlying transposed** at the Phase-1 call site (`derive_lake_underlyings` yields `(underlying, exchange)`; `phase1_cells` unpacks `(exchange, underlying)`) → every expiry fetch would have hit `EXCHANGE_<symbol>` → AttributeError, Phase 1 discovering nothing + corrupt coverage rows + a dead skip. **Fixed** (swap at the call site) + a seam-shaped intent test.
    - **HIGH — "complete" with 0 contracts** misled `/coverage` (a Phase-1-only F&O cell read as done). **Fixed** with `STATUS_EXPIRIES_ONLY` (Phase 1 writes it; reconcile counts it separately, keeps it out of `to_repull`, and `is_complete`/`incomplete` require zero of it; Phase 2 upgrades it → complete).
    - **MAJOR — dropped auth re-mint** (a long phase outlives one Groww token). **Fixed** via `_SdkRemintGuard`: one-shot `auth.refresh()` + rebind both fetchers under a lock on an auth error.
    - **MAJOR (pre-existing on main, now mitigated) — shared SDK across N pool workers.** **Fixed** by serialising every SDK call behind the same `_SdkRemintGuard` lock (≈free — the 8 r/s bucket already near-serialises).
    - **MED-HIGH — silent setup-failure swallow** in `_start_phase._run` (regressed DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001). **Fixed** — `_LOG.exception("universe.phase.failed", …)` before return.
    - **MINOR — single-flight latch** if `thread.start()` raises. **Fixed** — flag reset + logged on start failure.
    - **MED — dead `should_auto_pull_universe`** after auto-pull removal. **Fixed** — function + its test deleted (Golden Rule #10, not left as tested-but-unreachable).
    - **🚫 KNOWN LIMITATION (#5, not fixed here, honestly disclosed) — no socket timeout on the Groww expiry/contract SDK calls.** A hung call would block a pool worker until it returns (the SDK sets no client timeout at the adapter layer; fixing it means changing `GrowwAuth.build_session`, out of this PR's scope). Blast radius is bounded: the operator can re-click (the O(1) skip resumes only new work), and a *surfaced* timeout is already handled by `retry_call`. Tracked as a follow-up (add a session-level timeout so a hang becomes a retryable `VendorSdkError`). **RESOLVED as a tracked decision in DEC-PULL-TIMEOUT-DEFER-001 (#323): the watchdog patch was hostile-reviewed + REJECTED as unsafe (it breaks the single-flight SDK invariant on retry); the limitation is formally DEFERRED — the true session-level fix lands when `growwapi` is a CI integration dependency.**
    Verified PASS by the review: store + bucket thread-safety, single-flight atomicity, closure capture, all four frontend checks (XSS-escaped, poll-terminates, independent buttons, 400-before-launch), scope lock (engine untouched), and the O(1)/coverage-excluded honesty claims.

320. **DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001 — honest coverage page (in-progress ≠ error) + surface the swallowed pull-400 reason + true recent r/s** (operator runs 2026-05-30: "I can see so many missing which is not fair" + the `/universe` "Pull spot" button returned a blank `∅ no data returned` 400). Quick-wins PR (the operator-approved sequencing ahead of the two-phase rebuild, DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001). Three honesty fixes on the Observability priority rung:

    - **(A) "894 missing" was NOT 894 errors — it was an in-progress run.** The pull walks a 1,652-cell grid; a screenshot mid-run shows every not-yet-reached cell as `missing`. The `/coverage` headline led with that count next to `failed`, implying mass failure. `coverage_view.coverage_headline` now also emits `attempted` (= complete + failed + pending — cells the pull has TOUCHED) and `not_pulled` (= missing, an alias named so the UI never implies an error); the template leads with a **"pulled so far = attempted / total"** progress KPI, relabels `missing` → **"not pulled yet"**, `failed` → **"failed (real errors)"**, `pending` → **"pending (no F&O)"**, and shows a `pulling · N / total` live badge while `attempted < total`. The classification rule is unchanged — only the framing. `failed` remains the ONLY real-error count (`classify_cell`).

    - **(B) the swallowed 400 (the "how do I know it's an error?" bug).** `POST /api/v1/universe/pull` caught ONLY `ValueError` and returned a bodyless 400 with no log line — but the live path raises `VendorSdkError` (MRO: `VendorSdkError → BruteXError → Exception`, NOT a `ValueError`) and `RuntimeError` too, so the real reason vanished and the page showed a blank "no data returned". The route now logs `universe.pull.requested` / `universe.pull.ok` / `universe.pull.failed` (full `error_type` + message + traceback) to the operator's `.brutex-logs/brutex.log` JSONL, and returns `"{ExcType}: {message}"` as the 400 detail — a 400 is never a dead-end again.

    - **(C) true recent r/s.** The `universe.pull.rate` log emitted only a lifetime cumulative `achieved_rps` (the operator: "per second how many requests you are not even capturing"). It now ALSO emits `window_rps` — the rate over just the cells since the last readout — so the live throughput is visible, not just the average. (The low ~2.6 r/s itself — expiry discovery being sequential — is fixed by the two-phase rebuild, not here.)

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `coverage_view.py` stays 100% line+branch (13 tests, +1 new honesty assertion). `app.py` + `cli.py` + `coverage.html` are coverage-excluded glue (`[tool.coverage] omit`); the route/log/template changes are framing + observability, no logic change to the pull or the ledger rule. This PR does NOT change pull ordering or speed — that is DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 (the all-expiries-then-all-contracts rebuild + per-item watermark, next). **Decision ID:** DEC-PULL-ERROR-VISIBILITY-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 (#319) · DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001 · DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001.

319. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001 — parallel contract fan-out, start-at-8 r/s adaptive limiter, and never-give-up transient retry for the universe pull** (operator runs 2026-05-30, post-#317: the full 2020→now pull ran > 30 min and the operator — correctly — diagnosed three of *our own* defects, not Groww limits). Three coupled fixes on the priority law (Correctness > Reliability > Recoverability > Observability > Performance > Scalability). Layers cleanly on top of DEC-CONTRACTS-META-FIX-001 (#318): that fix made every contract *persist* (leg→underlying metadata); this one makes the pull *fast* + *resilient*.

    - **(A) Rate — start at 8 r/s, not 3.** `_run_live_universe_ingest` built `AdaptiveTokenBucket()` with its stale pre-pivot defaults (`initial_rps=3.0`, legacy cap 5.0) while the intended start-8/adaptive-[4..8] design (`adaptive_rate_limiter.py`, DEC-ADAPTIVE-RATE-LIMITER-001) sat unwired. Now `AdaptiveTokenBucket(initial_rps=8.0, downshift_rps=4.0)`: start at 8, step down to 4 on sustained throttling, recover to 8. **8 r/s is the safe sustained target (not a guess):** IF the backtesting endpoints meter as Non-Trading (500/min ⇒ ~8.3 r/s sustained — `docs/groww/api-reference/01-introduction.md`; the backtesting bucket itself is UNVERIFIED per CLAUDE.md §6), the PER-MINUTE cap — not the per-second 20 — binds, so sustaining >8 is futile. A sustained 8 r/s ≈ 480/min (≤485/min incl. the 5-token burst) stays under it; the bucket never upshifts above 8, and on sustained throttling steps down to 4 + retries, so if the real bucket is stricter the adaptive path self-corrects. Operator-approved per CLAUDE.md §2 rule 6.

    - **(B) Throughput — parallel fan-out, not sequential.** The bigger defect: `_pull_cell` issued one blocking `get_contracts` at a time, so throughput was ROUND-TRIP-LATENCY-bound at ~3 r/s regardless of the rate budget — raising the rate alone does nothing while sequential. The per-expiry contract pulls now fan out across a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`BRUTEX_UNIVERSE_PULL_WORKERS`, default 8) sharing the ONE token bucket (the global rate governor) + the thread-safe store (#317-A) — a few in-flight requests saturates the budget. Honest wall-clock is a RANGE: ~44 min at a sustained 8 r/s, up to ~88 min if throttled to 4 (≈21k calls = 1,652 expiry + ~19k contract; 10 min is physically impossible — needs ~35 r/s = 2,100/min, 4× over 500/min). #197's per-expiry `raw`/`skipped_*` observability is preserved through the fan-out.

    - **(C) Resilience + observability — never give up + measure the rate.** New tested `brutex.orchestrator.retry.retry_call` wraps every fetch: transient failures (rate-limit / timeout / generic — `RETRYABLE_OUTCOMES`) retry with the existing `backoff_delay` ladder up to `DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`; permanent failures (bad-request / auth / authz / not-found) surface at once (looping a deterministic 400 is a hang, not resilience); non-vendor exceptions are never caught. Auth errors still propagate to the cell-level re-mint+retry. A new `universe.pull.rate` log line (every 25 cells + final) emits the LIVE achieved r/s + ETA so the rate is measured, never assumed.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** `retry_call` is 100% line+branch covered (12 new cases in `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_retry.py`; 53 pass) + ruff/mypy-strict/pyright clean. The fan-out + start-8 wiring live in `cli.py` (coverage-excluded glue per `[tool.coverage] omit`); they are proven by the thread-safe-store stress test (#317-A) + the unchanged store suite, not line coverage. A 4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) found + fixed a mid-flight SDK re-mint race — every cell now DRAINS all its futures before the cell-level re-mint, so zero workers touch `contract_fetcher.sdk` during a rebind — and hardened the `BRUTEX_UNIVERSE_PULL_WORKERS` parse against malformed values; the partial-write-on-cell-failure it flagged is benign + self-healing via the idempotent resumable re-pull (coverage_ledger). Gradual one-by-one AIMD (the still-unwired `AdaptiveRateLimiter`) + a CLI/UI worker knob are tracked follow-ups. Whether Groww sustains 8 r/s on the backtesting bucket (UNVERIFIED) is operator-side + now visible in `universe.pull.rate`. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PARALLEL-001. **Builds on:** DEC-CONTRACTS-META-FIX-001 (#318) · DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-2020-001 (#317) · DEC-ADAPTIVE-RATE-LIMITER-001 · DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (#160) · CLAUDE.md §2 rule 6 · §6.

318. **DEC-CONTRACTS-META-FIX-001 — `contracts: 0` on every cell root-caused: the leg-metadata lookup queried the FULL contract symbol against the lean (underlyings-only) store** (operator live run 2026-05-30; every `universe.contracts.pulled` showed `contracts: 0` across all 236 underlyings × 7 years, including current 2026 expiries — see the pasted log). **Not** a rate-limit or vendor issue: the `get_contracts` calls succeeded, expiries pulled fine. Root cause: `cli._run_live_universe_ingest` built an inline `_meta_lookup(symbol)` that did `store.get(symbol)` with the **full contract-leg symbol** (e.g. `NSE-ADANIENT-30Jan20-1500-CE`). Per DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 the lean store persists ONLY the ~236 underlyings, never the legs — so the lookup always returned `None`, every contract was dropped as `skipped_no_metadata`, and the persisted count was 0 on every cell. **Fix:** cli.py now uses the already-tested `contracts.store_metadata_lookup(store)`, which reduces the leg to its underlying via `underlying_symbol_of` BEFORE the O(1) point lookup (the helper that exists precisely for the lean store — COMMON, no duplication, CLAUDE.md §11). **Observability (the why-was-it-hidden fix):** `universe.contracts.pulled` now logs `raw` (symbols Groww returned) + `skipped_no_metadata` + `skipped_malformed` alongside the persisted `contracts` count, so a 0 is never ambiguous again — `raw>0` ⇒ a drop, `raw=0` ⇒ an empty vendor response (DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001 extended). Covered by the existing `store_metadata_lookup` + `ContractFetcher.fetch` tests (`test_drives_a_real_fetch`, `test_inherits_from_underlying`, `underlying_symbol_of` suite); the cli wiring is coverage-excluded glue. **Decision ID:** DEC-CONTRACTS-META-FIX-001. **Builds on:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (#160) · DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-2020-001 (#317) · DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001.

317. **DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-2020-001 — automated full expiry+contract pull from Jan 2020, total pull-process logging, the /coverage threading crash, and /db paging** (operator runs 2026-05-30, post-#316 merge: the structured logs from #316 worked — the operator could finally copy them — which exposed the next layer of real defects). Five fixes, all on the priority law (Correctness > Reliability > Recoverability > Observability > Performance > Scalability):

    - **(A) DEC-STORE-THREADSAFE-001 — the `/coverage` 500 crash.** `GET /api/v1/coverage` 500'd with `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 26, got 1)` (`_row_to_instrument`): the dashboard shares ONE `InstrumentStore` (one DuckDB connection) across the uvicorn request threads AND the background universe-pull thread (DEC-AUTO-UNIVERSE-001 reuses the single writer). A DuckDB connection has ONE result cursor, so a request reading `instruments` mid-`refresh()` (upsert + prune) garbled the row. Fixed by a `_StoreMeta` metaclass that wraps EVERY public `InstrumentStore` method in a per-store `threading.RLock` (re-entrant; execute→fetch is now atomic), plus a `_LockedReadConn` returned by `.connection` so the whitebox `/db` reader holds the same lock across execute→fetch. Proven by `TestThreadSafety::test_concurrent_read_during_upsert_prune_never_corrupts` (1 writer churning upsert+prune across snapshots + 3 readers hammering `list_index_equity_instruments`/`has_placeholder_stock_economics`/`list_coverage`; 0 errors, lake stays clean). All 79 existing store tests still pass — the lock is transparent.

    - **(B) DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-2020-001 — automated, ALL years from 2020.** The on-run auto-pull (cli.py) and the `/coverage` "Re-pull gaps" (app.py) both pulled `years=[current_year]` only — so only 2026 expiries appeared and contracts stayed 0. Both now pull `range(2020, now+1)`: for every underlying (every admitted index + every F&O-eligible stock), every year 2020→now, every expiry → all contracts, fully automatic on run (Groww serves F&O from 2020, CLAUDE.md §6). Historical CANDLES stay manual + per-symbol by design (operator decree) — a from/to-date candle picker is the tracked follow-up.

    - **(C) DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001 (extended) — the WHOLE pull is now in the log file.** The pull loop logged only its final outcome, so the operator (rightly) saw no per-step trail. `_run_live_universe_ingest` now emits structured events for every step — `universe.master.refreshing/refreshed`, `universe.pull.start`, `universe.cell.start` (with `N/total` progress), `universe.contracts.pulled` (per expiry), `universe.cell.done`, `universe.cell.failed` (with the error), `universe.auth.reminted`, `universe.pull.done` — all landing in `.brutex-logs/brutex.log` (JSON) + the `/logs` viewer. Plus a stdout mirror so the Groww SDK's raw `Ready to Groww!` print (and any third-party stdout) is captured to the file too ("every nook and corner").

    - **(D) auth re-mint mid-pull.** The operator's pull failed partway with "Authentication failed. Your API token has either expired or is invalid." — a long ALL-underlyings × 2020→now pull outlives one short-lived Groww access token (resets daily 6 AM IST, CLAUDE.md §6). The pull now detects an auth error per cell, re-mints ONCE via `GrowwAuth.refresh()`, rebinds the expiry/contract fetchers, and retries the cell instead of failing every remaining one.

    - **(E) DEC-DB-PAGINATION-001 — see all rows + all 26 columns in `/db`.** The `/db` viewer only ever fetched page 1 (no `offset`); the backend already returned `total`/`offset`. Added Prev/Next paging (the grid already scrolls horizontally for the wide 26-column tables) so the operator can walk every row.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the live Groww pull (whether 2020 data actually returns, the contracts=0 question) is operator-side + network-gated — this PR makes the pull cover all years, log every step (so the operator can SEE exactly what each `get_contracts` returns), and survive token expiry; the live yes/no is then visible in the log. The full 2020→now pull is inherently long (hundreds of underlyings × 7 years × many expiries × contracts, rate-limited at the adapter) — not claimed O(1); it is the documented bulk ETL. `cli.py` + dashboard routes/templates are coverage-excluded glue; the real new logic (the store lock) is proven by a concurrency stress test + the unchanged 79-test store suite. **Decision ID:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-2020-001 (umbrella) with sub-IDs DEC-STORE-THREADSAFE-001 · DEC-DB-PAGINATION-001. **Builds on:** DEC-RUN-FIXPACK-001 (#316) · DEC-AUTO-UNIVERSE-001 (#314) · DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001 (#166) · CLAUDE.md §6 / §13.

316. **DEC-RUN-FIXPACK-001 — six real-run defects fixed + proven against the operator's REAL 152,444-row `instrument.csv`** (operator runs 2026-05-30: repeated `make run` still showed "0 stocks", `lot_size=1`/blank `freeze_quantity`, an empty `/logs` page, an opaque "Groww API Error 400: Bad Request", the `instruments` table growing 236 → 472 on a second-day reload, and no way to verify saved credentials inside the IDE). All six are root-caused, fixed, tested, and **verified end-to-end by loading the operator's actual uploaded CSV** (RELIANCE → lot=500/tick=0.05/freeze=15001, NIFTY → lot=65/freeze=1801, 25 indices · 211 stocks, 236 lean rows, 2.8 s parse). Priority law honoured (Correctness > Reliability > Recoverability > Observability > Performance > Scalability).

    - **(A) DEC-STALE-ECONOMICS-HEAL-001 — `lot_size`/`tick_size`/`freeze_quantity` stuck at the master placeholders.** The economics back-fill (DEC-UNDERLYING-ECONOMICS-001 / #164) was correct, but the auto-heal gate (`should_reload_instrument_master`, #315) only reloaded on empty / index-less / non-lean lakes — NOT on a lake loaded *before* the back-fill landed. So a lake with `lot_size=1` placeholders served them forever. New cheap probe `InstrumentStore.has_placeholder_stock_economics()` (indexed `EXISTS` over the latest snapshot: any NSE `EQ` with `lot_size <= 1` — every real F&O stock has lot > 1) feeds a new `stale_economics` arm of `should_reload_instrument_master`. A reload now re-enriches every stock; the probe then reads clean, so the heal fires at most once (idempotent).

    - **(B) DEC-INSTRUMENT-LEAN-SNAPSHOT-001 — `instruments` table grew 236 → 472 across days (read as a broken dedup guarantee).** Each keyless load stamps a new UTC `snapshot_date`, and `upsert_many(replace_snapshot=True)` only wipes the *same* day — so a reload on a later day ADDED a second full ~236-row copy (latest-per-symbol reads stayed correct, but the raw `/db` view doubled). New `InstrumentStore.prune_to_latest_snapshot()` (collapse to the newest `snapshot_date`) runs after every keyless refresh, keeping the lake lean + unique at ~241 rows. Idempotent + safe on empty/single-snapshot lakes.

    - **(C) DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001 — the `/logs` page + `.brutex-logs/brutex.log` were always empty.** uvicorn's loggers ship with `propagate=False` + their own stderr handlers, so HTTP/startup logs never reached our rotating file handler; and the `cmd_dashboard` milestones were `print()`s, not structured logs. Fix: `uvicorn.run(..., log_config=None)` so uvicorn's access/error loggers PROPAGATE into our root handlers, `configure_logging(json_renderer=False)` (pretty console, JSON file), and the run-path milestones + failures now emit via `structlog` (so they land in the file + the live viewer). Validated by running a real uvicorn server: brutex events + access logs + the autopull failure all captured as JSON.

    - **(D) DEC-CREDS-NORMALISE-001 — the opaque Groww 400 + the "no expiry?" confusion.** The 400 originates in `GrowwAPI.get_access_token` (HARD-VERIFIED in the wheel: `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` + `{"key_type":"totp","totp":<code>}` → HTTP 400 string "Groww API Error 400: …"). A pasted API key with a trailing newline → malformed Bearer header → 400; a base32 TOTP secret pasted in spaced groups (Groww shows `MPB2 AAWM …`) → undecodable by `pyotp` → wrong code → 400. New `normalise_api_key` (strip) + `normalise_totp_secret` (remove ALL whitespace + upper-case canonical base32) applied on BOTH save + resolve. Saving credentials now also `clear_cached_token()`s any access token minted from the OLD creds (Groww **resets API keys daily at 6 AM IST** — the TOTP *secret* has no expiry, but the API-key JWT/access token does, so a stale cache would keep failing). The autopull failure path now logs an ACTIONABLE hint (regenerate the TOTP Token + re-save) instead of an opaque "Bad Request".

    - **(E) DEC-CREDS-PREVIEW-001 — "is it loading what I pasted, or empty?" + "I can't see credentials inside IntelliJ".** The credentials file lives at `~/.brutex/credentials.json` (outside the repo, by security design — never committed), so it is invisible in the project tree. New `credentials_preview()` returns a MASKED, non-secret `head…tail` + length of each stored field; the `/api/v1/credentials/status` endpoint + Credentials page now show it (e.g. `key eyJraW…WXYZ (912 chars) · totp MP…A2 (32 chars)`) so the operator can VERIFY the paste landed without the UI ever echoing a usable secret.

    - **(F) DEC-RUN-FIXPACK-001 — "0 stocks" startup tally.** `cmd_dashboard` summarised via `universe_summary(load_snapshot(...))` with NO `fno_eligible` set; on a lean lake (no legs) every equity fell through unclassified → "25 indices · 0 stocks" (the DATA was fine — `/universe` already showed 211). Now uses the lean-correct `universe_summary(list_index_equity_instruments(), fno_eligible=fno_eligible_underlyings())` at both the count-message and auto-pull-gate call sites — the same path the keyless loader already used.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the 10 s "Load instruments" wait is the **22 MB CSV network download**, not the parse (measured 2.8 s for 152k rows) — it is an O(n) one-per-day ETL, not an O(1) op, and is not claimed to be. The live Groww auth (the 400's ultimate yes/no) is operator-side: if it still 400s after a freshly-generated TOTP Token is re-saved, Groww is rejecting the key itself. `cli.py` + the dashboard template/routes stay coverage-excluded glue; the real logic (`has_placeholder_stock_economics`, `prune_to_latest_snapshot`, `should_reload_instrument_master` stale-arm, `normalise_*`, `credentials_preview`, `clear_cached_token`) is 100% line+branch tested (full unit+integration suite green: 2482 passed / 18 skipped; ruff clean). **Decision ID:** DEC-RUN-FIXPACK-001 (umbrella) with sub-IDs DEC-STALE-ECONOMICS-HEAL-001 · DEC-INSTRUMENT-LEAN-SNAPSHOT-001 · DEC-RUN-LOG-CAPTURE-001 · DEC-CREDS-NORMALISE-001 · DEC-CREDS-PREVIEW-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNDERLYING-ECONOMICS-001 (#164) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-UNIVERSE-FAST-001 (#160) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-BULK-UPSERT-001 (#315) · DEC-COVERAGE-LEDGER-001 (#166) · DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 (#312) · CLAUDE.md §6 (Groww facts) · §13 (Merge-Readiness Charter).

315. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-BULK-UPSERT-001 — ultra-fast instrument-master load + auto-heal on stale lake** (operator finding 2026-05-29: `make run` still showed "0 INDEX · 211 stocks" AFTER the #313 index-parse fix merged, and loading/clicking "Load instruments" was painfully slow — "why so much struggle, our aim is O(1) ultra-fast"). **Two root causes, both fixed:** **(A) Stale lake** — the #187/#313 on-run auto-load only fired when the lake was *wholly empty* (`summary["total"] == 0`); an operator whose lake was populated by a PRE-#313 build (which quarantined all 30 index rows) had 211 stocks + 0 indices, so the guard said "present" and never re-loaded → the operator saw stale, index-less data and (wrongly) read it as the fix failing. Fix: a new pure gate `brutex/dashboard/auto_pull.py::should_reload_instrument_master(index_count, stock_count)` reloads when the lake is empty OR **missing indices** (`index_count == 0`) — the exact fingerprint of a pre-fix lake; reload is idempotent (the upsert dedups on `vendor_symbol`, DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001 / #313). 100% line+branch, all 4 states tested. **(B) Slow load (the O(1) claim audited honestly per Golden Rule #10)** — `upsert_many` did one `DELETE` + one `INSERT` **per row** (~2·N round-trips; ~10+ min for the ~150k-row master). Per-key dedup IS O(1) (the `(vendor_symbol, snapshot_date)` PK), but the BULK load was O(N) with a ruinous constant — the prior "O(1) load" framing was over-claimed and is corrected here. **Measured, not assumed:** DuckDB `executemany` is still a per-row loop internally (~22 s for 100k — no help); a set-based `DELETE … WHERE vendor_symbol IN (?, ?, … ×100k)` is **O(N²)** (the IN-list DELETE alone measured ~10 s). The real fix is DuckDB's vectorised columnar path: build the incoming rows as ONE registered Arrow table and drive both the replace (`EXISTS` semi-join, not an IN-list) and the insert (`INSERT … SELECT`) off it — **measured ~1.9 s fresh for 100k rows (~54k rows/s, ~300× the per-row loop)**, dedup + idempotent `rows_replaced` + single transaction all preserved (27 integration store tests pass unchanged; `tests/bench/test_instrument_bulk_upsert.py` pins a 30 s ceiling). **Architecture note (operator's Rust concern):** this slowness was a Python *glue* bug (a bad SQL shape), NOT a Python-vs-Rust or DuckDB limit — the same DuckDB does 257k rows/s on a clean bulk insert. The brute-force hot path (billions of combos) already runs on the Rust `fno_math` (PyO3) kernel + LMDB + Bloom with the O(1) NFR CI gate green (CLAUDE.md §4 — Python orchestration, Rust hot kernels); it never touches `upsert_many`, so this fix does not bear on the engine's latency budget. **Decision ID:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-BULK-UPSERT-001. **Builds on:** DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001 (#313, the parse fix this makes visible + fast) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-LOAD-001 (#311, the keyless loader) · DEC-AUTO-UNIVERSE-001 (#314, the sibling auto-pull in the same `cmd_dashboard` block) · CLAUDE.md §4 (Python/Rust split) · §5 O(1) discipline.

314. **DEC-AUTO-UNIVERSE-001 — on-run auto-pull of expiries + contracts, credentials-gated and non-blocking** (operator goal 2026-05-29: per CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED, when the app starts and Groww credentials are present, the full universe of expiries + contracts should pull automatically with zero clicks — the keyless instrument master already auto-loads on run per DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001 / #313, but expiries and contracts need Groww auth (CLAUDE.md §6 — `get_expiries` / `get_contracts` go through the authenticated SDK), so they could not ride the keyless path). **What landed:** `cmd_dashboard` (cli.py, coverage-excluded) gained a SECOND best-effort block AFTER the #187 keyless instrument auto-load: when `credentials_present()` (CLAUDE.md §6 — env vars OR the 0600 saved file via DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 / #312) AND the instrument master is non-empty, it launches `_run_live_universe_ingest` on a **background daemon thread** so a long live pull (≈250 underlyings × N years — CLAUDE.md §3 DEC-P0-063) never blocks the dashboard from serving, and a network/rate-limit failure (Groww Data APIs 5 r/s + 100k/day, CLAUDE.md §6) is caught so it never crashes the server. **Candles stay a manual pull** (no scope expansion — CLAUDE.md §3). The pure GO/NO-GO decision is extracted to `brutex/dashboard/auto_pull.py::should_auto_pull_universe(credentials_present, instrument_total)` (100% line+branch, all 4 combinations tested) so the gate logic is real tested code while only the live-SDK/thread glue stays `# pragma: no cover`. **Concurrency decision (verified, not assumed):** the dashboard holds an open read-write `InstrumentStore` (DuckDB single file). A throwaway in-process probe showed `InstrumentStore.open` (which does `duckdb.connect(str(path))`, default read-write) DOES allow a second handle to the same file in-process without locking — but two independent read-write handles do not coordinate write transactions cleanly, so option (b) was chosen: `_run_live_universe_ingest` gained an optional `store: Any = None` param — when injected (dashboard path) it REUSES the dashboard's single open store and does NOT close it; when `None` (the unchanged `fetch --universe` path) it opens/closes its own. One writer, no ambiguity. Backward-compatible.

313. **DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001 — index (IDX) rows now parse: the dashboard's "0 INDEX" was the parser quarantining all 30 index rows of the real Groww master** (operator finding 2026-05-29: `/universe` shows "0 INDEX" even after loading the master, while 211 stocks load fine). CONFIRMED against the operator's REAL `instrument.csv`: the master carries **30 `IDX` rows** (NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, SENSEX, INDIAVIX, FINNIFTY, BANKEX, MIDCPNIFTY/NIFTYMIDSELECT + ~23 sectoral/broad indices) and EVERY one of them failed `_row_to_instrument` on **three fields**, any one of which was fatal in the `_ROW_ERRORS` quarantine try/except: (1) `exchange_token` is the SYMBOL string for NSE indices (`"NIFTYMETAL"`, `"NIFTY"`; 24 of 30 non-numeric — BSE indices use small ints `1`/`14`) → `int(float("NIFTYMETAL"))` ValueError; (2) `lot_size` BLANK for all 30 → `int(float(""))` ValueError; (3) `tick_size` BLANK for all 30 → `normalise_tick_size("")` TickSizeFormatError. Indices are reference instruments — never directly tradable (`brutex/universe.py`) — so their economics are legitimately absent.

    **What landed:**
    - **`brutex/adapters/groww/instruments.py` `_row_to_instrument`** — index-tolerant for IDX only: new `_req_int_or_zero` helper maps a non-numeric/blank `exchange_token` → `0` (metadata, NOT the dedup key — `vendor_symbol` is primary; tolerant for ALL rows, only index rows hit the non-numeric branch in practice); `lot_size` → `0` and `tick_size` → `Decimal("0")` when blank-on-index; EQ/FUT/CE/PE stay STRICT (a blank lot/tick or bad token on a tradable row still quarantines).
    - **`brutex/models.py`** — added the `is_index` property (IDX only); `Instrument.__post_init__` lot/tick guards relaxed for indices (`< 0` rejected, `== 0` allowed) while tradable types keep `<= 0` rejection.
    - **`brutex/execution/types.py` `InstrumentMeta.__post_init__`** — the SAME guard surfaced again in the execution-layer projection (`InstrumentStore.load_snapshot` builds an `InstrumentMeta` for every instrument, indices included): relaxed to allow `lot_size == 0` for IDX only (the simulator never sizes an order against an index). This was the path actually hit by the dashboard's real-store load — the originally-broken surface.
    - **`brutex/cli.py` `cmd_dashboard`** — `brutex run` now AUTO-LOADS the keyless public instrument master on startup when the lake is empty (best-effort; a network failure never blocks serving), so `/universe` is never empty on a fresh lake with zero clicks (CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED). The existing Load-instruments button still works.

    **Tests:** real-30-row regression fixture `tests/fixtures/groww_idx_rows_real.csv` (header + all 30 real IDX rows) drives `test_real_index_rows_all_parse` (asserts parsed==30, quarantined==0); `_req_int_or_zero` table test; both-branch tests proving EQ/option strictness is preserved; dashboard-loader real-style IDX row; models `is_index` True/False; `InstrumentMeta` IDX zero-lot allowed + negative-lot rejected.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REAL — 100% line+branch on `instruments.py` / `instrument_loader.py` / `execution/types.py` / `models.py`; mypy --strict + ruff + bandit clean; full `tests/unit` green (2243 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated skip). 🟡 The auto-load + live HTTP fetch path is `# pragma: no cover` (network-blocked CI; exercised on the operator's Mac). 📋 INDIA VIX presence in the live master remains Phase 0b HARD-GATE unverified (CLAUDE.md §6); the fixture is the operator's pasted real export, not a live probe.

    **Decision ID:** DEC-INDEX-PARSE-FIX-001. **Builds on:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-LOAD-001 (entry #311, keyless load) · DEC-VENDOR-PIVOT-001 (Groww facts) · CLAUDE.md §6 (index symbol formats).

312. **DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 — secure local credentials store: operator sets the Groww API key + TOTP secret ONCE; they auto-load every session** (operator goal 2026-05-29: stop `export BRUTEX_GROWW_*` per shell — per CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED a one-time set must persist with zero clicks per day). A MECHANISM-only change: a hardened, secrets-never-logged file store plus the three set/load surfaces (`brutex auth set`, the dashboard Credentials page, and the existing `BRUTEX_GROWW_*` env vars), wired so the live auth + the dashboard's dry-run gate both honour a saved file.

    **What landed:**
    - **New module `brutex/config/credentials.py`** — `GrowwCredentials` (frozen slots dataclass), `CredentialsError`, `credentials_path` (`BRUTEX_CREDENTIALS_FILE` override → `~/.brutex/credentials.json` default), `save_groww_credentials` (atomic 0600 write, 0700 parent), `load_groww_credentials` (missing → `None`; insecure-perms / corrupt / wrong-shape / blank → `CredentialsError`), `resolve_groww_credentials` (PER-FIELD env-first, file-fallback), `credentials_present` (boolean; insecure-file → `False`, never raises), `clear_groww_credentials`. stdlib-only. **100% line + branch** (`coverage report` → `106 stmts / 0 miss / 34 branch / 0 BrPart / 100.00%`), zero `# pragma: no cover`. mypy --strict clean, ruff/bandit/interrogate clean.
    - **Wired `brutex/adapters/groww/auth.py::GrowwAuth.from_env`** (`# pragma: no cover` live wiring) to source `api_key` / `totp_secret` from `resolve_groww_credentials()` instead of raw `os.environ[...]` — env still wins per field, file fills the rest. `BRUTEX_GROWW_TOKEN_PATH` handling unchanged.
    - **Wired `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py::groww_creds_present`** to delegate to `credentials_present(env)` so a saved FILE (not only env vars) flips the dashboard pull route off dry-run. Signature unchanged; existing creds-present tests made HERMETIC (each `False` case points `BRUTEX_CREDENTIALS_FILE` at a nonexistent path so a developer's real `~/.brutex/credentials.json` can't contaminate CI).
    - **CLI `brutex auth set|status|clear`** (coverage-excluded glue) — `set` prompts via `getpass.getpass()` (NO echo, NEVER argv flags → no shell-history / `ps` leak), saves, and prints only `credentials saved to <path> (mode 0600)`; `status` prints `set`/`not set` + path; `clear` removes the file. Mirrors the `audit` subparser-with-subcommands pattern.
    - **Dashboard routes** (coverage-excluded) — `POST /api/v1/credentials` (Pydantic `CredentialsIn` BODY model, never Query; `CredentialsError` → HTTP 400 with NO value in the message; body NOT logged; returns `{"present": true}`), `GET /api/v1/credentials/status` (`{"present": bool}` only), `GET /credentials` (new `templates/credentials.html`, v28-hybrid dark page with two `type=password` inputs, an `esc()`-escaped status/message line, and the "stored locally / never committed / rotate" note). A "Credentials" nav link added to `universe.html`.
    - **`.gitignore`** safety net — `credentials.json`, `*.credentials.json`, `.brutex/` (the real default lives OUTSIDE the repo at `~/.brutex`, but the repo is guarded too).

    **Security invariants (the only thing this module is for):** (1) no secret VALUE is ever logged / printed / echoed — error messages name WHICH field, never its value; (2) file written mode 0600, parent 0700, ATOMICALLY (temp file in the same dir → chmod 0600 → `os.replace`, no world-readable window, temp cleaned on failure); (3) on READ a file with any group/world bits (`mode & 0o077`) is REFUSED → `chmod 600` (mirrors `auth._INSECURE_MODE_BITS`); (4) secrets NEVER enter `DashboardState` / `~/.brutex/runtime.json` — status surfaces return booleans only; (5) credentials accepted in request BODY only, never query params.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the real deliverable is the tested mechanism module + its three wirings. The CLI handlers, the FastAPI routes, the HTML template, and `from_env` are coverage-excluded glue (interactive / live-network / browser), consistent with the existing `# pragma: no cover` discipline for those surfaces. No claim is made that this audits the secret at rest beyond filesystem 0600 perms; full-disk encryption / OS keychain integration is out of scope (a possible future decision).

    **Decision ID:** DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001. **Builds on:** DEC-VENDOR-PIVOT-001 (CLAUDE.md §6 TOTP-ACCEPTED auth) · DEC-INSTRUMENT-LOAD-001 (#311).

311. **DEC-INSTRUMENT-LOAD-001 — keyless "Load instruments" capability: populate the `/universe` list from the public instrument master with NO Groww keys** (operator finding 2026-05-29: `/universe` shows "0 INDEX / 0 STOCKS / no matches" because nobody has loaded the instrument master, and the operator should be able to populate the index/stock LIST without keys — the master is a PUBLIC CSV; only expiries/contracts/candles need auth). Adds a thin, fully-testable seam plus a button + a CLI flag so the list can be filled keylessly.

    **What landed:**
    - **New module `brutex/dashboard/instrument_loader.py`** — `load_instrument_master(store, *, http_get=None, run_id_factory=None) -> dict`. Constructs an `InstrumentMasterFetcher` (real keyless public-CSV path via `InstrumentMasterFetcher.from_env(store)` when `http_get` is `None` — `# pragma: no cover`, live network; injected fake `http_get` for offline tests), calls `.refresh()`, reads back `store.load_snapshot(in_scope_only=False)`, and returns `{"parsed","filtered","quarantined","index_count","stock_count","total"}` by REUSING `universe_query.universe_summary` (COMMON — no re-derivation of the index/stock split). **NO `GrowwAuth` / creds referenced anywhere on this path.** 100% line+branch on the non-pragma path (`coverage report` shows `13 stmts / 0 miss / 0 branch / 100.00%`).
    - **Route (thin, coverage-excluded `app.py`)** — `POST /api/v1/universe/load-instruments` via `_require_store()` → `load_instrument_master(store)` → returns the dict. Maps `InstrumentFormatError` (CSV-format / parse failure) / `OSError` (network) → **HTTP 502** with a short message so the UI can show "couldn't reach Groww asset host". A non-UTF-8 / truncated body is a parse failure, so `from_env`'s SSRF-guarded fetch re-raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (a `ValueError`, NOT an `OSError`) as `InstrumentFormatError` at the decode boundary — closing the one path the keyless-load hostile review flagged as an uncaught 500. A store-integrity `CatalogError` (degenerate already-broken store) is out of scope of the "network/parse → 502" contract. Verified with a FastAPI `TestClient`: empty store + network-blocked CI → 502 (not 500); no store → 503.
    - **`/universe` UI (`templates/universe.html`)** — a "⟳ Load instruments" button in BOTH the pullbar AND the empty banner. On click → POST the endpoint, inline "loading…" state, then on success re-runs `loadSummary()` + `loadInstruments()` so the ~200 instruments appear; on error shows the `esc()`-escaped message. Matches the v28-hybrid palette.
    - **CLI (`cli.py`, coverage-excluded)** — `brutex fetch --instruments` runs ONLY the keyless master load (no auth), prints the index/stock counts, and exits. Existing `--universe` (expiries/contracts WITH keys) is unchanged.
    - **Tests `tests/unit/test_dashboard_instrument_loader.py`** — inject a fake `http_get` (CSV with 1 NSE IDX index + 1 F&O-eligible stock + its CE derivative + 1 MCX out-of-scope row) against a REAL temp `InstrumentStore`; assert parsed=3 / filtered=1 / index_count=1 / stock_count=1; malformed-header CSV raises `InstrumentFormatError`; empty CSV → all-zero counts; default `run_id_factory` path covered. ruff + ruff format + mypy --strict + pyright all GREEN; interrogate 100%.

    **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the instrument master is **keyless/public** (`growwapi-assets.groww.in/instruments/instrument.csv`, CLAUDE.md §6) — populating the LIST needs no Groww keys. Expiries / contracts / candles **still need keys** (separate `fetch --universe` / pull paths, unchanged). The live HTTP fetch (`InstrumentMasterFetcher.from_env`) is `# pragma: no cover` (network-blocked in CI; reachable on the operator's Mac) — so the keyless populate is **proven offline with a fake `http_get`** but the real fill needs the operator's online Mac. The `app.py` route + the template are coverage-excluded (same rationale as every FastAPI route + HTML asset in this repo). **Decision ID:** DEC-INSTRUMENT-LOAD-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-DASHBOARD-001 (#306, the `/universe` page + `universe_summary` classifier + v28-hybrid palette + `esc()` this reuses) · DEC-FETCH-UNIVERSE-001 (#299, the `--universe` ingest this sits beside) · the public instrument-master CSV (CLAUDE.md §6).

310. **DEC-DASHBOARD-AUTOOPEN-001 — `make run` auto-opens `/universe` + an empty-state banner explains why it's empty** (operator frustration 2026-05-29: ran `make run` three times, kept seeing "0 INDEX / 0 STOCKS", thought it was broken; "universe webpage didn't open automatically … why even logs directory and its architecture is not visible"). Two UX fixes — the app now explains itself instead of looking broken: **(A)** `cli.cmd_run` opens the browser to **`/universe`** (the operator's working surface) instead of `/`. **(B)** `templates/universe.html` shows a prominent empty-state banner when `index_count + stock_count == 0`: it states the dashboard works but the lake is empty (expected, not a bug), the exact unblock steps (allow Groww hosts + set `BRUTEX_GROWW_API_KEY`/`BRUTEX_GROWW_TOTP_SECRET`, then `brutex fetch --universe` or click→Pull), the on-disk paths (lake `~/.brutex/lake` · DB `instruments.duckdb` · logs `~/.brutex/logs/brutex.log`), and quick links to `/` · `/logs` · `/db`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is pure UX — it does NOT make data appear; the universe stays empty until the operator unblocks Groww + ingests (the one remaining wall, on the operator side per DEC-FETCH-UNIVERSE-001 §0). `cli.py` + the template are coverage-excluded glue (no new logic module). **Decision ID:** DEC-DASHBOARD-AUTOOPEN-001. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-DASHBOARD-001 (#306) · DEC-UNIVERSE-STORE-FIX-001 (#307) · DEC-ONECLICK-RUN-001.

309. **DEC-DB-VIEWER-001 — read-only DuckDB browser page (`/db`) + `/api/v1/db/tables` + `/api/v1/db/table/{name}` endpoints** (operator need 2026-05-29, pressed hard: "where is the DB, how can I see it, db design — every nook and corner"; today seeing the instrument-master store requires the `duckdb` CLI). Turns the 5-table DuckDB instrument store into a browsable dashboard page so the operator can inspect tables + row counts + sample rows in the browser.

    **Three-piece build:**
