430. **DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 — Stage-4 Deflated Sharpe Ratio + Probability of Backtest Overfitting implemented for real (the two previously-NULL statistical-validity metrics)** (2026-06-03, implements the two Stage-4 metrics the spec marks "Stage 4 only, NULL before then" at `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` lines 582-583 + pipeline filters #2/#5 at lines 382/405). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID is `DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001` (authoritative); the task brief drafted "#417" (already `DEC-RUST-RAYON-SUPERMASK-001`), and #424-#427 were claimed by PRs #326-#329 (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 / DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001 / DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 / DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001) which merged to `main` during this PR's review, so this lands at the next free integer **#430** — the ID, not the number, is authoritative (same convention as #423/#425/#426/#427). **What shipped (two NEW pure-function modules + a wiring seam):** (1) `brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py` — `probabilistic_sharpe_ratio(observed, benchmark, n, skew, kurtosis)` (PSR; Bailey & López de Prado 2012, *Journal of Risk* 15(2) — `PSR = Z[(SR̂−SR*)√(n−1) / √(1 − γ3·SR̂ + (γ4−1)/4·SR̂²)]`, the radicand being the Mertens 2002 / Lo 2002 SR-estimator variance), `expected_max_sharpe_ratio(n_trials, trial_sharpe_variance)` (`SR_0`, the Gumbel/EVT expected-max of N zero-edge trials), and `deflated_sharpe_ratio(...) -> DeflatedSharpeResult` (`DSR = PSR(SR_0)`; Bailey & López de Prado 2014, *Journal of Portfolio Management* 40(5), 94-107). (2) `brutex/metrics/pbo.py` — `pbo_probability(performance, *, n_splits=16, evaluator=sharpe_from_moments) -> PBOResult` via **CSCV** (Combinatorially-Symmetric Cross-Validation; Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu 2017, *Journal of Computational Finance* 20(4), 39-69): partition the timeline into `S` equal sub-matrices, enumerate all `C(S, S/2)` symmetric IS/OOS splits, and report `PBO = P(λ ≤ 0)` where `λ = logit(relative OOS rank of the IS-best strategy)` (rank normalised `rank/(N+1)` with average-rank ties — the de-facto LdP/mlfinlab reference convention, documented as such vs the 2017 paper's bare `rank/N`). (3) `brutex/metrics/compute.py` — `with_stage4_statistics(metrics, *, n_trials, trial_sharpe_variance, pbo_performance=None, pbo_n_splits=16)` fills the two new `ResultMetrics` fields `deflated_sharpe_ratio` / `pbo_probability` (default `None`); `compute_metrics` leaves them NULL because the per-result pass has no cross-trial inputs. The excess kurtosis stored by `_excess_kurtosis` is converted back to the **non-excess** kurtosis the PSR expects via `+ GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` (3.0). The other four Stage-4 fields (`cpcv_pass_rate`, `wfo_pass_rate`, `lockbox_sharpe`, `lockbox_mdd_pct`, lines 584-587) stay DEFERRED — only DSR + PBO are in scope here. **Pure stdlib, no new dependency (deliberate):** `brutex.metrics.types` is documented dependency-light (no `polars`/`pyarrow`/`numpy` at import), so both modules use only `math` + `statistics.NormalDist` (exact double-precision CDF / inverse-CDF) — NOT numpy, which is a *dev-only* extra; coupling a core package to it would break the design intent. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** both are closed-form / exhaustive — DSR has no bootstrap and CSCV enumerates every split, so there is no RNG and no seed to fix; same inputs → bit-identical outputs. **Full precision (DEC-MONEY-2DP-001, money-only):** every output is a probability or a Sharpe ratio and is NEVER rounded. **O(1) honesty (Golden Rule #10):** DSR is O(1) scalar math; CSCV is inherently `O(C(S,S/2)·S·N)` (C(S,S/2) splits × O(S·N) per split, plus a one-time O(T·N) block pre-accumulation) — a Stage-4 batch reduction run **once per leaderboard**, NOT a per-bar/per-mask hot path, so Rule #5's O(1) hot-path gate does not apply (a future numpy/Rust vectorisation is a roadmap option, not needed at `S=16`). The OOS half is summed **directly** from the pre-accumulated per-block moments, NOT recovered as `total − IS` — that subtraction of two nearly-equal positives suffers catastrophic cancellation near zero variance and made the PBO sensitive to a benign rescaling (caught by the scale-invariance property test; fixed). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12 — unit + property + golden):** `tests/unit/test_deflated_sharpe.py` + `tests/unit/test_pbo.py` + `tests/unit/test_metrics_stage4_wiring.py` (known-answer fixtures — PSR `z=2 → Φ(2)=0.97724986…`, PBO dominant-strategy `=0` / anti-generalising `=1`, every validation raise, every NULL-guard branch); `tests/property/test_deflated_sharpe_properties.py` (DSR ∈ [0,1]; DSR ≤ undeflated PSR(0); DSR ↓ as `n_trials` ↑; `SR_0` ≥ 0 and ↑ as `n_trials` ↑) + `tests/property/test_pbo_properties.py` (PBO ∈ [0,1]; an **independent naive-CSCV oracle** that recomputes each chunk Sharpe from concatenated rows — exact-arithmetic integer inputs so block-aggregation == direct-concatenation bit-for-bit; power-of-two-scale invariance); `tests/golden/test_deflated_sharpe_golden.py` + `tests/golden/test_pbo_golden.py` (locked numeric constants). **Honest finding (no illusion, Golden Rule #1):** the property suite surfaced that the PSR is NOT globally monotone in the observed Sharpe when skew ≠ 0 — `d(PSR)/d(SR) ∝ (1 − skew·SR/2)` flips sign once `skew·SR > 2`, because a larger Sharpe at the same skew implies a larger estimator variance. This is a real property of the estimator (the *code* is faithful to the formula); the monotonicity invariant is therefore asserted only for the symmetric `skew = 0` case, documented in the test. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9):** hot-path / security (PASS, 0) / correctness (every golden fixture independently reproduced bit-for-bit) / cite-path (all citations + spec lines + decision ID verified) — caught + fixed the `total−IS` cancellation, a complexity-headline understatement (now `O(C(S,S/2)·S·N)`), and the `rank/(N+1)` cite precision; a follow-up CodeQL gate flagged the PEP 695 `type MomentEvaluator` alias as "exported by `__all__` but undefined" → dropped from `__all__` (still explicitly importable), root cause removed (no suppression). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** per-module **100% line + 100% branch** — `deflated_sharpe.py` (41/10), `pbo.py` (100/36), `compute.py` (234/44), 0 miss / 0 partial; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` (161 source files) + `pyright` both **0 errors**; `bandit` clean; `interrogate` 100% docstring; the 111 metrics tests pass and the full `tests/unit tests/property tests/golden` run is **3146 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed**. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ REAL — DSR + PBO are correct, deterministic, cited-to-source, fully covered, and wired into the result row. 🟡 the DSR's `trial_sharpe_variance` (cross-trial Sharpe dispersion `V`) is a required caller input (the paper needs it for `SR_0`); the Stage-4 driver that supplies the real per-leaderboard `V` + `n_trials` + the CSCV matrix is FUTURE (the filter-cascade work). 📋 the remaining four Stage-4 metrics (CPCV / WFO / lockbox×2) and the composite ranking score / hard rejection gates remain out of scope. **Builds on:** `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` lines 382/405/582-587 · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the per-result metrics + the excess-kurtosis convention) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (statistical metrics never money-rounded) · CLAUDE.md §4 (no pandas/no look-ahead) / §10 (honest envelope) / §12 (7 test types).

431. **DEC-STAT-SPA-001 — `brutex/metrics/spa.py`: Hansen SPA + White Reality Check + Romano-Wolf step-down (Stage-4 data-snooping filters #4 + #6)** (2026-06-03, implements the two multiple-testing filters the spec locked under DEC-EXTREME-001 — `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 4 — Statistical filters" filter #4 "Reality Check / SPA" (lines 389-404) + filter #6 "Romano-Wolf step-down" (line 406). CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review ran on the diff — correctness/stats · perf/O(1)/memory · security/robustness · cite/path). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** lands at the next free integer **#431** — #424-#430 were claimed by sibling PRs that merged to `main` during this PR's long review (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 #424, DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001 #425, DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 #426, DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 #427, DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 #428, DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 #429, DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 #430); the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative. **Sibling Stage-4 modules (no overlap, shared `brutex/metrics/__init__.py`):** `cpcv.py`/`wfo.py` (#428) = cross-validation + walk-forward split/pass-rate engines; `deflated_sharpe.py`/`pbo.py` (#430) = DSR + PBO-via-CSCV; THIS PR = the orthogonal *data-snooping / multiple-testing* engine. All are pure offline Stage-4 primitives the future cascade will consume. **What shipped:** three pure NumPy functions over an `(n_obs, n_strategies)` matrix of strategy **excess returns vs a benchmark** → p-values / a rejection set: `reality_check` (White 2000), `hansen_spa` (Hansen 2005 — studentized, three null-recentring variants `lower ≤ consistent ≤ upper`, the *consistent* one recommended), `romano_wolf` (Romano-Wolf 2005 step-down + the 2016 adjusted-p recursion → FWER-controlled rejection set, returns adjusted + naive per-strategy p-values, "USE THIS, NOT Bonferroni" per spec line 407). Plus `BootstrapConfig` (frozen, **seed is the first mandatory field** so no test runs without a pinned RNG — Golden Rule #4), `BootstrapMethod` (STATIONARY = Politis-Romano 1994, the spec default; CIRCULAR = Politis-Romano 1992), `expected_block_length` (the spec's `⌊1.75·n^(1/3)⌋`, line 396), and the three result dataclasses. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** one shared deterministic block bootstrap (`numpy.random.default_rng(seed)`), rows resampled **jointly across strategies** (one index vector per replication → cross-sectional dependence preserved, which White/Hansen/RW require); same input + same seed ⇒ bit-identical p-values (golden + property + unit determinism tests assert it). **No invented critical values (Golden Rule #1):** every statistic/recentring/threshold traces to the cited papers (White Econometrica 2000 68(5); Hansen JBES 2005 23(4); Romano-Wolf Econometrica 2005 73(4) + Stat&ProbLett 2016 113; Politis-Romano JASA 1994 89(428)); `arch` (Sheppard) used only as a cross-check oracle, not copied. **Studentization** uses the self-consistent bootstrap variance `ω_k² = n·Var*[mean d*_k]`. **Edge cases handled (no NaN/inf — spec line 746):** non-2D / `n<2` / zero-strategy / non-finite input rejected; studentized tests reject constant (zero-variance) columns and a degenerate bootstrap whose variance collapses (clear `ValueError`, never `inf`/`NaN`); `n<3` `log log n` degeneracy guarded; circular block clamped to `[1, n_obs-1]`; `BootstrapConfig` rejects non-int seed, `n_resamples<1`, and non-finite / `<1.0` block_length. **4-agent review fixes applied:** (a) p-value convention unified to `>=` across all three tests (conservative); (b) Romano-Wolf step-down vectorized `O(B·m²)→O(B·m)` via a right-to-left `np.maximum.accumulate` suffix-max scan; (c) seed-not-int + `block_length<1` validation added; (d) every citation verified. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a bootstrap is **inherently `O(n_resamples·n_obs·n_strategies)`** — NOT an `O(1)` hot path and never claimed to be; offline Stage-4 code (top ~1,000 candidates, ~10-20 min, line 404), memory bounded `O(n_obs·m + B·m)` (no `(B,n,m)` tensor). **Size/FWER control is asymptotic** (as the papers prove), not exact in finite samples: bootstrap variance is mildly downward-biased at small `n`, so measured iid FWER is ~0.08 at `n=200` → ~0.053 at `n=2000` for nominal 0.05 — documented in the module docstring; **no fudge factor invented**. **CI gate (numpy-safe):** `brutex.metrics` eagerly imports numpy (the spa re-export), so the per-module 100% gates for spa + the sibling cpcv/wfo are driven via `--cov=brutex` + `coverage report --include` rather than the dotted `--cov=brutex.metrics.X` (which trips numpy 2.x's "cannot load module more than once" under pytest-cov). **Customer-facing comparison (operator ask — "easy table even millions can understand, no illusion"):** `docs/TRACK1_SPA_COMPARISON.md` — plain-English "is my strategy real or just lucky?" table (naive vs White vs Hansen-SPA vs Romano-Wolf) + an honest guarantees table (✅ guaranteed · 🟡 asymptotic FWER · 🚫 not-O(1)-and-says-so). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_spa.py` → **100% line + branch** on `brutex/metrics/spa.py` (182 stmts / 26 branches); `tests/property/test_spa_properties.py` (hypothesis: p∈[0,1]; determinism; SPA variant ordering; multiplicity never below naive); `tests/golden/test_spa_golden.py` (hand-fixed 8×3 winner/neutral/loser matrix locked under both schemes + bit-for-bit determinism). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + `fno_math` maturin build):** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) clean; `bandit -r` exit 0; spa suite **50 passed**; the three metrics gates (spa 182/26, cpcv 104/34, wfo 76/22) all 100% line+branch back-to-back. **Builds on:** DEC-EXTREME-001 · DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 (#428) · DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 (#430) · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 (#429) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 · CLAUDE.md §1 / §4 / §5 / §10 / §11 COMMON / §12.

432. **DEC-TRADESIM-001 — Stage-2 spot trade-simulation walker: `bool`-per-bar entry signal → int64-paisa `ClosedTrade` round-trips (PR-2)** (2026-06-03, implements PR-2 of the engine-scoping proposal `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_ENGINE_SCOPING.md` — the §9 review's C2 "the spot walker is NEW signal-only code, NOT `ExecutionSimulator`" + the open questions it said PR-2 must CREATE: Q1 same-bar tie-break, Q2 intrabar exit-fill, Q4 the `is_forced_exit_bar` tf-blindness fix). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the ID `DEC-TRADESIM-001` is the authoritative key; it lands as the next free integer **#432** — entries #424-431 were taken by concurrent PRs merged to `main` during this PR's review (DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 #424 / DEC-DHAN-STOCK-MONTHLY-ONLY-001 #425 / DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 #426 / DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 #427 / DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 #428 / DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 #429 / DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 #430 / DEC-STAT-SPA-001 #431), so DEC-TRADESIM-001 renumbered 424→432 on merge. **What shipped:** `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` — the Stage-2 walker. It consumes a `bool`-per-bar **entry-signal** stream (the per-bar "did mask M fire?" output of the Stage-2 supermask kernel) + a `CandleBar` feed and emits `list[ClosedTrade]` (`brutex/metrics/types.py`) that `compute_metrics` (`brutex/metrics/compute.py`) turns into Sharpe + the result row. Public API: `TradeSimWalker` (streaming `.push(bar, entry_signal, exit_signal)` → a `ClosedTrade` on the bar a position closes / else `None`, + `.finish()` once at end; batch `.run(bars, entry_signals, exit_signals)`) + the `simulate_trades(...)` functional wrapper + the `FillPolicy` / `LevelFill` / `SameBarTie` / `DEFAULT_FILL_POLICY` policy types; all added to `brutex/engine/__init__.py` `__all__`. **Signal-only (the §9 C2 finding):** it deliberately does NOT import `ExecutionSimulator` / costs / slippage (which fill at bar CLOSE + apply 5 bps slippage + ₹20 brokerage in `Decimal` — correct for Track-2 options, WRONG for spot per `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md:640-657`). P&L is the per-unit directional price move in **int64 paisa** end-to-end (no sizing — spot is research, not execution); rupees→paisa REUSES the canonical `brutex.engine.stage1a._price_to_paisa` seam (one source of truth, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON; sibling-private import carries the DEC-P0-017 `# pyright: ignore[reportPrivateUsage]`). **Fill conventions — the CONFIGURABLE `FillPolicy` (resolves the spec's open questions, default = the conservative choice):** entry is LOCKED to the next bar's OPEN (signal on bar N → enter @N+1 OPEN, spec line 240); the 15:20 IST forced exit is LOCKED to the forced bar's OPEN and **overrides every other exit** (spec line 658); a Mode-B signal exit is LOCKED to the next bar's OPEN (spec line 641). The two genuinely-open questions are the knobs: **(Q1) same-bar SL+TP tie-break** = `SameBarTie.SL_FIRST` (pessimistic, default) vs `TP_FIRST` (optimistic); **(Q2) SL/TP intrabar fill** = `LevelFill.AT_LEVEL` (fill at the trigger price, default) vs `NEXT_OPEN` (fill at the next bar's open — the spot "no order book, no fiction" stance of spec 640-654; falls back to the trigger bar's CLOSE when there is no next bar). End-of-data closes a still-open position at the last bar's CLOSE. **Single position / non-overlap** (Track 1 is non-overlapping — `time_in_market_pct` assumes it): while a position is open, entry signals are ignored, and an entry signal ON a bar where a position just closed is dropped (the exit bar is consumed). A signal whose N+1 entry bar is itself a forced-exit bar opens NO trade. **MFE/MAE** are folded per in-position bar (full high/low on a range-held bar; OPEN-only on a forced / next-open exit bar), both stored as `>= 0` magnitudes. **Q4 — `is_forced_exit_bar` tf-blindness FIX (`brutex/calendars/nse.py`):** the function took `tf_minutes` but IGNORED it (`return t >= 15:20`), so a coarse-TF bar whose *span* straddles 15:20 (e.g. a 15-minute bar opening 15:15 IST → runs to 15:30) was silently MISSED. Now a bar is forced iff its `[open, open + tf_minutes)` window's close is strictly after 15:20 (`close_seconds > forced_seconds`); identical to the old test for 1-minute bars, tf-aware for the rest; raises `ValueError` on `tf_minutes < 1`. The walker converts each bar UTC→IST via the shared `brutex.calendars.nse.IST` and passes its `tf_minutes`, so the forced exit is correct on every resampled timeframe. **No look-ahead (CLAUDE.md §4, Golden Rule #5):** a forward-only state machine — a trade reads only bars from its entry through its exit; the next-bar-OPEN fills make bar M+1 *part of* the trade that fills on it, never a peek. A property test asserts it directly (mutating every bar strictly after a trade's exit can never change that trade). **O(1) per bar (Golden Rule #5):** each `push` does constant work (a fixed set of paisa comparisons + at most one open/close, no scan-back, no growing per-bar state) — the per-bar claim, NOT the whole walk (the trade list grows with #trades, inherent output; §9 F-5/M3). A MEASURED bench (`tests/bench/test_engine_trade_sim_o1.py`, best-of-5, 1k vs 100k bars at fixed intraday + signal density) reports **per-bar ratio 1.01× (ceiling 5×)** — flat. **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** pure — no globals/wall-clock/RNG; a property test asserts the same bars+signals → the same trades. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12 — 7 types):** `tests/unit/test_engine_trade_sim.py` (40 tests — init validation, long/short SL+TP at level, same-bar SL-first/TP-first, forced-exit entry-skip + mid-trade override + tf-aware coarse-TF, signal exit, NEXT_OPEN fill + its no-next-bar fallback, EOD close, single-position + exit-bar-signal-drop, the `_levels` SL/TP optionality matrix, MFE/MAE, the streaming push/finish API); `tests/property/test_engine_trade_sim_properties.py` (determinism, no-look-ahead future-mutation, non-overlap + ClosedTrade invariants — hypothesis, 200 examples each); `tests/golden/test_engine_trade_sim_golden.py` (two hand-derived fixtures — a long TP+SL+forced triple and a short signal-exit — locked to literal `ClosedTrade` lists, every field hand-computed in the docstring, the byte-equality oracle, + streaming==batch + NEXT_OPEN); `tests/bench/test_engine_trade_sim_o1.py` (the per-bar O(1)-ratio gate via `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py::ratio_ceiling`); `tests/unit/test_calendar_nse.py::TestForcedExitTimeframeAware` (8 regression tests for the Q4 fix — the 15:15/15m straddle, same-open-different-tf, the 5m exact-15:20 boundary, 1-minute legacy parity, sub-minute seconds, 1-day, the `ValueError`). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** `brutex/engine/trade_sim.py` per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (168 stmts / 50 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial); `brutex/calendars/nse.py` **100%** (98/20) under the calendar suite; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) all clean on the module + all 5 test files; unit + property + golden + calendar = **105 passed**; the bench passes (ratio 1.01×). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this is PR-2 of the multi-PR engine effort — a correct, deterministic, O(1)-per-bar signal-only walker that turns mask-hits into `ClosedTrade`s; it does NOT itself run a sweep, wire Stage 1A→2, or meet the 33B / 2-4 day SLA (single-threaded). The instrumented `evaluate(N)` accessor that would turn look-ahead Property **P-06** into a LIVE enforcer is still ROADMAP (the no-look-ahead invariant is enforced here by the future-mutation property test, the same mechanism PR-1 used); Stage 1B (PR-3, gated on the §9 C-06 coarse-score resolution), the runner FSM + `brutex sweep` CLI (PR-4), and the result-store oracle (PR-5) remain FUTURE. A per-bar hot-path micro-optimisation flagged by the §9 hot-path agent — feeding the walker pre-converted int-paisa OHLC from the Stage-1A producer instead of re-deriving from `CandleBar` `Decimal`s each bar — is intentionally DEFERRED to the PR-4 driver wiring (where the paisa-bar interface is introduced); this PR already trims the redundant conversions (lazy forced-exit check on idle bars, lazy open-paisa, close converted once at EOD) and the per-bar cost is O(1)/flat at ratio 1.01×, so the deferral only leaves a constant-factor win for the 33B sweep, not a complexity regression. **Builds on:** DEC-ENGINE-DRIVER-001 (#423, the Stage-1A producer whose `_price_to_paisa` seam this reuses) · the §9 hostile review `docs/VERIFICATION_2026-06-03_ENGINE_SCOPING.md` (C2 + open Qs Q1/Q2/Q4) · `brutex/metrics/{types,compute}.py` (the `ClosedTrade` → `compute_metrics` consumer, already built) · `brutex.calendars.nse` (IST + the fixed `is_forced_exit_bar`) · `brutex.strategies.types.Side` · CLAUDE.md §4 (no look-ahead) / §5 (O(1)) / §11 COMMON / §12 (7 test types) / §13 (merge-readiness charter).

433. **DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 — `brutex/metrics/lockbox.py` + `brutex/metrics/monte_carlo.py`: the last two Stage-4 filter engines (Lockbox held-out validation #8 + Monte-Carlo entry-permutation #9) — all nine Stage-4 filter engines now exist** (2026-06-03, implements the two remaining Stage-4 filters of `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 4 — Statistical filters": item #8 Lockbox (lines 433-463, **DEC-LOCK-001** adaptive window) + item #9 Monte-Carlo permutation (lines 464-480, **DEC-EXTREME-001**). CLAUDE.md §9 4-agent hostile review ran on the diff. Preceded by a 4-agent workspace verification of the post-merge-storm `main` — static gates GREEN, docs/ledger consistent (one agent's "duplicate #428-430 entries" CRITICAL was a verified hallucination — grep line-numbers misread as entry-numbers; #428-431 each appear exactly once), Stage-4 metrics coherence CONFIRMED; the only finding was the local venv missing the `[data]` extra (CI installs it).) **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID `DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001` is authoritative; lands at the next free integer **#433** after #432 (`DEC-TRADESIM-001`, PR #332) which merged to `main` during this PR's review; if sibling PRs claim #433 during review it renumbers, ID-not-integer per the ledger convention. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/metrics/lockbox.py` — `lockbox_evaluation(trade_returns, trade_days, *, training_sharpe, training_max_drawdown, default_window_days=182, min_trades=500, sharpe_tolerance=0.30, mdd_tolerance=0.50) -> LockboxResult`. The held-out window is the most-recent `default_window_days` (~6 months); if it holds `< min_trades` it auto-extends BACKWARDS (day-aligned to the day of the `min_trades`-th most-recent trade) to reach the floor; if even all history is below the floor → `LockboxStatus.INSUFFICIENT_N` (spec line 443). Pass gates (spec 451-454): count `>= min_trades`, `lockbox_sharpe >= training_sharpe·(1-sharpe_tolerance)`, `lockbox_max_drawdown <= training_max_drawdown·(1+mdd_tolerance)`. Sharpe REUSES the COMMON `cpcv.sharpe_of_returns` (CLAUDE.md §11 — one source of truth); MDD is the cumulative-return peak-to-trough decline. The *data isolation* (the "any access outside Stage 4.8 raises" guarantee, spec 434) is the orchestrator's job, NOT this pure gate. (2) `brutex/metrics/monte_carlo.py` — `monte_carlo_permutation_test(observed_statistic, n_bars, n_entries, evaluate, *, seed, n_permutations=1000, alpha=0.01) -> MonteCarloResult`. Relocates the `n_entries` entry signals to random bar positions `B` times and re-runs the **injected** exit logic (`evaluate` callable — decoupled from the future trade simulator, exactly the spec seam "re-run the same exit logic", spec 468); the one-sided permutation p-value is the **bias-corrected** `(1 + #{perm >= observed}) / (B + 1)` (**Phipson & Smyth 2010**, *"Permutation P-values Should Never Be Zero"*, SAGMB 9(1) — the standard valid estimator, never exactly 0; no invented constant); pass = `p < alpha`. A non-finite permuted statistic is conservatively "did not beat". **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** lockbox is pure (no RNG); monte_carlo is deterministic under its mandatory `seed` (`numpy.random.default_rng`) — same inputs ⇒ bit-identical outputs. **Edge cases (no NaN/inf — spec 746):** both reject non-1D / mismatched-length / empty / non-finite inputs + out-of-range config with clear `ValueError`; lockbox returns `lockbox_sharpe=None` (not NaN) for a degenerate window; monte_carlo validates seed-is-int / observed-finite / `1<=n_entries<=n_bars` / `n_permutations>=1` / `alpha in (0,1)`. The `LockboxStatus.PASS = "pass"` string trips ruff S105 / bandit B105 (member named PASS is in the linters' password word-list) — a status label, not a credential; suppressed per-line with rationale (`# noqa: S105 # nosec B105`, DEC-P0-001 idiom). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** lockbox is `O(n_trades)`; monte_carlo is `O(B)` calls to `evaluate` — offline Stage-4 batch (spec: ~1,000 shuffles × top-10 candidates), NOT an `O(1)` per-bar hot path; never claimed to be. This PR ships the two filter ENGINES — it does NOT build the end-to-end Stage-4 cascade runner that chains all nine, nor wire `lockbox_sharpe`/`lockbox_mdd_pct` into the result-row schema (deferred; the cascade is the next decision). With this, **all nine Stage-4 filter engines exist as standalone pure functions** (DSR #430, CPCV #428, Reality-Check/SPA #431, PBO #430, Romano-Wolf #431, Walk-Forward #428, Lockbox + Monte-Carlo here). **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_lockbox.py` (PASS/FAIL/INSUFFICIENT_N statuses, default-vs-extended window, every gate, validation, the whitebox `_max_drawdown` empty-array branch) → **100% line+branch** on `lockbox.py` (96 stmts / 32 branches); `tests/unit/test_monte_carlo.py` (real-edge / no-edge / dominated / NaN-conservative / `n_entries==n_bars` / determinism / every guard) → **100%** on `monte_carlo.py` (42 / 18); `tests/property/test_lockbox_mc_properties.py` (hypothesis: lockbox determinism + gate/status invariants; monte_carlo `p∈(0,1]`, the exact `(1+n_beaten)/(B+1)` identity, determinism, the never-beats/always-beats extremes); `tests/golden/test_lockbox_mc_golden.py` (hand-fixed 8-trade lockbox + seeded MC, byte-exact). New strict per-module 100% CI gates (numpy-safe `--cov=brutex` + `coverage report --include` form). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + `[data,ui]` extras + `fno_math` maturin build):** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) clean on both modules + all 4 test files; `bandit -r` exit 0; the full lockbox+MC suite **44 passed**; both per-module gates **100% line+branch** back-to-back. **Customer-facing comparison (operator ask):** `docs/TRACK1_STAGE4_FILTERS.md` — a plain-English "all nine Stage-4 filters at a glance" table (what each catches · pass rule · build status). **Builds on:** DEC-EXTREME-001 (the 9-filter Stage-4 pipeline) · DEC-LOCK-001 (the adaptive-window rule) · DEC-STAT-SPA-001 (#431) / DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 (#428) / DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 (#430) (the sibling Stage-4 engines, shared `brutex/metrics/__init__.py`) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, `sharpe_of_returns` COMMON) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §4 / §5 (O(1) honestly N/A offline) / §9 / §10 / §11 COMMON / §12.
434. **DEC-COVERAGE-PARQUET-RESILIENT-001 — the `/coverage` lake reads survive one corrupt / version-incompatible Parquet file instead of 500-ing the whole endpoint** (2026-06-03, operator-reported: a live dashboard returned HTTP 500 `_duckdb.Error: don't know what type: \r` from `GET /api/v1/coverage/options` while a background pull was writing the lake). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID is authoritative; lands at the next free integer **#434** (main merged #431 DEC-STAT-SPA-001 + #432 DEC-TRADESIM-001 + #433 DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 during this work). **Root cause (verified — CLAUDE.md §6 facts + a local repro, no hallucination):** `summarize_option_datasets` / `summarize_spot_datasets` (`brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`) each read the lake with a single `read_parquet('<dir>/**/*.parquet', union_by_name=true)` aggregate. DuckDB's parquet reader is **all-or-nothing over a glob** — if ANY matched file is unreadable (corrupt, truncated, or carrying a schema the running DuckDB cannot map; the operator's `don't know what type: \r` is DuckDB's type-name parser choking on a byte read from one file's schema), the WHOLE scan raises `duckdb.Error` and the endpoint 500s — even though both endpoints' docstrings PROMISE "never a 500". The writer IS atomic (`option_parquet_writer._atomic_write_parquet`: tmp `*.parquet.tmp` + `os.replace`, and the glob excludes `*.tmp`), so a mid-write file is NOT the trigger — it is a completed-but-unreadable file. Confirmed locally (DuckDB 1.5.3 + polars): a `*.parquet` lacking the trailing `PAR1` magic makes `read_parquet(glob)` raise, and binding the readable file LIST instead aggregates cleanly. **What shipped (reliability only — happy path byte-identical):** one COMMON helper `_aggregate_parquet_resilient(conn, directory, sql, *, source)` (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON — both coverage summaries route through it, zero copy-paste): the FAST path binds the `<directory>/**/*.parquet` glob to the one `?` and returns `fetchall()` exactly as before (one scan, no behaviour change, O(1) steady-state per Golden Rule #5); ONLY on a `duckdb.Error` does the DEGRADED path engage — it probes each `directory.rglob('*.parquet')` with `SELECT 1 … LIMIT 1`, SKIPS the unreadable file(s) (each logged `coverage.parquet_skip` with `source` + `path` + the DuckDB reason so the operator can quarantine it), and re-runs the SAME `sql` over the readable subset bound as a LIST; when NO file is readable it logs `coverage.parquet_unreadable` and returns `[]` (an empty summary, never an exception). `db_view.py` gains its first `structlog` logger for these two events. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** a skipped file is OMITTED from coverage, never silently counted — a degraded read shows FEWER series/bars (or 0), never a wrong total; the 500 → 200-with-partial-data is the reliability win, while the underlying corrupt file still needs operator quarantine (the log names it). The other diagnostics in the same operator report are NOT bugs: the rate limiter (`brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`) correctly paces the adaptive [3..5] r/s token bucket; the LOW `effective_rps` (~0.6–0.8 vs the 3 r/s budget) is **latency-bound, not limiter-bound** — a SEQUENTIAL pull's throughput ≈ 1/latency and Dhan's observed per-call `latency_ms_p95` is multi-second (DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 already lowered the timeout 30→10 s + added the bounded fast-retry that emits `dhan.retry`); and the repeated `/coverage/*` log lines are the dashboard's normal 4 000 ms `setInterval` live-refresh (`templates/coverage.html`), not a malfunction. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py` per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (202 stmts / 80 branches, 0 miss / 0 partial); 4 new tests in `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py` (options: skip-one-corrupt + all-unreadable→`[]`; spot: skip-one-corrupt + all-unreadable→0 bars, each asserting the `coverage.parquet_*` structlog event); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` both **0 errors**; `bandit` clean; the db_view + coverage suites **177 passed** and the coverage-endpoint suites **34 passed**, no regressions. **Builds on:** DEC-OPTIONS-COVERAGE-LAKE-001 (the options-coverage lake read this hardens) · DEC-STORE-THREADSAFE-001 (the `_LockedReadConn` execute→fetch view used unchanged) · DEC-DHAN-CALL-TIMEOUT-RETRY-001 / DEC-DHAN-RATE-LOGGING-001 (the rate/latency diagnostics cited) · CLAUDE.md §10 (honest envelope) / §11 COMMON / §12 (7 test types).

434. **DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001 — the pre-open report 500'd on `M&M`: a read-side symbol-allowlist that disagreed with the write-side denylist (CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON)** (2026-06-03, operator: "Why error resolve this dude" — `GET /api/v1/reports/preopen.xlsx?from=2026-01-01&to=2026-06-03` returned **500 Internal Server Error**; the server log showed `ValueError: illegal candle symbol 'M&M'` from `brutex/dashboard/db_view.py:_validate_candle_coords`). **Root cause (a single-source-of-truth divergence):** the **write** path (`brutex/data/partition.py:_validate_symbol`) validates symbols with a *denylist* — it rejects only filesystem-illegal characters (`/ \ : * ? " < > | \0`), so the ingest happily writes a `…/bars/NSE/CASH/M&M/…` partition; but the dashboard **read** path (`db_view.py:_SYMBOL_RE`) used a tighter *allowlist* `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.\-]*$` that omitted `&`, so the report rejected the very symbol the lake legitimately held. `M&M` (Mahindra & Mahindra) and `GVT&D` (GE Vernova T&D) are real NSE F&O-eligible underlyings **present in** `tests/fixtures/fo_mktlots_real.csv` (lines 85, 73); `M&MFIN` (Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services) is likewise a real F&O underlying but is **not** in that fixture (Golden Rule #1: only `M&M`/`GVT&D` are fixture-evidenced here); the "all symbols" download (no `?symbols=`) hit `M&M` and crashed the **whole** export. **What shipped (one-character-class fix, plus the guard that pins it):** (1) `db_view.py` — `_SYMBOL_RE` now admits `&`: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.&\-]*$`. `&` is **neither** a path separator **nor** a DuckDB-glob metacharacter (`* ? [ ] { }`) and the read glob is a **bound** `read_parquet(?)` parameter, so admitting it CANNOT widen the glob, traverse the tree, or inject SQL — the path-traversal / glob-injection guard (and the explicit `..` reject) is fully preserved. This also fixes the candle **viewer** (`query_candles`), not just the report (both route through `_validate_candle_coords`). The option-side analog (`_OPTION_SEGMENT_RE`) is **unchanged** — its series segment is built from the numeric `security_id` (`db_view.py:819`), never the symbol text, so it never contains `&`. **Scope:** read-allowlist only; the engine, the lake layout, and the write path are untouched. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_dashboard_db_query.py` — `query_candles` now SERVES `M&M` candles (round-trips 2 bars); a parametrized **write↔read consistency** test asserts `build_partition_path` (write) and `_validate_candle_coords` (read) accept the same `{M&M, M&MFIN, GVT&D}` set so the two validators can never silently drift again; a parametrized negative test pins that `* ? [ ] { }` and spaces stay rejected. `tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py` — full write→resolve→build→render path for `M&M` (escaped to `M&amp;M`). `tests/unit/test_dashboard_reports_routes.py` — the exact reported request (`from=…&to=…`, no `?symbols=`) over a lake holding `M&M` now returns **200** (was 500). **Verified (project venv, py3.12 + `[data,ui]` + `fno_math`):** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) clean; `db_view.py` **100% line+branch** (200 stmts / 80 branches) across its two test files. **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (#424, the report) · DEC-DB-QUERY-001 (the candle read path) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON (the principle this restores).

435. **DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-STYLE-001 — the pre-open `.xlsx` gets the NSE look: bold header + bold SYMBOL column, a merged bold-centred date-range TITLE row, and precise per-column widths** (2026-06-03, operator: "make the headers and symbols name to look thick like same as shown in screenshot … But in that case how will you provide the date dude? … why the spaces are not proper and precise — make it precise"). **The date question, answered:** the NSE pre-open file states its date ONCE in the sheet *title* (`MW-Pre-Open-Market-27-May-2026`) because it is a **single-day** snapshot; BruteX exports a **multi-day range**, so the date is provided **two** complementary ways — (a) the existing per-row **`DATE` column** (every row self-describing across the range) AND (b) a **row-1 title banner** `Pre-Open Market: <from> to <to>` mirroring NSE's titled look. **What shipped (still a dependency-free stdlib OOXML writer — no `openpyxl`/`xlsxwriter` to vet through the licence/lockfile gates):** `brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py` gains an `xl/styles.xml` part (default font, **bold** font, **bold + horizontally-centred** font) wired via the workbook rels + content-types; `_sheet_xml` now emits row 1 = the merged (`A1:F1`), bold, centred title; row 2 = the **bold** header; data from row 3 with a **bold SYMBOL column** (money cells stay default — numbers right-align natively); a `<cols>` block gives each column a precise width (`_COL_WIDTHS`, 1:1 with `REPORT_COLUMNS`) so the sheet opens un-cramped (the operator's "make the spaces precise"); the freeze pane now pins **both** the title + header (`ySplit="2"`) and the auto-filter sits on the header row. Element order follows the OOXML `CT_Worksheet` sequence (`sheetViews → cols → sheetData → autoFilter → mergeCells`) so Excel/Numbers open it with **no repair prompt**. `render_xlsx(rows, *, title=None)` takes the banner (the route passes the requested `[from,to]`); omitted ⇒ derived from the rows' date span. **Determinism preserved (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7):** fixed zip member timestamps + deterministic part order ⇒ byte-identical re-render. **Verified for real (no illusion):** every XML part is well-formed AND a strict third-party reader (`openpyxl`, used only as a *test-time* check, NOT a runtime dep) opens the workbook and confirms — title bold + centred + merged `A1:F1`, all 6 header cells bold, the SYMBOL data cell bold while money cells are not, the exact column widths, freeze at `A3`, and `M&M` round-tripping. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_preopen_report.py` — styles part + bold font present, merged date-range title, bold header/SYMBOL vs plain numbers, default-title date-range derivation, empty-report bare label, `_COL_WIDTHS` aligned to `REPORT_COLUMNS`; `tests/unit/test_dashboard_reports_routes.py` — the banner carries the requested range end-to-end. `preopen_report.py` **100% line+branch** (106 stmts / 22 branches). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** styling + a title banner only — the numbers, their NSE-paisa fidelity, and the O(1)-per-row build are unchanged from DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001. **Customer-facing comparison (operator ask — "easy understandable comparison even any human can understand"):** `docs/TRACK1_PREOPEN_REPORT.md` — a plain-English NSE ↔ BruteX column-by-column table + the date-handling explainer + before/after the M&M fix. **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (#424) · DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001 (#434, same PR) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the 2-dp display rule) · CLAUDE.md §10 (honest limits).
436. **DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 — thread-safe parallelisation of the Dhan ingest loop so the pull saturates UP TO the 5 r/s ceiling (was ~1 r/s sequential)** (2026-06-03, operator: "make the pull saturate the existing 5 r/s rate ceiling — today it runs ~1 r/s sequentially"). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the ID `DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001` is the authoritative key; rebased onto current `main` it lands at the next free integer **#436** (main merged #433 DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 + #434 DEC-COVERAGE-PARQUET-RESILIENT-001 + #434 DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001 + #435 DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-STYLE-001 during this work — main carries a duplicate #434, so #436 is the next free integer; the decision ID, not the number, is authoritative, same convention as #428/#430/#431/#432). **Problem:** the multi-instrument spot fan-out (`run_dhan_spot_ingest`) and the options fan-out (`run_dhan_options_ingest`) ran their OUTER loops **sequentially** — one `(instrument, interval)` pair / one underlying at a time — so with a typical ~2-3 s per-call round-trip the achieved rate sat at **~1 r/s** against Dhan's verified **5 r/s** Data-API ceiling (CLAUDE.md §6), leaving ~80% of the budget idle (Little's law: `achieved ≈ in_flight / latency`, and `in_flight` was 1). **What shipped — parallelise the OUTER loop only, reusing the existing infra (no reinvention, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON):** the per-window spine (`ingest_spot`, the rolling-option series fetch) is BYTE-UNCHANGED; only the outer fan-out now maps through the already-built `brutex/orchestrator/parallel.py::PoolRunParallel` (a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` + `workers_to_saturate` Little's-law sizing, `MAX_FANOUT=32`) and the already-thread-safe `AdaptiveTokenBucket`. **Spot** parallelises per `(instrument, interval)` pair (each writes a DISTINCT, path-isolated lake partition → no write lock needed); **options** parallelise per underlying (each worker runs its existing 4-deep `flags×codes×strikes×types` series fan SEQUENTIALLY inside). Both expose an INJECTABLE `run_parallel: RunParallel | None` param (defaults to the real pool) so the fan-out stays 100% unit-testable with a synchronous fake (mirrors `universe_phases.run_two_phase`); both rebuild their aggregate report from the collected `ItemResult`s and emit the per-instrument / per-underlying `ingest.underlying` INFO rollup in a DETERMINISTIC post-pass (spot sorted by `symbol_name`, options by `security_id`) so the log order is reproducible regardless of worker completion order (Rule #4); both keep the `except DhanError → quarantine` + `ingest.quarantine` WARNING and let any non-DhanError SURFACE (preserve the "never raises on DhanError, but a real bug is never swallowed" semantics). **The 7 MANDATORY thread-safety fixes (a `threading.Lock` each; every critical section O(1); NEVER held across network I/O or a sleep):** (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py` `DhanRateController` (the GOVERNOR) — guard `on_rate_limit`/`on_success`/`snapshot`/`current_rps`; **`pace()` copies `self._bucket` into a local UNDER the lock then calls `.acquire()` on the local OUTSIDE the lock** (CRITICAL — holding the lock across the bucket acquire/sleep would re-serialise every worker back to ~1 r/s and defeat the entire change). (2) `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` `CallMeter` — lock `record` + `snapshot` (per call-COMPLETION only, never across the POST). (3) `brutex/data/option_dedup.py` `OptionDedupIndex` — lock `seen`/`add`/`add_if_new` so the check-then-act is atomic (a content key is admitted EXACTLY once across workers; idempotence, Rule #7). (4) `brutex/data/option_sink.py` `OptionBarSink` — a SINGLE-WRITER lock around the dedup→partition-write→audit tail so the hash-chained `AuditWriter` (explicitly NOT thread-safe) advances as exactly one writer (Rule #8); the per-series network fetch runs BEFORE this call, so cross-worker parallelism is fully preserved (the lock only serialises the fast local lake/audit write a single-writer chain requires anyway). (5) `brutex/data/fetch_coverage.py` `FetchCoverage` — lock `is_complete`/`mark_complete`/`completed_count`/`to_records` (defensive; cheap). (6) `brutex/data/catalog.py` `Catalog` — lock `upsert` + the reads (DuckDB connection is not concurrency-safe; the live spot path passes `catalog=None` today but tests wire one — future-proof). (7) **`pull_id` contextvar propagation** — worker threads spawned by `ThreadPoolExecutor` do NOT inherit the structlog contextvar, so `ingest.*` events in workers would lose `pull_id` (regressing DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 #426); each worker now captures `pull_id = current_pull_id()` on the controller thread and RE-BINDS it via `brutex.observability.correlation.pull_id_scope(pull_id)` inside the worker. Left UNCHANGED (already safe): the spot `ParquetBarSink` (path-isolated), `AdaptiveTokenBucket` (its own lock is the shared rate gate), and `PullProgress`. **Dashboard wiring (`pull_controller.py` + `option_pull_controller.py`):** a live pull builds ONE shared `DhanRateController` and derives BOTH the pacing hooks AND a `PoolRunParallel` sized to `workers_to_saturate(controller.current_rps or 5.0, DEFAULT_LATENCY_BUDGET_S)` from it; a dry-run / injected-factory pull → `None` controller → `None` pool (the ingest spine uses its default pool). The sizing seam (`_spot_run_parallel` / `_options_run_parallel`) is a pure, covered function; only the live controller construction is `# pragma: no cover`. No change to range/coverage resolution. **`on_progress` semantics:** for the spot bulk pull it now fires in worker-COMPLETION order (parallelism makes order non-deterministic), so `test_on_progress_forwarded_per_pair` asserts the SET of pairs (each fires once, all clean) — the deterministic surface is the `ingest.underlying` rollup; options `on_progress` fires in the sorted post-pass (deterministic). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10) — mandatory, stated everywhere:** this targets/SATURATES **UP TO ~5 r/s when Dhan is healthy** and CANNOT guarantee a constant 5 r/s — a 429 step-down (`DhanRateController` 5→4→3) + per-call latency spikes lower the achieved rate; the parallelisation is the *mechanism* that lets the rate BUCKET (not a single-threaded loop) be the bottleneck. No docstring / commit claims "guaranteed 5 r/s". **Tests (deterministic — fake clock + fake high-latency adapter, NO real network/sleep; CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/integration/test_dhan_spot_parallel.py` — a discrete-event simulator proves parallel saturates to ~5 r/s with **peak in-flight == max_workers** vs a 1-worker control at ~1/latency r/s (**measured 5.10 r/s vs 0.50 r/s, 10.2× at 10 workers / 2 s latency**), the burst-corrected steady-state rate never exceeds 5 even at the 32-worker cap (Rule #6 guard, incl. a REAL 32-thread `DhanRateController` + `AdaptiveTokenBucket` over a virtual clock), idempotent re-pull issues ZERO net-new fetches (Rule #7), and one terminal-DhanError pair is quarantined while the rest succeed; `tests/integration/test_dhan_options_audit_chain.py` — **the Rule #8 oracle**: runs the real per-underlying fan-out over 8 underlyings (288 series) through the REAL `ThreadPoolExecutor` with a real `AuditWriter` to a tmp file, then `verify_chain` passes + `seq` is 0..N-1 contiguous + rows == material writes (a duplicate re-pull adds zero rows and the chain still verifies); `tests/unit/test_dhan_parallel_locks.py` — barrier-synced high-contention storms for EACH new lock (controller hooks keep `rps` in `[3,5]`; `CallMeter.record` counts every call exactly once; `OptionDedupIndex.add_if_new` admits each key exactly once; `FetchCoverage.mark_complete`; `Catalog.upsert` all-distinct-rows-persist); `tests/unit/test_dhan_spot_parallel_wiring.py` + `tests/unit/test_dhan_options_parallel_wiring.py` — the `run_parallel` seam (every job dispatched once), `pull_id` re-bound into workers (proven by running each worker in a FRESH `contextvars.Context`), the deterministic sorted rollup, the `workers_to_saturate` sizing table ((5,3)→15, (5,1)→5, cap 32, floor 1), and the non-DhanError-surfaces case; `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_pool_sizing.py` — the controller→pool sizing seam. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math` build):** the 6 modified core modules + the 2 dashboard controllers all at per-module **100% line + 100% branch** (`rate_control` 65/6, `client` 122/18, `option_dedup` 46/4, `option_sink` 36/4, `fetch_coverage` 36/2, `catalog` 138/40, `run_ingest` 82/16, `option_universe_ingest` 116/20, `pull_controller` 177/28, `option_pull_controller` 107/18 — 0 miss / 0 partial each); `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (strict) both **0 errors** on every changed source + test file; `bandit -ll` clean. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-PHASED-001 / DEC-UNIVERSE-PULL-8RPS-001 (the `PoolRunParallel` + `workers_to_saturate` infra this reuses) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (#352, the `[3..5]` r/s controller now made thread-safe) · DEC-DHAN-INGEST-LOGGING-001 (#426, the `pull_id` correlation preserved across the pool boundary) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip ledger now thread-safe) · the operator decree "O(1) uniqueness deduplication" (#342, the option dedup guard) · CLAUDE.md §2 rules 6/7/8 · §4 (no pandas hot path / no look-ahead) · §10 (honest envelope) · §11 COMMON (no reinvention — reuse `parallel.py` + `AdaptiveTokenBucket`) · §12 (7 test types).

436. **DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 — `brutex/metrics/cascade.py`: the Stage-4 cascade orchestrator that chains all nine filters end-to-end** (2026-06-03, implements the full Stage-4 pipeline of `docs/TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 4" lines 371-631: hard rejection gates → the nine statistical filters in spec order with short-circuit → composite ranking. CLAUDE.md §9 hostile review (2 parallel agents on the diff) ran before merge and found real defects, all FIXED in this PR: a **BLOCKER** — a constant / zero-variance returns series in a survivor crashed Romano-Wolf (`_require_positive_variance`) uncaught (reality_check tolerates a constant column, RW does not) → now isolated at the SPA stage as a `degenerate returns` rejection so the pool matrix is always valid; two **MAJOR** — (a) the spec's 6th hard gate (`lockbox_sharpe/training_sharpe < 0.5`) was a dead config field → removed + reconciled (subsumed by the stricter Lockbox filter #8, `sharpe_tolerance` 0.30 rejecting below 0.70·training; the out-of-sample lockbox Sharpe is unknowable at the pre-gate), (b) a non-finite scalar metric (`inf` calmar / `nan`) crashed the composite z-score with an opaque `AttributeError` → `CandidateInput.__post_init__` now validates every scalar + series value finite (clear `ValueError`); plus **MINOR** — uncaught engine domain `ValueError`s (DSR radicand, CPCV/WFO too-short, MC entries>bars, Lockbox length-mismatch) now isolate the one bad candidate as a per-stage rejection instead of aborting the sweep, and the DSR `n_trials`+`trial_var` are now both taken over the full entering pool (consistent populations). A second agent verified every cited spec line + threshold + the composite weights (zero findings). The headline "cascade" the prior Stage-4 PRs deferred). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** decision ID `DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001` authoritative; lands at **#436** — `#434`/`#435` are reserved by the already-open PR #339 (`DEC-PREOPEN-AMPERSAND-001` / `DEC-PREOPEN-XLSX-STYLE-001`), so this cedes them to keep the ledger merge-conflict trivial in either merge order, and renumbers further only if another sibling claims #436. **What shipped:** `run_stage4_cascade(candidates, config) -> CascadeReport` — a **pure, deterministic** orchestrator over the nine pre-existing filter *engines* (DSR #430, CPCV/WFO #428, SPA/RW #431, PBO #430, Lockbox/Monte-Carlo #433). Pipeline: (1) **hard rejection gates** (spec 595-600 — total_trades<30, profit_factor<1.2, max_drawdown_pct>30, win_rate<25%∧win_loss_ratio<2.0, max_consecutive_losses>10), scalar, applied first; (2) the **nine filters in spec order with short-circuit** — a candidate failing any filter is rejected and the rejecting `FilterStage` + the failing statistic are recorded; (3) **composite ranking** (spec 607-615 — weighted clamped-[-3,+3] z-scores) of the survivors. **Per-candidate vs pool-level:** DSR/CPCV/WFO/Lockbox/Monte-Carlo score one candidate at a time; **SPA #4, PBO #5, Romano-Wolf #6 are pool-level** — they consume the matrix of the *still-surviving* candidates' returns. Documented cascade semantics (the spec pins each filter's own pass rule, not the cross-filter wiring): SPA p≥α ⇒ the whole surviving pool is data-snooped noise → all rejected; PBO>max ⇒ overfit pool → all rejected (skipped for a lone survivor / a series shorter than one CSCV split-block, since CSCV needs ≥2 strategies + a row count that is a whole multiple of n_splits — the most-recent whole multiple is used); Romano-Wolf ⇒ keep only the FWER rejection set. **Injected, pure (CLAUDE.md §2 r11):** every per-candidate series the filters need (returns / lockbox trades+days / Monte-Carlo entries+exit-logic) is carried on `CandidateInput`, so the orchestrator is deterministic + 100%-testable with hand-built candidates; the production adapter that builds `CandidateInput`s by re-running the Stage-2 trade-sim (`brutex.engine.trade_sim.simulate_trades`, #432) on the top leaderboard rows + reading the lake is DEFERRED (needs real bars). **Determinism (Golden Rule #4):** one mandatory `CascadeConfig.seed` threads the SPA/RW `BootstrapConfig` + the Monte-Carlo seed; same pool + config ⇒ bit-identical `CascadeReport`. **Thresholds:** spec-pinned where given (SPA p<0.05, RW p<0.05, MC p<0.01, WFO ≥0.75 of walks all-3-schemes, Lockbox per #8 + the hard gates); the DSR/CPCV/PBO cut-offs (0.95 / 0.5 / 0.5) are conventional cascade-config defaults flagged as NOT spec-pinned (Golden Rule #1). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** offline Stage-4 batch — `O(K)` per-candidate filter calls + the pool bootstraps, run once on the top ~1,000 candidates; NOT an O(1) hot path and never claimed to be. Edge cases (no NaN/inf, clear errors): empty pool → empty report; duplicate `candidate_id` → `ValueError`; unequal-length pooled returns → `ValueError` (pool filters need a common time axis); pool<2 or too-short series → PBO skipped; degenerate (constant / <2-obs) returns → rejected at SPA before the studentized pool tests; a per-candidate engine domain error (DSR/CPCV/WFO/Lockbox/MC) → that ONE candidate rejected at its stage (never an aborted sweep); non-finite `CandidateInput` scalar/series or empty id → clear `ValueError` at construction. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12):** `tests/unit/test_cascade.py` (32 — a full-pass survivor exercising every keep-branch + composite ranking, a rejection at each of the 10 stages, the pool-filter semantics incl. PBO skip-small/skip-short, every edge guard, the `_zscore_clamped` helper, plus the §9-review hardening: `CandidateInput` finiteness/empty-id validation, the SPA degenerate-returns rejection, and per-candidate engine-error isolation for DSR/CPCV/WFO/Lockbox/MC) → **100% line + branch** on `cascade.py` (262 stmts / 84 branches); `tests/property/test_cascade_properties.py` (hypothesis: per-input verdict, passed-XOR-rejected, survivor bookkeeping, ranking monotone, stage-counts non-increasing, determinism); `tests/golden/test_cascade_golden.py` (a hand-fixed 3-candidate pool → byte-exact survivor set + per-stage counts + verdicts). New strict per-module 100% CI gate (numpy-safe form). **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + `[data,ui]` + `fno_math` build):** ruff + ruff-format + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` (0/0) on the module + 3 test files; `bandit -r` exit 0; the full cascade suite **36 passed**; per-module **100% line+branch** (262/84). **Customer-facing comparison:** `docs/TRACK1_STAGE4_FILTERS.md` updated — the cascade now ties the nine filters into one gauntlet. **Builds on:** DEC-EXTREME-001 (the 9-filter pipeline) · DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 (#430) / DEC-STAT-CPCV-WFO-001 (#428) / DEC-STAT-SPA-001 (#431) / DEC-STAT-LOCKBOX-MC-001 (#433) (the engines it chains) · DEC-TRADESIM-001 (#432, the future series-regeneration source) · DEC-RESULT-STORE-001 (#429, the leaderboard) · CLAUDE.md §1 / §4 / §5 (O(1) honestly N/A offline) / §9 / §10 / §11 COMMON+r11 / §12.

437. **DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001 — dashboard fast-read SPEED CORE: offload every blocking read off the event loop + an O(1) summary cache + incremental coverage counters so read pages stop freezing during a pull** (2026-06-03, operator: "dashboard read pages stop freezing during a data pull, and the coverage/db summary reads become O(1) memory hits instead of O(files) full-lake scans"). **Numbering note (Golden Rule #1):** the decision ID `DEC-DASHBOARD-FASTREAD-001` is the authoritative key; it lands at the next free integer **#437** (main carried a duplicate `#436` — both DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 and DEC-STAT-CASCADE-001 ceded #434/#435 to the already-open PR #339, so #437 is the next free integer; the ID, not the number, is authoritative — same convention as #428/#430/#436). **Three verified root causes (the freeze):** (1) the production read connection is a per-store `_LockedReadConn` (`brutex/data/instrument_store.py`) that acquires ONE global `threading.RLock` from `execute()` until `fetch*()` — so a dashboard read serialised behind the active universe-pull writer; (2) EVERY read route in `brutex/dashboard/app.py` was `async def` but called a BLOCKING DuckDB scan DIRECTLY on the event loop with no `run_in_threadpool`, so one slow scan froze the WHOLE async server (not just that request); (3) `summarize_spot_datasets` / `summarize_option_datasets` (`brutex/dashboard/db_view.py`) glob + `read_parquet` the WHOLE lake on every call, and `templates/coverage.html` polls them every 4 s — so a 200-symbol pull turned every 4 s tick into a full-lake rescan that also blocked the loop. **What shipped (3 deliverables, COMMON — one cache module, no copy-paste, CLAUDE.md §11):** **A1 — offload every blocking read off the event loop.** Each blocking `db_view`/store call in the read routes is now wrapped `await run_in_threadpool(fn, ...)` (`from fastapi.concurrency import run_in_threadpool`): `api_coverage` (store.list_coverage + candidates scan), `api_coverage_spot`, `api_coverage_options`, `api_db_tables`, `api_db_table`, `api_db_columns`, `api_db_query`, `api_db_candles`, `api_db_options`, `api_instruments_stats`, `api_instruments_list`, `api_expiries_list`, `api_contracts_list`, `api_preopen_xlsx`. **Correctness rule honoured:** `store.connection` returns a FRESH `_LockedReadConn` whose RLock MUST be acquired+released on the SAME thread, so every offloaded callable BUILDS + USES `store.connection` INSIDE the threadpool worker (we pass `store`/closures, never a pre-built conn); the existing `try/except ValueError → HTTPException(400)` stays AROUND each `await`, and the request-side validation that itself raises HTTPException (`_parse_filters`, the pre-open date parse) stays on the loop (no I/O) so only the blocking aggregate is offloaded. **A2 — in-memory summary cache** (`brutex/dashboard/summary_cache.py`, NEW): a thread-safe (`threading.Lock`) `SummaryCache` holding the last spot/option summary payloads + a monotonic `generation` int + `computed_at`; `mark_dirty()` bumps the generation; `get_or_refresh(kind, recompute)` returns the cached payload on a clean hit, and recomputes via the INJECTED `recompute` closure ONLY when dirty AND past a **2 s TTL floor** (so a 200-symbol fan-out's hundreds of `mark_dirty` calls trigger at most one rescan per window — a write storm can't become a scan storm); a per-kind in-flight guard collapses two concurrent dirty reads into a single scan; `recompute` runs OUTSIDE the lock (the lock guards only O(1) bookkeeping). Instantiated in `build_app` next to `_pull_job` and INJECTED into the routes (no module globals, CLAUDE.md §4); the route does `await run_in_threadpool(cache.get_or_refresh, "spot", recompute=...)` where the recompute builds `store.connection` on the worker thread. **A3 — incremental coverage counters** (`CoverageCounters` in the same module): a thread-safe per-dataset-label int64 running bar tally + grand total + an update counter; `snapshot()` is O(1) (one dict copy). Hooked into the SINGLE write-progress funnel `BackgroundPullJob._on_progress(label, bars, failed)` (`brutex/dashboard/pull_jobs.py`): `self._counters.add(label, bars)`. Because `bars` is the POST-DEDUP newly-written count, a duplicate re-pull passes `bars == 0` → `add` is a no-op → idempotent for free (Rule 7) and the audit hash-chain (Rule 8) is UNTOUCHED (no change to `option_sink`'s audit section). The counters + the cache are INJECTED into `BackgroundPullJob` via its constructor (the job marks the cache dirty on every write tick); a small read-only route `GET /api/v1/coverage/counters` surfaces `counters.snapshot()` for the headline (a pure in-memory O(1) read, not threadpooled). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10) — verbatim, stated NOT hidden (in the module docstring + here):** a cached summary read = **O(1) per poll** (a dict handoff under one lock, independent of lake file count); the amortised refresh is **still O(files)** (it calls the real `read_parquet` aggregate — the TTL floor bounds how OFTEN that O(files) cost is paid, ≤ once/2 s, it does NOT make the refresh O(1)); the running coverage counter add + `snapshot` = **O(1)**; an arbitrary user `/db` SQL query is inherently **O(rows scanned)** — now non-blocking + paginated but **NOT O(1)**. We never claim "everything is O(1)": the headline counter + the cached summary read are O(1); the underlying lake aggregate is not, and the offloaded-but-uncached `/db` reads still WAIT for the store lock — but on a WORKER thread, so the event loop stays free (proven below). **Measured (the regression oracle, project venv):** with a background thread holding the store RLock for ~1000 ms, `GET /api/v1/state` returned **200 in 2.18 ms**, a cache-served `GET /api/v1/coverage/spot` returned **200 in 2.28 ms** (served from the SummaryCache, touches neither lake nor lock), while an uncached `GET /api/v1/db/tables` correctly took **1005 ms** (it genuinely needs the lock) — but on its threadpool worker, so it did NOT freeze the loop or the two fast reads. **Tests (CLAUDE.md §12, 5 of 7 types — unit/integration/bench + the strict-100 self-gates):** `tests/unit/test_summary_cache.py` (20 — fake recompute + fake clock: cold miss, clean hit served-without-recompute, dirty→recompute-once-past-2 s-floor, dirty-within-floor throttled, 200×mark_dirty→≤1 rescan, zero-floor recomputes-every-read, kind namespacing, generation reflects mark_dirty, the in-flight single-flight guard, recompute-raises clears the guard, barrier-synced `mark_dirty`/`get` thread-safety; CoverageCounters: per-label+total accumulation, `bars==0` AND `bars<0` no-ops, isolated-copy snapshot, JSON `to_dict`, barrier-synced add storm) → **100% line + branch** on `summary_cache.py` (80 stmts / 10 branches); `tests/integration/test_dashboard_responsive_under_write.py` (THE regression oracle — real `InstrumentStore` on tmp_path, a thread holds the whitebox `store._lock` ~1 s, asserts `/api/v1/state` + a cache-served `/api/v1/coverage/spot` return 200 well under the hold time, proving reads no longer block behind the writer / event loop); `tests/integration/test_dashboard_e2e.py` (+16 wired-store tests proving every offloaded route still returns correct JSON + the 400-on-bad-input paths survive the offload + the new counters route); `tests/unit/test_pull_jobs.py` (+5 — the write funnel feeds the counters, injected counters used, `bars==0` re-pull leaves the headline unchanged, the cache is invalidated once per window, the `summary_cache=None` branch skipped) keeping `pull_jobs.py` at **100%** (50/4); `tests/bench/test_summary_cache_o1.py` (cached `get` latency at 10 vs 1000 datasets under `ratio_ceiling(5.0)` via `tests/bench/_o1_tiers.py` — **MEASURED flat: ~497 ns median @ 1000 datasets vs ~609 ns @ 10**, ratio < 1× so it would pass even the strict 1.1× M4-Pro tier; plus a counter-snapshot bench documenting the snapshot is linear-in-labels, never quadratic). **CI:** a `--cov=brutex.dashboard.summary_cache … --cov-fail-under=100` gate block added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (mirrors the existing `db_view` gate); the responsive-under-write + e2e suites co-run in the `pull_jobs` gate so the write-funnel hooks stay exercised end-to-end; the new O(1) bench is auto-discovered by the `ci.yml` `bench` job (`tests/bench/*`) and added to the strict-tier list + `paths` trigger of `bench-m4pro.yml`. **Verified (project venv, Python 3.12 + `[dev,data,ui]` + maturin `fno_math` build):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 8 changed source + test files; `mypy --strict brutex` **0 issues / 165 files**; `pyright` **0 errors / 0 warnings** on every changed source + test file (the 2 whitebox test files carry the established file-top `# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=none` pragma);
