## DEC-DSR-SWEEP-001 (2026-06-04)

460. **DEC-DSR-SWEEP-001 — wire the Deflated Sharpe Ratio over a sweep: penalise each combo's Sharpe for the multiple-testing (`N` combos) it was selected from — the deepest anti-fluke defense** (2026-06-04, operator: *"no illusion ... real guarantee and assurance"*; the DSR is the deepest anti-fluke layer flagged across the session). **Why:** when you search `N` combos, the BEST in-sample Sharpe is inflated by selection ALONE — even on pure noise the maximum of `N` zero-edge trials is positive. A high in-sample Sharpe + a passing OOS holdout (#456 / #458) are necessary but NOT sufficient: a combo can still "win" purely because we tried millions. The DSR (Bailey & López de Prado 2014) deflates the observed Sharpe against the EXPECTED MAXIMUM Sharpe of `N` zero-edge trials → the probability the true Sharpe is positive AFTER the selection-bias correction. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/engine/deflate.py::deflate_sweep(results) -> dict[mask, DeflatedSharpeResult]` — supplies the cross-trial inputs the pure `brutex.metrics.deflated_sharpe.deflated_sharpe_ratio` needs but a single combo cannot carry: `N` = number of combos searched (`len(results)`), `V` = population variance of the defined trial Sharpes. Per combo it returns the DSR (+ `SR_0` + the un-deflated `PSR`) for every combo whose DSR is DEFINED, and OMITS (never crashes) combos where it is not — undefined Sharpe, `<2` trades, or an invalid moment radicand (caught `ValueError`). **Convention (safety-critical — Golden Rule #2):** `compute_metrics` measures Sharpe / skewness / kurtosis on the PER-TRADE return series (`compute.py:543`, `returns = [pnl/start_equity for t in trades]`), so the DSR's `sample_length` = the combo's `total_trades` (frequency matches the Sharpe) and its `kurtosis` = the metrics' EXCESS kurtosis + `GAUSSIAN_KURTOSIS` (the PSR radicand needs the non-excess `g4`). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_deflate.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `deflate.py` (26 stmts / 6 branches; 245 tests across the engine suite), covering empty results, all-undefined-Sharpe (the variance fallback), a valid leaderboard (the `DSR <= PSR`, `SR_0 >= 0`, `n_trials` invariants), each skip guard (Sharpe / skew / kurtosis `None`, `<2` trades), and the invalid-radicand omit (no crash); `mypy --strict` 0; `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a swept leaderboard can now be deflated — the combo that "won" only because we tried millions gets a LOW DSR, the honest "real vs data-mined" number, 100% gated. 🟡 it deflates the IN-SAMPLE sweep Sharpes (the multiple-testing correction); it COMPOSES with the OOS holdout (#456/#458) but does not itself re-run out-of-sample. `N = len(results)` treats every swept mask as one trial (the conservative, standard interpretation); the CPCV pass-rate is the remaining Stage-3 refinement. 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds). **Builds on:** DEC-STAT-DSR-PBO-001 (the pure `deflated_sharpe_ratio` this wires) · DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 (#445, the `(mask, ResultMetrics)` sweep shape this consumes) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the per-trade Sharpe/skew/kurtosis convention) · CLAUDE.md §2 · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-CPCV-ROBUSTNESS-001 (2026-06-04)

461. **DEC-CPCV-ROBUSTNESS-001 — wire CPCV robustness over a combo's returns: the LAST Stage-3 layer — does the combo work across MANY time-splits, not one lucky period?** (2026-06-04, operator: *"no illusion ... real guarantee and assurance ... go ahead with the plan"*). **Why:** a combo can pass the OOS holdout (ONE train/test split, #456/#458) AND survive the DSR (multiple-testing, #460) yet still owe its whole edge to a single lucky stretch. Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (López de Prado 2018, Ch. 12) tests it across ALL `C(16,8) = 12,870` held-out fold combinations: the pass-rate is the fraction whose held-out Sharpe is positive — high ⇒ robust across periods, low ⇒ one-lucky-period. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/engine/robustness.py::cpcv_robustness(returns, *, n_groups=16, n_test_groups=8, min_sharpe=0.0) -> float | None` — wires the pure `brutex.metrics.cpcv.cpcv_pass_rate` to a combo's PER-TRADE return series with a SAFE guard: a series too short to partition into `n_groups` folds (`< 16` by default) is CPCV-UNDEFINED → returns `None` (`cpcv_pass_rate` would raise `ValueError` via `_validate_params` when `n_groups > n_samples`; the wrapper turns that into a graceful `None` so the caller computes CPCV only for combos with enough trades). **Convention (Golden Rule #2):** the input `returns` are the combo's per-trade returns (`pnl_paisa / start_equity_paisa` per closed trade — the SAME series `compute_metrics` uses for Sharpe), so the fold Sharpes match the rest of the pipeline. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_robustness.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `robustness.py` (8 stmts / 2 branches; 249 tests across the engine suite), covering the too-few-returns → `None` guard (both branches), a varied all-positive series (a high pass-rate in (0,1]), a varied all-negative series (every fold fails → 0.0), and a custom `n_groups` that lowers the fold-count threshold; `mypy --strict` 0; `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a combo's returns can now be CPCV-tested across 12,870 held-out folds — the "does it survive in MANY periods?" robustness number, 100% gated; this COMPLETES the Stage-3 anti-illusion stack (hard gates → OOS holdout → Sharpe/DD tolerance → DSR → CPCV). 🟡 it takes a RETURNS series — the caller computes it from a candidate's trades (`[pnl/start_equity for t in trades]`); the end-to-end "run combo → returns → CPCV" + a pass-rate threshold composed into the leaderboard is the thin glue that follows. CPCV's purge/embargo govern the TRAINING set (a no-op for the signal-only test-fold returns, per `cpcv.py`). 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds). **Builds on:** the `brutex.metrics.cpcv` module (the pure `cpcv_pass_rate` this wires — López de Prado 2018, Ch. 12) · DEC-DSR-SWEEP-001 (#460, the prior Stage-3 layer) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the per-trade return convention) · CLAUDE.md §2 · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-COMBO-RETURNS-001 (2026-06-04)

462. **DEC-COMBO-RETURNS-001 — the producer brick: run a combo over bars → its per-trade return series, connecting the engine's trades to the returns-based validators (CPCV / lockbox)** (2026-06-04, operator: *"go ahead with the plan ... real guarantee and assurance ... no illusion"*). **Why:** DEC-CPCV-ROBUSTNESS-001 (#461) added `cpcv_robustness(returns)` but NOTHING produced its `returns` input — the sweep pipeline (`evaluate_combo` / `metrics_for_mask`) computes the per-trade returns INSIDE `compute_metrics` and exposes only the aggregated `ResultMetrics`, not the raw series. This is the missing producer that closes that gap, so CPCV (and any future returns-based validator) is usable END-TO-END on a real combo. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/engine/robustness.py::combo_returns(bars, mask, *, direction, tf_minutes, stop_loss_paisa, take_profit_paisa, start_equity_paisa, proximity, prior_n) -> list[float]` — builds the Stage-1A `bar_bits`, projects the mask via `mask_to_entry_signals`, walks the trades via `simulate_trades`, and emits one return per closed trade as `trade.pnl_paisa / start_equity_paisa` — the SAME formula `compute_metrics` uses (`compute.py:543`), so a downstream CPCV / lockbox sees fold Sharpes consistent with the rest of the pipeline (Golden Rule #2). Empty bars → `ValueError`; a no-trade combo → empty list. The end-to-end robustness check is now `cpcv_robustness(combo_returns(bars, mask, …))`. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_robustness.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `robustness.py` (22 stmts / 4 branches; 252 tests across the engine suite); NEW deterministic tests on a rising-then-falling 5-bar session — empty-bars raise, a BUY held to the falling tail → one NEGATIVE return, the mirror SELL → one POSITIVE return (direction-correct, value = `pnl/start_equity`); `mypy --strict` 0; `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the engine → returns → validator path is now complete — `combo_returns` REUSES the proven Stage-1A / trade-sim bricks (no re-implementation) and emits the canonical per-trade return series; 100% gated. 🟡 it RE-RUNS the combo (build + walk) to recover the trades the sweep discards — fine for validating the top-K survivors (not the full sweep); a future refactor could expose the returns from the sweep pass if that ever matters. 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds). **Builds on:** DEC-CPCV-ROBUSTNESS-001 (#461, the consumer this feeds) · DEC-SWEEP-DRIVER-001 (#445, the `build_bar_bits → mask_to_entry_signals → simulate_trades` chain reused) · DEC-METRICS-001 (#305, the `pnl/start_equity` per-trade return convention) · CLAUDE.md §2 · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.
## DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (2026-06-04)

463. **DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 — reconcile the fetch-coverage skip-ledger against the LAKE + stop marking empty fetches "done": fixes the missing 1-day datasets + the conflict flood** (2026-06-04, operator: *"the successful window which is available in db table should never ever be refetched ... not started or failed window should be pulled ... partial failed data should never ever be stored"* + the NIFTY/ADANIENT/COALINDIA 1-day `no_data` logs). **Root cause (two bugs, one fix):** (a) `_ingest_one_window` called `coverage.mark_complete(key)` UNCONDITIONALLY on any non-exception fetch — so a 0-bar response (an empty 200 under a 429 storm, or a genuinely-empty range) stamped the window "done" → skipped forever → the missing NIFTY/ADANIENT/COALINDIA 1-day datasets (`universe.pull.ok no_data=1`); (b) the skip-ledger read ONLY its `<lake>/fetch_coverage.json` sidecar, never the lake — so a fresh-clone / lost / never-persisted ledger re-fetched EVERY window even though the Parquet bars were already stored → the `ingest.conflict` flood on NIFTY 1-minute. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py` — mark a window complete ONLY when the vendor actually returned bars (`len(raw_bars) > 0`, NOT `bars_appended`: a re-pull whose bars are all already stored dedups to 0 appended via keep-first yet the window IS complete, so it stays marked); a 0-bar window is left un-marked → re-pulled next run (un-sticks the 1-day). (2) NEW `brutex/dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py` — `reconcile_windows` (pure) + `reconcile_coverage_with_lake` (wired at pull start in BOTH `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles`): the LAKE is the single source of truth — every window the stored span ENCLOSES (`first_date <= window_start AND window_end <= last_date`, bars > 0) is marked complete → skipped (no re-fetch / flood), while a window the lake does NOT cover (a missing 1-day, a recent gap) stays un-marked → re-pulled. Conservative by design: re-fetching an un-enclosed window is safe (keep-first idempotent, DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001), and the window tiling reuses the SAME `_windows` the ingest uses (COMMON), so a marked key matches the ingest skip probe byte-for-byte (`market="dhan"`, `security_id=symbol_name`). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_coverage_reconcile.py` (10) → `brutex.dashboard.coverage_reconcile` **100.00%** (33 stmts / 14 branch, 0 miss) incl. a REAL-Parquet-lake end-to-end (write 1-day bars → reconcile → window marked) + a NEW strict per-module 100% CI gate; `tests/unit/test_dhan_ingest.py` keeps `ingest.py` at **100.00%** (NEW: empty-response-not-marked + re-pull-all-already-stored-stays-marked); the 541-test ingest/pull/dashboard slice green; `mypy --strict` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a window already in the DB is NEVER re-fetched (O(1) skip) — the conflict flood is killed; an empty/missing window is re-pulled (un-sticks NIFTY/ADANIENT/COALINDIA 1-day); 100%-gated incl. a real-lake test. 🟡 enclosure uses the dataset min/max span, so an INTERNAL gap inside an enclosed span is not detected here — the precise per-window SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED windows-ledger table (browsable on /db) is the follow-up; a legitimately-empty window (SENSEX 1-minute pre-2021-08-04) re-fetches each run (a few cheap calls) until that table marks it EMPTY-terminal. 🚫 does NOT touch the brute-force engine; does NOT change the keep-first sink or the rate limits. **Builds on:** DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger this reconciles) · DEC-LAKE-CONFLICT-KEEPFIRST-001 (keep-first makes a re-fetch safe) · DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 (#459, the in-run retry this complements) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1) skip) · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-CANDIDATE-VERDICT-001 (2026-06-04)

464. **DEC-CANDIDATE-VERDICT-001 — the Stage-3 capstone: ONE composed VALIDATED/rejected verdict per candidate, running a combo through OOS holdout + DSR + CPCV in a single call** (2026-06-04, operator: *"find the precise combo ... is it real ... no illusion ... go ahead with the plan"*). **Why:** the Stage-3 layers (#456/#458 OOS holdout + Sharpe/DD tolerance, #460 DSR, #461 CPCV, #462 `combo_returns`) each answer ONE question; nothing composed them into the single answer the operator actually wants — *is this combo real?* This is the capstone composer. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/engine/candidate.py` (pure composition, no new statistics): (a) `validate_candidate(bars, mask, sweep_results, *, direction, tf_minutes, ..., train_frac=0.7, dsr_min=0.95, cpcv_min=0.5) -> CandidateVerdict` — runs `validate_out_of_sample` (the OOS holdout) + `deflate_sweep(sweep_results).get(mask)` (the DSR, fed the leaderboard's trial population) + `cpcv_robustness(combo_returns(bars, mask, ...))` (the cross-period pass-rate), and composes them; (b) `CandidateVerdict(mask, oos, deflated_sharpe, cpcv_pass_rate, validated)` — every component carried so a REJECTION is attributable (did it fail OOS, fail the multiple-testing deflation, or fail across periods?); (c) `validated = held_up AND DSR >= dsr_min AND CPCV >= cpcv_min` — a DEFINED DSR + CPCV are required (an unprovable `None` is NOT "validated"). **Thresholds (documented, tunable):** `dsr_min = 0.95` (Bailey & López de Prado: ≥95% confidence the true Sharpe is positive after the selection-bias correction) · `cpcv_min = 0.5` (robust in a MAJORITY of the 12,870 held-out folds). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `tests/unit/test_engine_candidate.py` — the `brutex.engine` package gate reaches **100.00%** incl. `candidate.py` (260 tests across the engine suite); `_compose_verdict` is tested DIRECTLY across every branch of the three-layer AND — incl. the all-pass VALIDATED=True path — plus `validate_candidate` end-to-end on a synthetic multi-day session (orchestration + the empty-bars raise); `mypy --strict` 0; `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a candidate now gets ONE honest verdict — VALIDATED only if it clears the holdout AND the deflation AND the cross-period robustness — with the component reasons attached; 100% gated. This COMPLETES the Stage-3 composition: the engine FINDS the precise tight-SL/high-win combo and answers "is it real?" in one call. 🟡 it validates a GIVEN combo (the caller selects it on the train period + supplies the sweep's trial population for the DSR); the thresholds are the institutional defaults (tunable per run). 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds); on synthetic data the verdict is REJECTED (too few trades for CPCV) — by design, not a bug. **Builds on:** DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (#456) + DEC-OOS-LOCKBOX-TOLERANCE-001 (#458, the holdout) · DEC-DSR-SWEEP-001 (#460) · DEC-CPCV-ROBUSTNESS-001 (#461) + DEC-COMBO-RETURNS-001 (#462, the producer) · CLAUDE.md §2 · §10 · §11 COMMON · §12.

## DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (2026-06-04)

465. **DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 — the browsable per-window SUCCESS / EMPTY / FAILED status table: the precise windows-ledger the operator asked "where are the windows table db dude?"** (2026-06-04, operator: *"the successful window which is available in db table should never ever be refetched ... not started or failed window should be pulled ... how many times retry per window ... where are the windows table db dude? we need to precisely track this ... partial failed data should never ever be stored and should be marked as failed and refetched"*). **Why:** DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (#463) fixed the SKIP decision (a window the lake encloses is never re-fetched; an empty/missing one is re-pulled) but its own honest-envelope named the gap it left: the skip-ledger (`brutex.data.fetch_coverage`) is a flat *set* of completed windows — it answers "skip?" but cannot say WHY a window is or isn't done, nor track per-window attempts. The operator asked precisely for that table. This is the visibility layer: one durable, browsable row per `(market, security_id, interval, window_start, window_end)` fetch window with its status, attempt count, bars, and last error. **What shipped:** (1) NEW `brutex/data/window_status.py` — `classify_window_status(raw_bars, error_type) -> SUCCESS|EMPTY|FAILED` (pure; mirrors the #463 mark rule: error→FAILED, `raw_bars > 0`→SUCCESS, else EMPTY) + the frozen `WindowStatusRecord` + a thread-safe `WindowStatusLog` (one `threading.Lock`-guarded dict threaded into every parallel window worker; `record()` is O(1) and ACCUMULATES `attempts` across re-pulls, so a window FAILED-then-SUCCESS shows `attempts == 2` — the cross-run history the flat skip-set cannot give). (2) NEW `brutex/data/window_status_store.py` — the durable JSON sidecar at `<lake_root>/window_status.json`: degrade-to-empty load (a missing / corrupt / wrong-shaped file logs a WARNING and never raises — a lost status file costs only visibility), crash-safe atomic save (`*.tmp` + `os.replace`), and the `begin_pull_status` / `end_pull_status` dry-run rule (a dry-run records nothing; a live pull loads the persisted history then saves it back). (3) WIRED — `_ingest_one_window` records the outcome (FAILED before a retryable-error return; SUCCESS/EMPTY on the clean path, sharing the EXACT `raw_bars > 0` condition with the skip-ledger mark so the two never disagree) threaded through `ingest_spot` → `run_dhan_spot_ingest` → BOTH `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` (begin/end around the existing coverage reconcile). (4) NEW READ-ONLY `/api/v1/coverage/windows` route (FastAPI) — loads the sidecar + returns `{count, windows:[{market, symbol, interval, window_start, window_end, status, bars, attempts, last_error, last_attempt_at}]}`, empty (never a 500) when no lake root is wired or no window has been recorded. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.data.window_status` **100.00%** (58 stmts / 6 branch, `tests/unit/test_window_status.py` ×8) + `brutex.data.window_status_store` **100.00%** (36 stmts / 6 branch, `tests/unit/test_window_status_store.py` ×10), each held by a NEW strict per-module 100% CI gate; `brutex.adapters.dhan.ingest` stays **100.00%** (NEW `TestIngestSpotStatusLog` ×3: records SUCCESS on bars / EMPTY on a 0-bar response / FAILED with `last_error="DhanRateLimitError"` on a 429); `brutex.adapters.dhan.run_ingest` stays **100.00%** (NEW threading assertion: the SAME log reaches every per-pair `ingest_spot`); `brutex.dashboard.pull_controller` stays **100.00%**; NEW `TestWindowStatusApi` ×4 (empty / recorded-read-back / unwired-503 / no-lake-root) on the route; `mypy --strict` 0; `pyright` 0; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the operator's "windows table db" exists + is browsable — every ATTEMPTED window's SUCCESS/EMPTY/FAILED + attempt-count + last error is durable + visible; the status SUCCESS condition is byte-identical to the #463 skip mark, so the table never contradicts the skip decision. 🟡 it RECORDS windows the ingest ATTEMPTS — a window the #463 reconcile already encloses is skipped BEFORE the record (`_ingest_one_window` line 475, no wasted vendor hit), so its row reflects whenever it was first fetched (or is absent until first touched on a fresh sidecar); the table + the reconcile are complementary visibility/skip layers, not yet one unified store. The retry COUNT accumulates, but a per-window "mark EMPTY-terminal after N empty re-pulls" policy (so a legitimately-empty window — SENSEX 1-minute before 2021-08-04 — stops re-fetching) is the next brick this table now UNBLOCKS, not yet wired. 🚫 still NOT run on real data (lake empty — no Dhan creds); does NOT touch the brute-force engine; does NOT change the keep-first sink or the rate limits. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (#463, the skip decision this makes visible) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the flat skip-ledger this enriches) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the parallel window workers the thread-safe log serves) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1) record/lookup) · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (2026-06-04)

466. **DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 — retry a 429-failed window IN-RUN (after the backoff/step-down cooldown), fixing the 1-day window that failed every single pull** (2026-06-04, operator: *"why current day / 1-day failed every time ... even retry as well ... no illusion"* + the make-run logs: NIFTY `still_failed_windows=9 ... no_data=1`, the `interval=1day window_start=2021-01-01 window_end=2026-06-04` window stamped `error_type=DhanRateLimitError in_run_retry=False`). **Root cause (verified `ingest.py:496-533`):** every pull opens the rate controller at the full 5 r/s; a symbol's 23 windows (22× 1-minute 90-day tiles + the 1× 1-day call) fan out in PARALLEL, draining the bucket in <1 s → a 429 burst → the controller steps 5→4→3. The single cheap **1-day** call is thrown into that same storm; when it's a 429 casualty it was marked transient with `retry_window = None` (`in_run_retry=False`) — DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 DELIBERATELY excluded 429s from the in-run retry ("don't fight the limiter") and deferred them to the next pull. **But the next pull re-opens at 5 r/s and re-bursts**, so the 1-day 429s again and again — stuck at `no_data=1` FOREVER (an empty 1-day dataset, which also gates the Pre-Open report's current-day row). **What shipped (one-line behaviour reversal + tests):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py::_ingest_one_window` — a retryable 429 now sets `retry_window = window` (was `None if rate_limited`) + logs `in_run_retry=True`, so the 429 window joins the existing bounded in-run retry passes. By the time the first retry runs it has waited the seconds-scale backoff (`_default_retry_backoff`: 1 s → 2 s), the opening burst is over, the controller has STEPPED DOWN (DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001, fed by the unchanged `on_rate_limit`), and the retry is token-bucket-paced — so it WAITS the limiter out instead of fighting it. A window still failing after `max_retry_passes` stays transient + UNMARKED (the no-skip guarantee, DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 — re-pulled next run, never half-stored). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.adapters.dhan.ingest` stays **100.00%** (142 stmts / 34 branch); the locking `test_429_is_not_retried_in_run` was REWRITTEN to `test_429_is_retried_in_run` (always-429 → `retried_windows == 1`, `on_rate_limit` fires per attempt, 2 retry passes); NEW `test_429_recovers_on_retry` (`[429, 200]` → bars_appended=1, still_failed=0 — the 1-day self-heals WITHIN the run); 3 always-429 unit tests pinned to `max_retry_passes=0` (single-attempt accounting); the 53-test run_ingest/rate-control/parallel slice green; `mypy --strict` 0; `ruff` + format clean. The browsable windows table (DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001, #465) now SHOWS the self-heal: the 1-day row goes `FAILED (attempts=1, DhanRateLimitError)` → `SUCCESS (attempts=2)` in one pull. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a 429-failed window — above all the cheap 1-day call — now self-heals in-run after the cooldown, so the 1-day dataset stops failing every pull; 100% gated. 🟡 a SUSTAINED 429 storm that outlasts the retry budget (`_DEFAULT_MAX_RETRY_PASSES = 2`) still defers the stragglers to the next pull (no worse than before — un-marked, re-pulled); the deeper fix (smooth the OPENING burst so the 1-day never 429s in the first place — start below 5 r/s / sequence the 1-day before the 1-minute fan-out) is a separate queued item. Does NOT change the Rule #6 rate caps (5 r/s / 100k-day) or the token bucket — only WHICH failed windows are re-attempted in-run. 🚫 still NOT run on real data here (no Dhan creds); does NOT touch the brute-force engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 (#459, the in-run retry this AMENDS) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the step-down the cooldown leans on) · DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (#463, the no-skip guarantee for the still-failing case) · DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (#465, the table that now shows the self-heal) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-PREOPEN-CURRENTDAY-001 (2026-06-04)

467. **DEC-PREOPEN-CURRENTDAY-001 — include the CURRENT day in the Pre-Open report: anchor each IEP to the latest prior 1-day close (as-of), not the day's own 1-day bar** (2026-06-04, operator: *"why current day is not included in report generation bro ... even though we have current date data why?"* + the screenshots: the lake has ADANIENT 1-minute to `2026-06-04 15:29` yet the Pre-Open `.xlsx` stops at `2026-06-03`). **Root cause (verified `preopen_report.py:198-209` + `db_view.py:1246`):** `build_preopen_rows` anchored each day's 09:15 IEP via `_prev_trading_close`, which maps **each 1-day bar date → its predecessor's close** — so the anchor map is keyed by days that have their OWN 1-day bar. The loop then iterates the 1-**minute** dates (which include today) and does `prev_close.get(day)`; **today has a 1-minute IEP but no 1-day bar yet** (Dhan finalises the daily bar after close — compounded by the historical 1-day failures #466 fixed), so today is absent from the map → the row is dropped, EVEN THOUGH the value it needs (yesterday's official 1-day close) is in the lake. **What shipped:** NEW `brutex/dashboard/preopen_report.py::_prev_close_asof(daily, daily_dates, day)` — the NSE "previous close" computed as the latest 1-day close **strictly before** `day` (O(log N) `bisect.bisect_left` over the pre-sorted daily dates); `build_preopen_rows` now uses it instead of `_prev_trading_close`. For a day that HAS its own 1-day bar the result is byte-identical to the old predecessor-close (every historical row unchanged); for **today** (no own 1-day bar) it resolves to the prior trading day's official close, so the current-day pre-open row appears at 09:15 — exactly what a *pre-open* report is for. The first day (no earlier 1-day bar) still yields `None` → skipped, and the zero-prev-close divide-by-zero guard is unchanged. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.dashboard.preopen_report` **100.00%** (113 stmts / 24 branch) under a NEW strict per-module 100% CI gate; NEW `test_build_includes_current_day_without_its_own_1day_bar` (a `2024-03-04` IEP with NO 1-day bar of its own → one row anchored to the `2024-03-01` close — the old same-date lookup dropped it); the existing match-NSE-to-the-paisa (COALINDIA), skip-first-day, skip-zero-prev-close, out-of-range + render tests all pass UNCHANGED; `mypy --strict` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the current day now appears in the report the moment its 09:15 IEP exists, anchored to yesterday's official close — the operator's exact complaint closed; 100% gated. 🟡 on an INTERNAL 1-day gap (a missing prior daily bar) the as-of returns the most-recent AVAILABLE earlier close — a best-effort anchor that could be >1 trading day old rather than dropping the row; the 1-day series is kept complete by DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (#466) + the windows table (#465), so a gap is transient. PREV. CLOSE is the prior day's 1-day OFFICIAL close (deliberately distinct from the engine's 1-minute prev-close baseline, DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001). 🚫 does NOT touch the brute-force engine; not run on real data here (no Dhan creds). **Builds on:** DEC-PREOPEN-REPORT-001 (the report this fixes) · DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (#466, keeps the 1-day series complete) · DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (#465) · DEC-SPOT-PREVCLOSE-1MIN-001 (the distinct engine baseline) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON.

## DEC-DHAN-EASE-IN-001 (2026-06-04)

468. **DEC-DHAN-EASE-IN-001 — ease into each pull: shrink the opening token burst so the parallel fan-out stops dumping a request spike at t=0** (2026-06-04, operator: *"ultra fast extreme speed ... covering all worst cases ... no illusion"* + the chosen "smooth the opening burst" approach for the every-pull 429 storm; make-run logs: each pull opens `current_rps=5.0` → `rate.429` ×3 → `rate.stepdown` within the first second). **Part B of the operator-chosen "both"** (this PR + the companion persist-the-learned-rate-across-pulls change, the next PR). **Root cause (verified `rate_control.py` + `rate_limiter.py:228`):** the reused `AdaptiveTokenBucket` starts **FULL** (`_tokens = float(burst)`), and the controller built its bucket with `BURST = 5`. So at the very start of a pull the parallel window fan-out (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001) found 5 tokens waiting and fired **5 requests instantly** — an instantaneous rate far above Dhan's strict 5 r/s → the opening 429 burst on EVERY pull. **What shipped (one-constant change + a test):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py` — `BURST` 5 → **1**, so the bucket starts with a single token and every worker thereafter **paces from the first call** at `current_rps` (one token per `1/rps` s) instead of dumping a spike. Steady-state throughput is UNCHANGED (still `current_rps`); only the opening (and post-step-rebuild) spike is removed. A 429 that still slips through self-heals in-run (DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001, #466). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.adapters.dhan.rate_control` stays **100.00%** (65 stmts / 6 branch); NEW `test_eases_in_no_opening_burst` (with burst 1 the 2nd back-to-back `pace()` WAITS exactly `1/5 s` for a refill — paced, not a free burst; the old burst-5 bucket fired it free); the existing step-ladder / floor / recovery / `pace`-delegates tests + the 30-test rate-control/parallel gate all green; `tests/integration/test_dhan_spot_window_parallel.py`'s max-fan-out guard was TIGHTENED from `achieved_rps > 5` (which had ENCODED the old burst spike inflating a short 22-window series above the ceiling) to `achieved_rps <= 5` (the spike is gone) — a STRONGER never-exceeds-ceiling invariant; `mypy --strict` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a pull no longer fires a 5-request spike at t=0 — it paces from the first call, so the opening 429 storm is removed at the source (and any straggler self-heals via #466); 100% gated. 🟡 this is HALF the chosen "both": each pull still constructs a FRESH controller at the 5 r/s ceiling, so the first pull can still nudge the wall and a multi-symbol run re-learns per symbol — persisting the stepped-down rate across pulls so symbol 2+ START at the learned ~3 r/s is the companion change (the next PR). burst 1 trades a little cadence-jitter absorption (the bucket can no longer bank tokens to catch up after a stall) for no spike — the right trade for a strict-limit API; steady throughput is unchanged. Does NOT change the Rule #6 caps (5 r/s / 100k-day) or the step ladder. 🚫 not run on real data here (no Dhan creds); does NOT touch the brute-force engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the controller this tunes) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the fan-out whose t=0 spike this removes) · DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (#466, the self-heal for any 429 that still slips) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 (2026-06-04)

469. **DEC-DHAN-PERSIST-RATE-001 — persist the learned rate ACROSS pulls: one shared controller per dashboard session, so symbol 2+ start at the stepped-down rate instead of re-storming at 5 r/s** (2026-06-04, operator chose **"Both"** for the opening-burst smoothing → this is **Part A**, completing it after the Part B ease-in #468). **Root cause (verified `pull_controller.py`):** every `POST /universe/pull` called `_live_rate_runtime` → `_build_live_controller()`, building a **FRESH** `DhanRateController` at the 5 r/s ceiling — so each symbol-pull re-opened at 5, re-hit Dhan's wall, and re-learnt the step-down from scratch (the make-run logs show BANKNIFTY, NIFTY, SENSEX, ADANIENT each opening `current_rps=5.0` under a different `pull_id`). The rate the system LEARNED on symbol 1 (stepped to 3 r/s) was thrown away before symbol 2. **What shipped (DI, not a global — CLAUDE.md §4):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py::SessionRateController` — a thread-safe lazy holder that builds the controller ONCE (via an injectable `factory`, default `_build_live_controller`) and returns the SAME instance to every pull; `_live_rate_runtime(use_live_rate, session_rate)` resolves the controller from the holder (`session_rate.get()`) when wired, else builds fresh (back-compat for dry-run / injected-factory pulls); `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` take a `session_rate` param; `build_app` creates **ONE** `SessionRateController` per dashboard session and threads it into both pull routes. So the learned rate CARRIES OVER — symbol 2, 3, 4… start at the stepped-down ~3 r/s, not 5. Because the controller is itself thread-safe (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001), sharing it across sequential AND concurrent pulls correctly keeps the AGGREGATE issue rate ≤ 5 r/s (Rule #6) — concurrent pulls now share ONE global budget instead of each running its own 5 r/s. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.dashboard.pull_controller` stays **100.00%** (204 stmts / 34 branch); NEW `TestSessionRateController` ×2 — `get()` returns the SAME controller across calls + builds it ONCE (the persist invariant), and the default factory builds a real `DhanRateController` (cached on re-get); the 102-test dashboard/pull/ingest integration slice green (the app builds + threads the holder, dry-run pulls unaffected since they take the no-controller path); `mypy --strict` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ "Both" is now COMPLETE — Part B (#468) removed the t=0 spike WITHIN a pull, and this Part A stops every pull re-opening at 5 r/s: after symbol 1 learns the safe rate, the rest of a multi-symbol run start there, so the per-symbol 429 re-storm is gone. 100% gated on the holder + the wiring covered by the existing dry-run pull tests; the live controller RESOLUTION stays `# pragma: no cover` (as the fresh-build always was — no live Dhan in CI). 🟡 the persisted controller lives for the dashboard process (a restart re-learns from 5 r/s on the first pull — acceptable; it re-converges in ~1 s); the rate is NOT persisted to disk across restarts (in-memory by design). Does NOT change the Rule #6 caps (5 r/s / 100k-day), the step ladder, or the ease-in burst. 🚫 not run on real data here (no Dhan creds); does NOT touch the brute-force engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-EASE-IN-001 (#468, Part B — the other half of "Both") · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the controller whose learned rate this persists) · DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the thread-safe controller shared here) · DEC-DASHBOARD-PULL-ASYNC-001 (the pull routes this threads the holder through) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 · §4 (DI, no global state) · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 (2026-06-04)

470. **DEC-EMPTY-TERMINAL-001 — mark a genuinely-EMPTY window terminal after N attempts so it stops re-fetching every run** (2026-06-04, operator: *"a legitimately-empty window ... only non-successful response it should retry ... how many times retry per window ... either we can mark it as partial or complete failed"*). The follow-up the windows table (#465) explicitly UNBLOCKED — named `🟡` in BOTH DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (#463) and DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (#465): *"a per-window mark-EMPTY-terminal after N empty re-pulls policy (so a legitimately-empty window — SENSEX 1-minute before 2021-08-04 — stops re-fetching) is the next brick."* **Why:** a window that returns a CLEAN 0-bar response (genuinely no data — e.g. SENSEX has no 1-minute history before 2021-08-04) is recorded EMPTY and, by the no-skip guarantee (#463), left UN-marked → re-pulled EVERY run, costing a few wasted Dhan calls each time, forever. **What shipped (pure + wired):** NEW `brutex/dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py::reconcile_empty_terminal(coverage, status_log, *, threshold=EMPTY_TERMINAL_THRESHOLD)` — walks the per-window status log (DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001, whose `attempts` ACCUMULATE across re-pulls) and marks complete every window whose status is `EMPTY` with `attempts >= threshold` (default **3**), so the ingest's O(1) skip probe then skips it. CRITICAL safety: only a clean `EMPTY` is ever terminal — a `FAILED` window (429 / timeout / 5xx, `last_error` set) is NEVER marked even past the threshold, so a rate-limited window that happened to read 0 bars is never mistaken for genuinely-empty (it keeps retrying via DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001, #466); the rebuilt `WindowKey` matches the ingest skip probe byte-for-byte. Wired at pull start in BOTH `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles` (after `begin_pull_status`, guarded by `not dry_run and coverage is not None and status_log is not None`), so it runs ONCE per pull (O(recorded windows)), alongside the existing lake reconcile. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `brutex.dashboard.coverage_reconcile` stays **100.00%** (43 stmts / 18 branch) — NEW `TestReconcileEmptyTerminal` ×5: EMPTY at the threshold → marked + skipped, EMPTY below threshold → not marked (a few more chances), FAILED past the threshold → NEVER marked, SUCCESS → not the terminal path, custom threshold; `brutex.dashboard.pull_controller` stays **100.00%** (the wiring covered by the existing `dry_run=False` factory tests, which run the reconcile over an empty log); the 103-test reconcile/window-status/pull/dashboard slice green; `mypy --strict` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a genuinely-empty window (SENSEX 1-minute pre-2021-08-04) is now skipped after 3 confirmed empties — the last per-run waste from the #463/#465 `🟡` is closed; 100% gated incl. the FAILED-is-never-terminal safety. 🟡 "terminal" marks the window complete in the skip-ledger, so if Dhan ever BACKFILLS a window that was empty 3×, it would not be re-fetched until the ledger is rebuilt (acceptable: the empty cases here are STRUCTURAL — the instrument didn't trade at that granularity then — not pending backfills; the threshold gives a transient empty 3 chances first). The `EMPTY` vs `FAILED` distinction is exactly DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001's classifier, so a 429 is never silently terminal. 🚫 not run on real data here (no Dhan creds); does NOT touch the brute-force engine; does NOT change the rate caps or the keep-first sink. **Builds on:** DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (#465, the `attempts` this reads) · DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (#463, the same pull-start reconcile seam + the no-skip guarantee this completes) · DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (#466, why FAILED is never terminal) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger this marks) · CLAUDE.md §5 (O(1) skip) · §10 · §11 COMMON.

The live fetch stays `# pragma: no cover` (NSE bot-blocks CI). 🚫 not run against live NSE/BSE here (403); does NOT touch the brute-force engine; does NOT change Dhan/rate behaviour. **Builds on:** DEC-UNIVERSE-NSE-CONSTITUENTS-001 (#445, the mapping this extends) · DEC-CONSTITUENTS-CACHE-001 (the NIFTY 100/200/500 basket precedent) · CLAUDE.md §1 (no hallucination) · §10 · §11 DYNAMIC.

## DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (2026-06-04)

473. **DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 — wire the Stage-1B coarse pre-filter into the sweep: prune masks that fire on too few bars to ever clear the trade-count gate, BEFORE the expensive trade sim (correctness-preserving)** (2026-06-04, operator: *"go ahead with the plan"* — the next named funnel gap after DEC-SWEEP-SUBSET-001). **The gap:** the Stage-1B kernel `count_supermasks` (batched per-mask superset-hit count, Rust — DEC-RUST-SUPERMASK-KERNEL-001) was BUILT but `docs/SHARED_CORE_COMPARISON.md` §5 listed it 🔴 NOT WIRED: the sweep ran the full `simulate_trades → compute_metrics` chain on EVERY enumerated mask, including masks that fire on so few bars they can never produce enough trades to be rankable. **The insight (correctness-preserving, not a heuristic):** the trade simulator opens **at most one trade per entry signal** (verified — `trade_sim.py:367` only opens when flat, no pyramiding), so a mask's `total_trades ≤ its superset-hit count`. The first hard ranking gate rejects `total_trades < MIN_TRADES` (30). Therefore a mask whose hit-count `< 30` can NEVER be rankable, and dropping it BEFORE the sim leaves the *ranked leaderboard byte-identical* — it only skips provably-dead work. **What shipped (100%-gated):** (a) `brutex/ranking/__init__.py` — `_MIN_TRADES` promoted to PUBLIC `MIN_TRADES = 30` (the single source of truth shared by the gate AND the pre-filter, so they can never drift — CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON); `passes_gates` + `__all__` updated. (b) `brutex/engine/sweep_driver.py::sweep_masks(…, min_hits=0)` — when `min_hits > 0`, one batched `count_supermasks(bar_bits, masks)` call (built once) drops every mask with `hits < min_hits` before the per-mask sim; returns one `(mask, metrics)` pair per **surviving** mask (every mask when `min_hits == 0` — the unchanged default, so existing callers/tests are untouched). (c) threaded `min_hits` through `rank_sweep`; (d) `rank_sweep_over_bits` now defaults `min_hits=MIN_TRADES` (the operator-facing entry pre-filters by default — you want the speedup; pass `0` to force-sim every mask). `SHARED_CORE_COMPARISON.md` §5 Stage-1B row → ✅ WIRED. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** over the whole package (783 stmts / 196 branch, 284 passed); `sweep_driver.py` 67 stmts / 20 branch; `brutex.ranking` stays **100.00%** (64/12, 19 passed — the rename is safe, no test referenced the private name); NEW `TestStage1BPreFilter` ×6: zero-hit mask pruned, `min_hits=0` keeps all, **surviving masks' metrics byte-identical to unfiltered** (the prune never alters a result), `rank_sweep` threads it, **`rank_sweep_over_bits` default-prefilter leaderboard == `min_hits=0` leaderboard** (the correctness-preservation proof), `MIN_TRADES` is the shared constant; `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (179 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `vulture` clean (`MIN_TRADES` now consumed by the engine); `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the sweep now skips provably-unrankable masks before the trade sim, a real speedup on any sweep where most masks fire rarely (the common case at K≥3), with the *ranked* result mathematically unchanged (proven by the equivalence test, not asserted). 🟡 the prune is by the trade-COUNT gate only (the cheapest, exactest bound); ## DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 (2026-06-04)

474. **DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 — `brutex sweep`: the runnable top-combo finder — load lake bars → run the funnel → print the ranked condition table (print-only; persistence deferred on an honest schema fork)** (2026-06-04, operator picked the print-only CLI as the recommended last-mile after the funnel core completed). **Why this, not persistence:** the operator OK'd a `ResultsStore` persistence brick, but it has a real schema mismatch — `ResultRow` requires `avg_entry_price`/`avg_exit_price`, yet the signal-only spot sweep produces NO prices (`ClosedTrade` + `ResultMetrics` carry only int64-paisa P&L + ratios; `ResultRow` was shaped for the options/execution producer). Jamming `0.00` placeholder prices would seed the lake with misleading data (Golden Rule #1), so persistence is deferred to a deliberate schema decision and the CLI ships **print-only**. **What shipped:** (a) NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_report.py::sweep_report(bars, *, instrument, tf_label, tf_minutes, direction, condition_bits, k, …) -> str` — the PURE report core: runs `rank_sweep_over_bits` (sweep → Stage-1B prune → gates → composite rank), decodes each winning mask to its condition NAMES (`explain_combos` → `render_leaderboard`), and prepends a self-describing header (instrument / TF / direction / combo space / bars / gate-survivors). Bars in, `str` out, no I/O. (b) NEW `brutex sweep` subcommand + `cmd_sweep` handler in `brutex/cli.py` — loads the `(symbol, interval)` window from the Parquet lake via the SAME `Catalog` / `ReplayFeed` path the engine uses, then calls `sweep_report` and prints; flags for `--exchange/--segment/--interval` (lake partition labels), `--direction/--k/--conditions/--sl/--tp/--top/--min-hits`, `--catalog/--lake-root`; a no-bars window prints an honest message + exits non-zero (never a crash). `SHARED_CORE_COMPARISON.md` §5/§6 updated (CLI row → ✅ SHIPPED). **The integration test earned its keep (no illusion):** `cli.py` is coverage-OMITTED (the lake-touching layer), so a temp-lake INTEGRATION test (`tests/integration/test_cli_sweep.py`) is the honest proof — it persists bars with the real `ParquetWriter`/`ParquetBarSink`, runs `brutex sweep`, and asserts the report renders from lake-loaded bars. It **caught a real read/write-label bug**: the LAKE partition segment for an index is `INDEX` (`VALID_SEGMENTS = CASH/FNO/INDEX`), NOT the Dhan API's `IDX_I` request segment — the original `IDX_I` default would have silently loaded ZERO bars from a real lake. Fixed: the CLI default is `--segment INDEX`. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** (802 stmts / 198 branch, 289 passed) — NEW `sweep_report.py` 19 stmts / 2 branch fully covered by `TestSweepReport` ×5 (header context, the honest empty-board line, empty-bars / k-too-large / over-cap guardrails); NEW `tests/integration/test_cli_sweep.py` ×3 green (lake→report happy path, the `main(argv)` argparse+dispatch path, the no-bars user-error path); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (180 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean repo-wide. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ you can run `brutex sweep NIFTY --start 2024-01-02 --end 2024-01-03` today and get the ranked top-combo table on real lake data — the funnel is end-to-end runnable, proven against a temp lake. 🟡 print-only: the leaderboard is NOT persisted (the `ResultRow` price-schema fork above) and the CLI is coverage-omitted (proven by the integration test, not the unit gate); `--exchange/--segment/--interval` must match the lake's ingest labels (defaults: `NSE`/`INDEX`/`1minute`). 🚫 not run against a 2021→today real lake here (no Dhan creds / no ingested data — the temp-lake test is 6 synthetic bars, so the board is empty by gate discipline, not a bug); does NOT persist, does NOT touch the shared Rust core or rate behaviour. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-SUBSET-001 (#472, `rank_sweep_over_bits`) · DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (#473, the prune in the sweep) · DEC-RANKING-001 (the gates + composite the table shows) · `brutex.engine.leaderboard` (`render_leaderboard`/`explain_combos`) · `brutex.feed.replay` (`ReplayFeed` loader) · CLAUDE.md §1 · §9 · §10.

## DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001 (2026-06-04)

475. **DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001 — show net P&L, win-rate, and profit-factor on every leaderboard row, so the printed table answers the operator's actual question** (2026-06-04, operator's standing goal: *"the combo which made the massive profit + max win-rate"*). **The gap:** `render_leaderboard` (DEC-LEADERBOARD-EXPLAIN-001) printed `score / risk_eff / trades / mask / conditions` per combo — useful, but it did NOT show the two numbers the operator cares about most (profit + win-rate). The `brutex sweep` table (DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001) therefore didn't directly answer *"which combo made the most profit, with the best win-rate?"*. **What shipped (pure, 100%-gated):** `brutex/engine/leaderboard.py::render_leaderboard` now renders, per row, `pnl=<₹net P&L>  win=<win-rate %>  pf=<profit-factor>` alongside the existing `score / risk_eff / trades / mask` + the decoded condition names. Money goes through `brutex.money.format_inr` (the ₹, 2-decimal, grouped display path — DEC-MONEY-2DP-001; handles negative P&L: `₹-5,000.00`); win-rate is shown as a percentage; `profit_factor` is `Optional` (undefined when a combo had no losing trades) so it renders defensively as `n/a` in that case (gate-passing combos always have a real value). The composite-score RANKING is unchanged — the row just surfaces the headline numbers so the operator reads profit + win-rate in-line, while the leaderboard order stays the anti-overfit blended score (Golden Rule #10 — a single lucky huge-P&L combo must not dictate the ranking; DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** (805 stmts / 198 branch, 291 passed); `leaderboard.py` 26 stmts / 6 branch (the new `pf is None` branch covered both ways); NEW tests: `test_row_shows_pnl_winrate_profit_factor` (`pnl=₹12,345.67` / `win=62.5%` / `pf=2.34`) + `test_row_renders_negative_pnl_and_na_profit_factor` (`₹-5,000.00` / `pf=n/a`); the 3 `brutex sweep` integration tests still green (the header-only assertions are unaffected; the synthetic board is empty by gate discipline so no rows render); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (180 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the `brutex sweep` table now shows net P&L + win-rate + profit-factor per combo — the operator's headline question is answered in the output, money via the canonical 2dp ₹ path. 🟡 the leaderboard is still ordered by the composite anti-overfit score, NOT by raw P&L or win-rate (deliberate — a sort-by-raw-metric option is a trivial follow-up if wanted, but raw-metric ordering invites overfitting to one lucky combo). 🚫 display-only — the stored statistical metrics are untouched (never rounded; only the *display string* is formatted, DEC-MONEY-2DP-001); does NOT change the ranking, the engine, or persistence. **Builds on:** DEC-LEADERBOARD-EXPLAIN-001 (the renderer this enriches) · DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 (#474, the table this feeds) · DEC-MONEY-2DP-001 (the ₹ display path) · DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 (why ranking stays composite, not raw-P&L) · CLAUDE.md §4 · §10.

## DEC-SWEEP-SORT-001 (2026-06-04)

476. **DEC-SWEEP-SORT-001 — `brutex sweep --sort-by {composite,pnl,win,pf}`: order the gate-passing board by the operator's headline metric so the max-profit / max-win-rate combo is on top** (2026-06-04, operator's standing goal: *"the combo which made the massive profit + max win-rate"*). **Why (pivot from the price-threading brick, recorded honestly):** the previously-flagged "persistence-price" next step is plumbing for a DEFERRED feature (a large, core-`trade_sim` change for results that can't persist yet — the `ResultRow` run-id fork is still open). The operator's ACTUAL question — *which combo made the most profit / had the best win-rate?* — is answered far more directly + design-safely by letting them SORT the board by that raw metric (it pairs with DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001, which now SHOWS P&L/win-rate/PF per row). So this brick ships first. **What shipped (pure, 100%-gated):** NEW `brutex/engine/sweep_report.py::sort_ranked(ranked, by)` — re-orders the gate-passing `RankedCombo` list **descending** by one of `SORT_KEYS = ("composite", "pnl", "win", "pf")`: `composite` keeps the anti-overfit composite-score order (default), `pnl`/`win`/`pf` order by raw `net_pnl_paisa` / `win_rate` / `profit_factor`. The sort is **stable** (ties keep the incoming composite order — deterministic) and a combo with an undefined `profit_factor` (no losing trades) sorts **last** under `pf`; an unknown key raises. `sweep_report` gained a `sort_by="composite"` param (applied after the rank, before render; the header now prints `sort=<key>`), and `brutex sweep` gained `--sort-by` (argparse `choices=SORT_KEYS`, default `composite`). **The composite ranking itself is unchanged** — `pnl`/`win`/`pf` only re-order the SAME gate-survivors; the gates (≥30 trades, PF≥1.2, DD≤30%, …) still decide membership, so a single lucky huge-P&L combo can top the `pnl` view but the honest default stays the overfit-resistant composite (Golden Rule #10, DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** (817 stmts / 206 branch, 300 passed); `sweep_report.py` 31 stmts / 10 branch — NEW `TestSortRanked` ×7 (each key, `pf` None-sorts-last with both branches, stable ties, unknown-key raises, the `SORT_KEYS` constant) + `TestSweepReportSort` ×2 (header shows `sort=pnl`; unknown key propagates); the 3 `brutex sweep` integration tests updated + green (the argv path now asserts `--sort-by pnl` → `sort=pnl` reaches the report); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (180 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean repo-wide. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex sweep NIFTY … --sort-by pnl` (or `win` / `pf`) now puts the max-profit / max-win-rate / best-PF combo at the top of the table — the operator's question answered directly, opt-in. 🟡 raw-metric ordering re-introduces the single-lucky-combo bias the composite resists, so it is OPT-IN and the default stays `composite`; ordering does NOT change which combos pass the gates. 🚫 display/ordering-only — no engine, ranking-formula, persistence, or scope change; the price-threading prerequisite for lake persistence is still deferred (its run-id schema fork is unresolved). **Builds on:** DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001 (#475, the P&L/win-rate this sorts by) · DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 (#474, the CLI this extends) · DEC-RANKING-RISK-EFFICIENCY-001 (why composite stays the default) · CLAUDE.md §9 · §10.

## DEC-SWEEP-OOS-001 (2026-06-04)

477. **DEC-SWEEP-OOS-001 — `brutex sweep --oos`: append an out-of-sample (train → unseen) verdict per top combo, so the operator sees whether an edge is REAL or just overfit** (2026-06-04, operator's standing demand: *"I dont need any illusion or hallucination"*). **Why this is the no-illusion brick:** after DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001 (#475, shows P&L/win-rate) + DEC-SWEEP-SORT-001 (#476, sort by them), the operator can find the max-profit combo — but a combo that tops the in-sample board can be pure **overfitting** (the ultimate illusion of edge). The Stage-3 validator that answers "did it hold on UNSEEN data?" — `validate_out_of_sample` (DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001: build `bar_bits` once, split at an IST day boundary train 70% / test 30%, run the SAME mask on each half, verdict `held_up` = test clears the 5 gates AND Sharpe/drawdown stay within the DEC-LOCK-001 tolerances) — was BUILT + 100%-tested but **never surfaced in the sweep**. This wires it in (reuse, no new statistics). **What shipped (pure, 100%-gated):** `brutex/engine/sweep_report.py` — NEW `render_oos_verdict(oos)` (one line: `HELD ✓` / `FAILED ✗` + the three attributable components `gates`/`sharpe`/`dd` + the train/test day split + test-trade count — so a failure is explainable, not just a flag) and `oos_section(bars, ranked, …)` (runs `validate_out_of_sample` per shown combo; a window with `< 2` distinct IST trading days renders an honest `n/a` once, identical for all; an empty board renders "nothing to validate"); `sweep_report` gained `validate_oos=False` (when on, appends the section for the shown top-N), and `brutex sweep` gained `--oos`. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** (840 stmts / 212 branch, 307 passed); `sweep_report.py` 54 stmts / 16 branch — NEW `TestRenderOosVerdict` ×2 (HELD all-✓, FAILED with attributable ✗ components — covers the `_tick` both ways) + `TestOosSection` ×3 (empty board, single-day → `n/a`, **two-IST-day window renders a per-combo verdict** via a real `validate_out_of_sample` call) + `TestSweepReportOos` ×2 (`--oos` appends the section; `top_n=None` branch); the 3 `brutex sweep` integration tests updated + green (the argv path now asserts `--oos` → `Out-of-sample` reaches the report on a real lake); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (180 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean repo-wide. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `brutex sweep … --oos` now tells you, per top combo, whether its edge **HELD on unseen days** or was overfit — the single most important no-illusion signal, reusing the already-tested Stage-3 validator. 🟡 opt-in + bounded: it RE-SIMULATES each shown combo on train+test (cost ∝ `top_n`), and needs `≥ 2` IST trading days (a shorter window is an honest `n/a`); it uses the simple **train/test holdout**, not yet the full CPCV pass-rate (`brutex/engine/candidate.py` composes `cpcv_robustness` + `deflate_sweep` too — wiring that richer "this is real" score is the next robustness brick). 🚫 ordering/annotation-only — it does NOT change which combos pass the in-sample gates or the ranking; no persistence, no engine-formula change. **Builds on:** DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (the validator this surfaces) · DEC-LOCK-001 (the Sharpe/drawdown holdout tolerances) · DEC-SWEEP-SORT-001 (#476) + DEC-LEADERBOARD-PNL-001 (#475) + DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 (#474, the table/CLI this extends) · CLAUDE.md §1 (no illusion) · §10.

## DEC-SWEEP-OOS-ONLY-001 (2026-06-04)

478. **DEC-SWEEP-OOS-ONLY-001 — `brutex sweep --oos-only`: FILTER the board to combos whose edge held out-of-sample, so only the genuinely-robust combos are shown** (2026-06-04, operator's standing demand: *"no illusion or hallucination"*). **Why (the complement to #477):** DEC-SWEEP-OOS-001 (#477) *annotates* each shown combo with its out-of-sample verdict; this lets the operator go one step further — *drop* the overfit ones entirely, so `brutex sweep NIFTY --sort-by pnl --oos-only` answers the real question: *"the highest-profit combo that ALSO survived unseen data"* — the genuinely-real best combo, not a backtest mirage. Chosen over the heavier full DSR/CPCV candidate-verdict wiring (`engine/candidate.py` composes `validate_candidate` = OOS + deflated-Sharpe + CPCV, but surfacing it needs the trial-population plumbing + per-combo CPCV compute — a bigger brick flagged for next); this reuses the already-merged `validate_out_of_sample` with no new statistics + no CPCV cost. **What shipped (pure, 100%-gated):** `brutex/engine/sweep_report.py` — NEW `filter_oos_held(bars, ranked, …)` keeps only combos whose `validate_out_of_sample(...).held_up` is `True` (order-preserving; propagates the underlying `ValueError` on a `< 2`-trading-day window); `sweep_report` gained `oos_only=False` (when on, filters the sorted board BEFORE render and the header reports `oos-only=<held>/<gate survivors>`), and `brutex sweep` gained `--oos-only`. Plus a UX hardening: `cmd_sweep` now wraps `sweep_report` in `try/except ValueError` → any honest user error (over-cap sweep, bad `k`, `--oos-only` on a `< 2`-day window) prints `"[brutex] sweep error: …"` + exits non-zero, never a traceback. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** the EXACT CI engine gate `pytest --cov=brutex.engine --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_engine_*.py` stays **100.00%** (847 stmts / 214 branch, 311 passed); `sweep_report.py` 61 stmts / 18 branch — NEW `TestFilterOosHeld` ×3 (keeps-held-drops-failed via a monkeypatched validator for a DETERMINISTIC keep/drop, empty board, `< 2`-day `ValueError` propagates) + `TestSweepReportOosOnly` ×1 (the `oos-only=0/0 held` header note); the `brutex sweep` integration suite grew to **5 green** — NEW `test_sweep_oos_only_filters` (the flag → `oos-only=0/0 held` on a real lake) + `test_sweep_invalid_k_is_user_error` (the new graceful `try/except` → exit 1 + `sweep error`, no traceback); `mypy --strict brutex` 0 (180 files); `pyright` 0; `interrogate` 100%; `ruff` + format clean repo-wide. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `--oos-only` shows ONLY combos that survived out-of-sample — overfit in-sample winners are dropped, so the board is the genuinely-robust set; the CLI now degrades every sweep-time user error to a clear message, not a stack trace. 🟡 it re-simulates each gate-survivor on train+test (cost ∝ #survivors, more than the `--oos` top-N annotation), needs `≥ 2` IST trading days, and uses the simple train/test holdout — NOT the stronger DSR (multiple-testing) / CPCV robustness, whose wiring (`validate_candidate` + the trial-population plumbing) is the next brick. 🚫 filter/annotation-only — it does NOT change the in-sample gates or the ranking formula; no persistence, no engine change. **Builds on:** DEC-SWEEP-OOS-001 (#477, the verdict this filters by) · DEC-OOS-VALIDATION-001 (the `validate_out_of_sample` it reuses) · DEC-SWEEP-SORT-001 (#476) · DEC-SWEEP-CLI-001 (#474) · CLAUDE.md §1 · §10.

## DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 (2026-06-05)

479. **DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 — `make run` / `bootstrap.sh` now build the `trading_core` Rust wheel, fixing `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'trading_core'` on a clean clone** (2026-06-05, operator-reported: `make run` crashed at `brutex/indicators/fib_levels.py:68` → `import trading_core`). **Root cause:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 Phase 2b (#441) repointed BruteX's 52-condition vocabulary + evaluate-time indicators at the shared `rust/trading-core/` PyO3 crate, so three modules now import it at module top (`brutex/indicators/fib_levels.py:68`, `brutex/indicators/pivots.py:46`, `brutex/vocabulary/evaluator.py:28`). The build automation, however, only ever built the OTHER kernel (`fno_math`) — `make run`, `scripts/setup/bootstrap.sh`, and `scripts/run/preflight.sh` were never updated to build `trading_core`. Net effect: on any clean checkout the whole engine + dashboard import chain dies the moment `brutex.engine` is touched (the traceback the operator hit). **What shipped (build-tooling only — no `brutex/` source touched):** (a) `Makefile` `run` target gains a second maturin block — `import trading_core` probe → `cd rust/trading-core && maturin develop --release` if absent — mirroring the existing `fno_math` block exactly (same idempotent guard, same `VIRTUAL_ENV`/`PATH` wiring); (b) `scripts/setup/bootstrap.sh` gains Step 6/7 "build + install trading_core" (renumbered 6→7 steps, doctor now 7/7); (c) `scripts/run/preflight.sh` cargo message now reads "builds fno_math + trading_core kernels". This follows the repo's established convention that the Rust kernels are **build prerequisites** (bare `import fno_math` / `import trading_core` at module top, no soft-import guard — combo.py:64 is the precedent), so the fix is to BUILD the wheel, not to guard the import. **Regression test (bug-class guard):** NEW `tests/unit/test_run_builds_rust_kernels.py` encodes the violated invariant DYNAMICALLY (CLAUDE.md §11) — it DISCOVERS every maturin crate under `rust/*/pyproject.toml` (`fno_math` + `trading_core` today), asserts each is imported at module top by `brutex/`, then asserts BOTH `make run` AND `bootstrap.sh` build it. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix `Makefile` (`assert 'import trading_core' in makefile` → AssertionError — exactly the reported crash) and PASS after, so the same bug cannot recur for this kernel or any future PyO3 crate (7 tests, green). **Verified:** `rust/trading-core` `maturin develop --release` compiles + builds the wheel cleanly (release profile, ~17s); the only env-specific note is that the crate is `abi3-py312` (`requires-python >=3.12`), so the wheel installs on the operator's Python 3.12.13 (the `make run` env) — a Python 3.11 box rejects it by design. `bash -n` clean on both scripts; the Makefile/script diffs are mechanical mirrors of the proven `fno_math` path. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `make run` now builds BOTH kernels on a clean clone, so the `trading_core` import resolves and the engine/dashboard boot — the exact crash the operator reported is fixed at its three import sites, and a regression test mechanically prevents recurrence. 🟡 build-tooling + its guard test — the `Makefile` + `*.sh` source surface is not itself in the `brutex/` coverage gate; the fix was additionally validated by an actual `maturin develop --release` build + `bash -n`. 🚫 does NOT touch any `brutex/` source, the shared Rust core's logic, CI workflows, or the 400-case golden contract; it only wires the already-existing crate into the turnkey build path. **Builds on:** DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (#441, the crate this builds) · DEC-ONECLICK-RUN-001 / DEC-CLONE-RUN-002 (the `make run` turnkey path) · DEC-RUN-PREFLIGHT-001 (the preflight surface) · DEC-INFRA-OPS-001 (#244, `bootstrap.sh`) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON (one source of truth — no recipe copy-paste; the trading_core block mirrors fno_math).

## DEC-RUN-NUMPY-CORE-001 (2026-06-05)

480. **DEC-RUN-NUMPY-CORE-001 — `numpy` moved from the `[dev]` extra to core `dependencies`, fixing the SECOND `make run` crash (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy'`) surfaced once #479 unblocked the import chain** (2026-06-05, found by the operator-requested LIVE `make run` verification). **Root cause:** with DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 (#479) fixing the `trading_core` import, the engine import chain (`cli.build_parser` → `engine.sweep_report` → `engine.leaderboard` → `ranking` → `metrics.cascade`) now reaches `brutex/metrics/cascade.py:87`, which does `import numpy as np` UNCONDITIONALLY at module top (same for `metrics/spa.py:98`, `monte_carlo.py:48`, `lockbox.py:61`). A clean `make run` installs `.[data,ui]`, NOT `[dev]`, so `python -m brutex …` crashed on numpy. (The operator's own Mac escaped it only because a prior `.[dev]` install had left numpy present.) **What shipped (dependency metadata only — no `brutex/` source touched):** (a) `pyproject.toml` — `numpy>=1.26,<3.0` added to core `[project.dependencies]` (it is runtime, not dev tooling); (b) the duplicate `numpy` line removed from `[dev]` (core deps are always installed, so dev inherits it — no duplication, CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON). **Regression test:** NEW `tests/unit/test_make_run_runtime_deps.py` (3 tests) — parses `pyproject.toml`, asserts the `make run` install set (core deps + `data` + `ui` extras) contains `numpy`, asserts numpy is specifically in core `dependencies` (metrics is core, not behind an extra), and grounds the assumption by asserting `make run` really installs `.[data,ui]`. Verified to FAIL against the pre-fix pyproject (numpy dev-only → 2 failures) and PASS after. **Live verification (the operator's "make run live" ask):** built BOTH kernels into a fresh Python 3.12.3 venv via maturin, `pip install -e ".[data,ui]"`, then `python -m brutex run --no-browser` — the dashboard booted (`Application startup complete`, Uvicorn on 127.0.0.1:9080) and served the full index over HTTP 200 (214 KB). The only runtime warning is `instrument_master.autoload_skipped HTTP 403` — the sandbox network policy blocks the Dhan scrip-master CSV; the app degrades gracefully (autopull disabled, no crash) rather than failing, exactly as designed. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ `make run` now boots end-to-end on a clean clone (both #479 + this fix) — verified live, not on paper. 🟡 dependency-metadata + its guard test only; no source/logic change; the live boot ran without Dhan creds so the lake is empty (the 403 is expected, not a defect). 🚫 does NOT touch any `brutex/` source, the Rust cores, CI workflows, or the golden contract. **Builds on:** DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 (#479, the fix that surfaced this) · DEC-P0-020 (#42, where numpy was originally added to `[dev]`) · DEC-ONECLICK-RUN-001 / DEC-CLONE-RUN-002 (the `make run` turnkey path) · CLAUDE.md §11 COMMON.

## DEC-RUN-SMOKE-GATE-001 (2026-06-05)

481. **DEC-RUN-SMOKE-GATE-001 — new CI hard gate `make run smoke (cold-start boot)`: actually run `make run` from a clean clone and boot the app, so "100% green but the app won't start" can never recur** (2026-06-05, operator: *"everytime you are telling me this is fixed but error everytime ... why everytime it is a big struggle"*). **Root cause of the struggle (the honest structural gap):** EVERY existing CI job installs `.[dev,data,ui]` AND `pip install ./rust/{fno-math,trading-core}` — i.e. CI hand-installs everything `make run` builds itself. So the cold-start `make run` path (operator's real flow: `.[data,ui]` ONLY + `maturin develop` the kernels) was **never executed by the machine**. Two real crashes shipped behind "100% green" because of this blind spot: `trading_core` not built (DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 / #479) and `numpy` declared `[dev]`-only (DEC-RUN-NUMPY-CORE-001 / #480) — both invisible to every green gate, both only surfacing when a human ran `make run`. **What shipped:** NEW `run-smoke` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that reproduces the operator environment EXACTLY — `pip install -e ".[data,ui]"` (NO `[dev]`, so numpy-class bugs surface), build BOTH kernels, then four escalating smokes: (1) `import trading_core, fno_math`; (2) `import brutex.indicators.fib_levels` + `brutex.engine` (the exact chains that crashed); (3) `python -m brutex --help` (the `cli.py:329` parser build); (4) **boot** `brutex run --no-browser` and assert it serves **HTTP 200** (>1000 bytes) on `127.0.0.1:9080`, failing fast if the server process dies. Wired into `ci-ok.needs` + the aggregate echo + the pass/fail loop, so it is a **HARD merge-blocking gate**. Added to the branch-protection drift snapshot (`branch-protection-drift.yml` expected set) and the operator runbook (`docs/runbooks/github-branch-protection-setup.md`) as a required check. **Verified (locally, faithful py3.12.3 + cargo):** every smoke step was run by hand before wiring — kernels import, `fib_levels`/`engine` import, `brutex --help` renders the subcommand list, and `brutex run --no-browser` booted (`Application startup complete`, Uvicorn on :9080) and served the 214 KB index over HTTP 200; the only runtime line is the Dhan scrip-master CSV HTTP 403 (sandbox network policy — the app degrades gracefully, autopull disabled, no crash). `ci.yml` validated as well-formed YAML. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ from now on a broken cold-start `make run` is a RED required gate — the machine catches it, not the operator; both #479 + #480 would have been caught by this job. 🟡 the boot smoke runs WITHOUT Dhan creds, so it proves the app STARTS + serves the dashboard, not that ingest works (the 403 is expected); it does not exercise real data flow. 🚫 CI-config + docs only — no `brutex/` source, Rust, or golden-contract change. **Builds on:** DEC-RUN-TRADING-CORE-BUILD-001 (#479) + DEC-RUN-NUMPY-CORE-001 (#480, the two bugs this would have caught) · DEC-ONECLICK-RUN-001 / DEC-CLONE-RUN-002 (the `make run` path) · DEC-P0-005 (the branch-protection / Z+ PREVENT layer this extends) · CLAUDE.md §10 (honest limits) · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-DRIFT-YAML-FIX-001 (2026-06-05)

482. **DEC-DRIFT-YAML-FIX-001 — fix the permanently-red `branch-protection-drift` workflow: its issue-body heredocs were column-0 inside a `run: |` block (spec-invalid YAML → startup_failure on every run)** (2026-06-05, found while diagnosing the operator's "the drift detector is red" concern). **Root cause (evidence-based, no guessing):** the `Open drift-alert issue` step built the GitHub issue body with `--body "$(cat <<EOF … EOF)"` where the heredoc body lines start at **column 0**. A YAML `|` block scalar ends at the first non-empty line indented LESS than the block (here 10 spaces); a column-0 line therefore TERMINATES the scalar and the parser then chokes on `**Drift…` as a stray node. Result: GitHub cannot instantiate the workflow → every trigger is a **`startup_failure`** with 0 jobs (confirmed via `actions_get`: run #789 `conclusion=failure`, `run_started_at==updated_at`, `total_jobs=0`). So the detector that is supposed to alarm when the merge-guarantee weakens has **never actually run** — a silent hole in the Z+ PREVENT layer. **What shipped:** rewrote the step to build the body with indented `printf … > drift-body.md` + `gh issue … --body-file` (every line properly inside the `run:` block — no column-0 heredoc), preserving the exact issue/comment content. `git`-side env (`SERVER_URL`/`REPO`/`RUN_ID`) hoisted to `env:` for clean quoting. **Verified:** `python3 -c "yaml.safe_load(...)"` now PARSES the file (it raised `expected alphabetic or numeric character, but found '*'` at the old heredoc line before the fix); a column-0-line scan of the file is clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the workflow is now valid YAML, so on its next schedule/dispatch it will actually RUN the drift check (parse → compare → alert) instead of startup-failing. 🟡 I could NOT end-to-end-confirm from this session: dispatching the workflow returned `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, and reading live branch protection needs an **admin** token I don't have — so whether the live `main` rule currently matches the snapshot is still an OPERATOR check (the workflow will now report it instead of silently dying). 🚫 CI-workflow + ledger only — no `brutex/` source, no required-gate change; does NOT itself apply or alter the server-side branch-protection rule (operator-only). **Builds on:** DEC-P0-005 (the Z+ PREVENT / branch-protection layer) · DEC-RUN-SMOKE-GATE-001 (#481, same workflow's expected-check snapshot) · CLAUDE.md §10 (honest limits).

## DEC-ACTIONLINT-GATE-001 (2026-06-05)

483. **DEC-ACTIONLINT-GATE-001 — add `actionlint` as a HARD `ci-ok` gate so broken workflow YAML can never silently startup-fail again** (2026-06-05, C3 of the operator's strict-hardening sweep; direct follow-up to DEC-DRIFT-YAML-FIX-001). **Why:** the drift detector rotted red for ~789 runs because a column-0 heredoc made its YAML spec-invalid — and NOTHING caught it, because no gate lints the workflow files themselves. `actionlint` validates workflow syntax, `${{ }}` expressions, globs, event names, and action refs — exactly that bug class. **What shipped:** new `actionlint` job in `ci.yml` (downloads actionlint **1.7.7** pinned by SHA256 `023070a2…0757`, verified via `sha256sum -c` before exec — no `curl|bash`), wired into `ci-ok.needs` + the result-loop so it BLOCKS merges. **Scope honesty (Golden Rule #10):** runs `-shellcheck= -pyflakes=` (CORE checks only) — embedded shellcheck/pyflakes are DEFERRED to **DEC-ACTIONLINT-SHELLCHECK-001** (tracked follow-up) to avoid a pre-existing-warning flood across the 2500-line `ci.yml` that would make the gate un-green-able in one PR. **Verified:** ran actionlint 1.7.7 locally over all 12 workflows → **0 core problems** (per-file confirmed), so the gate is green on merge and protective immediately; `yaml.safe_load` parses the edited `ci.yml`. **Out of scope:** shellcheck-on-workflows (next PR); no `brutex/` source touched. **Builds on:** DEC-DRIFT-YAML-FIX-001 (#482) · DEC-P0-005 (the gate-integrity layer).

## DEC-DEFINITION-OF-READY-001 (2026-06-05)

484. **DEC-DEFINITION-OF-READY-001 — the PLAN-FIRST gate: no PR is accepted until its body enumerates every scenario + failure mode + a real-run proof + a rollback + what's out of scope** (2026-06-05, operator decree: *"until or unless thoroughly designing / deriving an extensive plan by covering everything we should never ever go ahead with implementation"*). **Why:** the repo had a Definition of DONE (the ci-ok merge gates) but no Definition of READY — so the failure the operator fears most ("a situation/functionality nobody thought to cover") had no gate, because you cannot test a scenario you never imagined. **What shipped:** (1) `scripts/ci/definition-of-ready-guard.sh` — fail-closed PR-body guard requiring 5 section markers (`Scenarios covered` / `Failure modes` / `Real-run proof` / `Rollback plan` / `Out of scope`), mirroring `zplus-pr-guard.sh` (bot-exempt for renovate/dependabot per DEC-P0-058; `OPERATOR_OVERRIDE`+reason → audit-logged to `pre-merge-overrides.log`); (2) `tests/redteam/test_redteam_definition_of_ready_guard.py` — 12 cases asserting fail-closed + override-audit + bot-exempt (all green); (3) `docs/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md` — the gate spec; (4) the 5-section block added to `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; (5) a `definition-of-ready` CI job (gated on `pull_request`), **wired into `ci-ok.needs` as a HARD gate** (no other PR was open at ship time, so no in-flight work is retroactively blocked). **Honest boundary (Golden Rule #10):** the gate guarantees the **existence + completeness** of a plan, NOT its **correctness** — no machine can grade whether the author imagined the *right* scenarios. This is not a zero-bug promise; it is a promise that nothing is built blind. **Rollout:** hard now because the only open PR is the one introducing it (dogfooded — this PR's body carries the 5 sections); flip to advisory = remove the one `ci-ok.needs` line. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-014 (zplus-pr-guard pattern) · DEC-MERGE-GUARANTEE-001 (the Definition of Done it complements) · DEC-ACTIONLINT-GATE-001 (#483, shipped together).

## DEC-DASHBOARD-CONSTITUENTS-CACHE-TICK-001 (2026-06-05)

486. **DEC-DASHBOARD-CONSTITUENTS-CACHE-TICK-001 — fix: "⊕ tick its constituents" silently ticked NOTHING + showed red on a CACHE hit** (2026-06-05, operator-reported from a live `make run` — the red "…ticked — from cache…" line on `/universe`). **Root cause (frontend/backend contract mismatch):** `GET /api/v1/universe/index-constituents` returns valid `members` for BOTH `source:"nse"` (fresh fetch) and `source:"cache"` (served from a prior fetch — the NORMAL path on the operator's machine, where NSE is network-blocked so the live fetch fails and the cache serves), and even pre-builds a `note` that says "…ticked — from cache (fetched <date>; pass refresh=true…)" (`app.py:949-951`). But the JS guard `if (source !== "nse" || !members.length)` (`universe.html:735`) treated `"cache"` like an error: it returned early WITHOUT ticking and rendered that "ticked" note in the **error-red** class (`toggle("err", source !== "nse")`). So the message literally said "ticked" while nothing got ticked, in red. **Fix:** tick whenever `members.length && (source==="nse"||source==="cache")`; only `"unavailable"`/`"unknown-index"` are errors (red); the success path uses the backend `note` (already correct per source). **Hardening:** backend cache path already covered by `test_second_call_serves_from_cache_even_when_live_fetch_breaks`; the JS is client-side (not TestClient-executable) — verified by logic + CI boot-smoke + operator visual. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ logic fix is certain; 🟡 the *visual* on the live page needs the operator's eyes (this CI env is Python 3.11, cannot render). **Builds on:** DEC-CONSTITUENTS-CACHE-001 (#445/#457).
