## DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 (2026-06-08)

585. **DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 — the expired-option `OptionParquetWriter` gets a per-PARTITION write lock + an `os.fsync` before the atomic rename, so its merge-on-write is correct on its OWN (no longer safe only by the coarse `OptionBarSink` audit lock) and a crash can't leave a truncated partition** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #10 B-2). **Problem (code-traced):** `option_parquet_writer.py` `_merge_partition` did a read→`pl.concat`/`unique`→`os.replace` read-modify-write with **NO per-partition lock** — unlike the spot `ParquetWriter` (`parquet_writer.py:102-117`) which interns a `threading.Lock` per destination PATH (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001) — and its `_atomic_write_parquet` did `df.write_parquet(tmp)`→`os.replace` with **NO `os.fsync`** (vs the spot writer's `_atomic_write` at `parquet_writer.py:535`). The option write was therefore safe ONLY by the coarse process-wide `OptionBarSink._lock` (DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001) that also serialises the audit-chain append — i.e. correctness was borrowed from a lock whose real job is the single-writer audit chain, and that global lock kills ALL option-write parallelism. Two writers to the SAME `options/<series>/<YYYY>-<MM>.parquet` (a 30-day option pull straddles a month boundary, so two windows of one series share a month partition) would race a lost-update: both read the old file, each unions only its own bars, the later `os.replace` wins and silently drops the other's bars. **Fix (mirror the spot writer, belt-and-braces):** (1) a process-wide `_PARTITION_LOCKS: dict[Path, threading.Lock]` + `_PARTITION_LOCKS_GUARD` + `_partition_lock(dest)` — interned lazily, keyed by resolved PATH (not writer instance, so one-writer-per-worker fan-out still shares the file's lock), O(1) get-or-create under the guard, the guard held ONLY for the dict op never across the write; `_merge_partition`'s existence-check→read→union→atomic-rename now runs `with _partition_lock(dest)`, so same-file writers serialise while different partitions never contend (parallelism preserved). The union is order-independent (keyed by `(side, timestamp)`), so the stored bytes are identical regardless of which window lands first (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 7). (2) `_atomic_write_parquet` now `os.open(tmp, O_RDONLY)`→`os.fsync`→`os.close` BEFORE `os.replace`, so the tmp's data is on stable storage before the rename publishes it (a crash between rename and the OS flushing the page cache can no longer surface a zero-length/truncated parquet — `os.replace` orders metadata, not data; `polars` owns the write so the fd is re-opened read-only purely to fsync, which Linux permits). This makes the writer correct independently so the option write can later be lifted out from under the global sink lock without a lost-update race. **O(1) discipline (CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5):** the lock lookup is an O(1) dict get-or-create; per-bar work is unchanged (O(1) amortised union); the fsync is one syscall per flush, not per bar. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** `pytest --cov=brutex.data.option_parquet_writer --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=100 tests/unit/test_option_parquet_writer.py` = **100.00%** (98 stmts / 18 branch, 17 passed) — NEW `TestPartitionLock` ×3 mirroring the spot writer: `test_same_path_returns_same_lock` (interning), `test_different_paths_get_distinct_locks` (no false contention), and `test_concurrent_same_partition_writes_lose_no_bars` (16-thread `threading.Barrier`, all 16 distinct-minute bars survive the merge → no lost update); the existing money-rounding / idempotent-repull / partial-merge / month-split / atomic-cleanup / path-safety cases unchanged; `ruff` check + format clean, `mypy --strict` clean on the module. This is the exact CI strict-100% gate at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1274`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the writer is now correct on its own (per-partition lock) AND crash-durable (fsync) — matching the spot writer; ✅ option-write parallelism is now SAFE at the writer layer (the global sink lock can be narrowed in a follow-up — NOT done here, out of scope). 🟡 the lock is in-PROCESS only (one host) — a multi-process pull would still need OS-level file locking (no such pull exists; the ingest is multi-thread, single-process per DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001); cross-RUN vendor-drift on the same `(side, ts)` is still keep-first (existing behaviour, a tracked follow-up). 🚫 no change to the merge semantics, the schema, the 2dp money rounding, or the `OptionBarSink` audit lock. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-WINDOWS-001 (the spot per-partition lock this mirrors), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the coarse audit lock this de-couples correctness from), DEC-EXPIRED-OPTIONS-TABLE-001 (the option table), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1)) · Rule 7 (idempotence/order-independence) · §4 (no-look-ahead n/a; atomic-durable write) · §13 (merge-readiness: correctness > reliability > performance).

## DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 (2026-06-08)

586. **DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 — add operator-configurable SPKI (SubjectPublicKeyInfo SHA-256) TLS public-key pinning to the Dhan production transport, with a SAFE opt-in fallback, a security-specific terminal error, and a never-silent audit+alert on mismatch** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #9 E-1: `brutex/adapters/dhan/client.py` wired `urllib_transport` = default `urllib.request.urlopen`, which validates the `api.dhan.co` server certificate against the **system CA store ONLY**. A CA compromise / mis-issuance / corporate-proxy MITM presenting a *validly chained* cert for `api.dhan.co` would be accepted → the 24h bearer access-token JWT + every fetched bar would flow to the attacker). **Fix (defence-in-depth, second independent check ON TOP of CA validation):** new pure module `brutex/adapters/dhan/cert_pinning.py` (`DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001`): (1) `spki_sha256_pin(cert_der)` = `base64(SHA-256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo))` — the standard HPKP / mobile-pinning pin, computed by a minimal, self-contained DER walk (`_extract_spki_der`: Certificate→tbsCertificate→skip optional `[0]` version + the 5 RFC-5280 fields → SubjectPublicKeyInfo), so NO new runtime dependency and every malformed-input branch is testable; (2) `PinPolicy` (frozen, injectable) resolved from env via `from_env` — `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PINS` (comma/whitespace pin set, optional `sha256/` prefix) + `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PIN_DISABLE` (explicit break-glass opt-out); (3) `PinPolicy.verify(cert_der, host)` decision table — **opt-out** → WARNING + return; **no pins configured** → DEBUG + return (the SAFE fallback to system-CA validation, so a missing config NEVER breaks a live pull); **enforced + key matches any configured pin** (current+next ⇒ rotation-survivable) → DEBUG + return; **enforced + MISMATCH or absent/empty peer cert** → emit the CRITICAL `dhan.tls.pin_mismatch` audit line + fire the injected `alert` hook + raise the security-specific `DhanCertPinError` — **NEVER a silent fall-back** (a mismatch is treated as an active MITM, not a soft warning). `DhanCertPinError` is deliberately NOT in `is_retryable`, so an attacker-presented cert is never fast-retried/re-queued. **Wiring:** `client.make_pinning_transport(policy)` runs the request over `http.client` (returns status+body for 2xx AND 4xx/5xx like the old shim), extracts `getpeercert(binary_form=True)` and calls `policy.verify` BEFORE sending the token-bearing request (a MITM never even receives the JWT); `client.default_dhan_transport()` is the COMMON single wiring point (`make_pinning_transport(PinPolicy.from_env())`) now used by all 3 production builders (`cli.py` `_build_live_pull_adapter`, `pull_controller.py` `_build_live_pull_adapter` + `_start_token_keepalive`). With no pins configured this is byte-equivalent in behaviour to the prior `urllib_transport` wiring. **NO hardcoded pin** for `api.dhan.co` (a baked-in pin would brick every operator on Dhan's next key rotation, and Golden Rule #1 forbids unverifiable embedded facts) — pins are operator-supplied; a pin is a PUBLIC key hash, not a secret, so it is safe to log/echo (unlike the token). **O(1):** the pin check is O(1) per connection (one SHA-256 over the fixed-size SPKI + a frozenset membership test) — handshake-time, NOT a per-bar hot path; no O(1)-total claim. **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** new `tests/unit/test_dhan_cert_pinning.py` (32 cases) + `test_dhan_client.py` factory tests → `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.cert_pinning --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.client --cov-branch` = **100.00% line+branch on BOTH** (cert_pinning 108 stmts/34 branch, client 151 stmts/22 branch, 0 miss); covers pin-MATCH, pin-MISMATCH (audit+alert+raise), ROTATION (multi-pin), missing-config fallback, explicit opt-out (all truthy/falsy spellings), absent/empty peer cert, and every malformed-DER branch — the real-cert SPKI cross-checked against `cryptography`'s `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` bytes (importorskip, NOT a runtime dep). `ruff` + `ruff format` + `mypy --strict` + `pyright` + `bandit` (No issues identified) all clean; `semgrep` rule-registry fetch is blocked by this environment's network policy (HTTP 403) — bandit is the security gate that ran. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ when an operator configures `BRUTEX_DHAN_TLS_PINS`, a CA-compromise/MITM with a non-pinned key is REFUSED + audited + alerted before the token is sent. 🟡 pinning is **opt-in** — out of the box (no pins) the behaviour is unchanged (system-CA validation only); the operator must obtain + configure the real `api.dhan.co` SPKI pin(s) to enforce (the `pins_from_certs` helper derives them from trusted material). The `alert` hook defaults to a no-op; the always-on CRITICAL `dhan.tls.pin_mismatch` structlog line is the audit+alert surface (consistent with the `rate.breach` pattern), and production wiring can inject a Telegram bridge later. 🚫 no change to the request shape, rate gating, retry budget, credentials store, or any non-production transport. **Builds on:** the SSRF `_guard_url` (https + host allow-list, unchanged), DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-GET-001 (the GET/POST verbs the pinning transport preserves), DEC-CREDENTIALS-STORE-001 (the env-config pattern `from_env` mirrors), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no hallucination — no baked pin) · Rule 5 (O(1) handshake check) · §11 COMMON (one wiring point) · Golden Rule #10 (honest opt-in envelope).

## DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 (2026-06-08)

587. **DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 — rolling, NSE-calendar-anchored walk-forward mode for the brute-force engine (train 90d / test 5d / shift 1w), each combo scored per held-out fold then aggregated, so a seasonal overfit no longer hides in a single OOS block** (2026-06-08, closes audit Gap #4 — "only a single OOS split exists; rolling walk-forward is not implemented, so seasonal overfits (earnings, index reconstitution) slip through"). (1) The **substantive** guarantee is the build-once-then-slice causality — each bar's truth-vector reads only bars `<= N`, so a later fold's test window can never inform an earlier one; this is *proved* by a counterfactual property test (perturbing bars after a fold's `test_end_bar` leaves that fold's metrics byte-identical). (2) The named **P-06 `LookAheadBarrier`** (`brutex/feed/lookahead.py`) is reused as a belt-and-suspenders runtime guard in two places: `verify_walk_forward_no_lookahead` re-asserts the *schedule* keeps every training window before its test window (a structural regression guard — robustly maps a malformed hand-built schedule to `passed=False`, never an uncaught `ValueError`), and `_assert_trades_confined` drives the barrier over each fold's *realized test trades* to prove none escapes its window and that they are chronologically ordered (a genuine guard on the scoring OUTPUT); both fail-closed with `LookAheadError`. **4-agent hostile review (CLAUDE.md §9) ran on the diff** — architecture/causality · duplication/COMMON · correctness/edge-cases · test-adequacy/mutation — in the project venv (Python 3.12 + maturin `fno_math`/`trading_core` `--release`). the schedule hash now binds `n_bars` + `n_trading_days` (closing a length-aliasing gap) and the "iff collide" wording was corrected to assume BLAKE3 collision-resistance; the malformed-schedule `ValueError`-leak was fixed to `passed=False`; the aggregation layer gained direct `_aggregate_folds` unit tests (exact pass-rate, distinct-Sharpe min/mean, the `0.6` threshold boundary, all-`None` Sharpe) and the leaky-schedule fixture was tightened to a 1-bar leak — killing the surviving min→max / sum→max / threshold / barrier-cursor off-by-one mutants the review surfaced. **Tests (5 of 7 types — unit / property / golden / integration + the strict per-module self-test):** `tests/unit/test_engine_walk_forward.py`, `tests/property/test_engine_walk_forward_properties.py` (folds partition the range with no overlap/leak; ## DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (2026-06-08)

588. **DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 — per-`(symbol, window)` retry-storm give-up guard + once-per-symbol 100%-window-failure Telegram alert + hash-chained give-up/alert audit rows (closes audit Gap #3)** (2026-06-08). Entry numbered **588** (next free integer after #587 DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001; renumbered from #585 on the repeated append collision with main's #585 DEC-OPTION-PARTITION-LOCK-001 / #586 DEC-DHAN-TLS-SPKI-PIN-001 / #587 DEC-WALK-FORWARD-OOS-001 — the decision ID, not the integer, is authoritative). **Problem:** a multi-hour continuous-429 storm across the parallel window fan-out (e.g. 100 symbols × 15 windows) loses bars *silently* until the run ends — `orchestrator/watchdog.py` (the heartbeat `Watchdog`, DEC-WATCHDOG-001) is a hung-worker detector, NOT a per-tuple give-up guard, so a window that keeps failing under the storm has no bounded "stop trying + tell the operator + record it" verdict; the only recovery was the operator hand-diffing the audit chain after the fact. **Fix (scope-locked to watchdog / notifications / cli flag wiring + tests):** new `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py::RetryStormWatchdog` — a pure, no-thread, O(1)-per-tuple policy oracle poked by the caller. `record_failure(symbol, window)` times the *continuous-failure streak* per tuple against an injected monotonic clock and gives up the instant the streak reaches `max_retry_seconds`; `record_terminal_failure` is the immediate-give-up fast path for an already-exhausted window (the ingest progress stream's `failed=True`); `record_success` resets the streak. Each give-up marks the tuple terminally given-up (idempotent), stamps a hash-chained `RETRY_GIVE_UP` audit row via an injected `AuditSink` (`AuditWriter`-shaped), and counts toward its symbol; when a symbol reaches 100% window-failure it stamps one `SYMBOL_WINDOW_FAILURE` row and fires the operator alert **exactly once per symbol — never per window** (`== total` fires once, no unreachable double-alert branch). A failing audit write / buggy callback is swallowed + logged (Golden Rule #10) — the guard never crashes the ingest. `brutex/notifications/`: new `TelegramEventKind.SYMBOL_WINDOW_FAILURE` + `SweepAlerter.symbol_window_failure` / `symbol_failure_callback` (kept wheel-free via a structural `SymbolFailureLike` — no orchestrator import, so the strict per-module gate stays green). `brutex/cli.py`: `brutex fetch --max-retry-minutes N` flag (validated `>= 1`) → `_arm_retry_storm_guard` builds the guard (audit writer under `<lake>/audit/retry-storm-<pull_id>.jsonl`, `SweepAlerter` alert callback), registers the `(symbol_name, interval)` fan-out, and feeds the existing `run_ingest` `on_progress` stream into it (no `run_ingest` change). **Verified (project venv, py3.12):** new `tests/unit/test_orchestrator_retry_storm_watchdog.py` + `tests/property/test_retry_storm_watchdog_props.py` + `tests/integration/test_retry_storm_watchdog_integration.py` + the `--max-retry-minutes` CLI tests + the `sweep_alerts` symbol-failure tests — give-up fires **exactly at the boundary** (and not one tick below), the alert fires **once per symbol not per window** (hypothesis property over random fan-outs), and give-up + alert audit rows are written and the real hash chain **verifies** (`verify_chain`); `brutex/orchestrator/watchdog.py` + `brutex/notifications/sweep_alerts.py` at **100% line + branch**; `ruff` + format + `mypy --strict` clean on the touched files. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the give-up guard, the once-per-symbol alert, and the hash-chained audit rows are fully implemented + tested; the live `fetch --max-retry-minutes` path drives the per-symbol 100%-window-failure **alert + audit** end-to-end via the `on_progress` terminal-failure feed. 🟡 the engine's real fan-out unit is `(instrument, interval)`, so "window" = that fan-out unit (not a date sub-chunk); the **time-based** per-attempt give-up (`record_failure` streak ≥ N min) needs the ingest retry loop to poke the guard on **each** attempt — that one-call adoption lives in the ingest spine (`ingest_spot`/`auto_retry`) and is intentionally **out of this PR's file scope** (the guard is complete + tested, ready to wire). 🚫 no change to `mutation.yml`, coverage config, `rust/`, or the dhan option path (L1-owned). **Builds on:** DEC-WATCHDOG-001 (the heartbeat `Watchdog` this complements), DEC-TELEGRAM-WIRE-001 (the `SweepAlerter` seam extended here), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#571, the bounded-retry residual this turns from silent into audited), NFR-OBS-003 (the hash-chained `AuditWriter`), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) per-tuple) · Rule 8 (audit trail) · Rule 10 (honest envelope) · §11 AUTOMATED (watchdog + Telegram).

## DEC-ORCH-LAZY-BLOOM-001 (2026-06-08)

589. **DEC-ORCH-LAZY-BLOOM-001 — `brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py` imports `fastbloom_rs` LAZILY (on first `BloomFilter` construction), unblocking the standalone strict per-module 100%-coverage gate for the `brutex.orchestrator.*` modules** (2026-06-08, gap-sweep #12/#13). **Problem:** the strict per-module coverage gate (`ci.yml`, DEC-COV-001 ratchet) runs `pytest --cov=brutex.orchestrator.<mod> …` per module. For the orchestrator submodules this aborted at COLLECTION with `ImportError: PyO3 modules compiled for CPython 3.8 or older may only be initialized once per interpreter process` — the `fastbloom_rs` wheel is built `cp37-abi3`, and `coverage`'s source-package import of `brutex.orchestrator.<mod>` (which pulls the package `__init__` → `pipeline` → `store` → `bloom` → top-level `from fastbloom_rs import BloomFilter`) collided with the coverage machinery's own import, so PyO3's abi3≤3.8 single-init rule fired. The global `--cov=brutex` run was unaffected (one import), which is why these modules were covered at 100% via the aggregate but had their *standalone* strict gates commented out (`orchestrator.replay`) or never added (`orchestrator.retry` and the rest). **Fix:** `bloom.py` now defers the `fastbloom_rs` import to a one-line lazy loader `_load_rust_bloom()` called inside `BloomFilter.__post_init__` — mirroring the EXISTING lazy `fno_math` import in `_popcount_bytes`. Importing the orchestrator package no longer initialises the PyO3 extension, so the per-module coverage gate imports cleanly; the very first `BloomFilter()` still triggers exactly one init (behaviour byte-identical). The `_RustBloomFilter` type name moves under `TYPE_CHECKING` (annotations are strings via `from __future__ import annotations`), and the loader returns `cast("type[_RustBloomFilter]", …)` since `fastbloom_rs` ships no stubs. **Re-enabled gates:** `ci.yml` strict per-module 100% line+branch gates ADDED/re-enabled for `brutex.orchestrator.{replay, retry, audit, adaptive_rate_limiter}` — the four modules that reach 100% standalone with their dedicated test files (verified locally, Python 3.12). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the ABI3 import blocker is RESOLVED for ALL `brutex.orchestrator.*` modules (the import-time init is gone). 🟡 only the four named modules are gated NOW — `state` (98.6%), `store` (91.3%), `pipeline` (97.3%), `rate_limiter` (86.6%), `quota_tracker` (92.6%) and `bloom` (96.8%) carry RESIDUAL standalone-coverage gaps (lines exercised only by the aggregate `--cov=brutex` run / cross-module integration tests), a DISTINCT concern from the (now-fixed) import blocker — tracked as the next ratchet. 🚫 no runtime behaviour change; `mypy --strict` + `ruff` clean on `bloom.py`. **Verified:** `pytest --cov=brutex.orchestrator.{replay,retry,audit,adaptive_rate_limiter} --cov-branch --cov-fail-under=100` = 100.00% each (standalone). **Builds on:** DEC-COV-001 / DEC-L3-REPLAY-ORACLE-001 #241 (the deferred replay gate), DEC-COV-BACKFILL-LIMIT-001 #261 (the operator-accepted ABI3 limit this lifts), CLAUDE.md §4 (no-look-ahead lazy-import precedent) · §11 COMMON.

Folding them in (pragma sweep + a few more unit tests) is the tracked next ratchet. 🟡 DISCOVERED, not introduced: `tests/property/test_ranking_overfit_properties.py::test_dsr_monotone_in_observed_sharpe` is an over-strong property — the PSR/DSR is genuinely NON-monotone in observed Sharpe at large-negative Sharpe with a non-trivial deflation benchmark (the estimator-variance radicand grows faster than the numerator), so hypothesis can falsify it; a domain-restriction fix is a tracked follow-up (it does not affect this PR's unit-only gate). 🚫 `mutation.yml` is weekly / main-push only (not a per-PR `CI OK` gate), so this change is exercised by the weekly run, not this PR's CI. **Verified:** `mutmut run --paths-to-mutate brutex/metrics/deflated_sharpe.py` (unit-only runner) → 0 survivors; `ruff` + `mypy --strict` clean. **Builds on:** DEC-P0-001/002/003 (the mutmut 85% gate lineage), CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 12 (mutation ≥ 85%) · §4 (no-pandas/typed) · §10 (honest limits).

(2) `fno-math/fuzz/fuzz_supermask` over `count_supermask_u64s` / `count_supermasks_u64s`: asserts the SUPERSET count is bounded by `n_bars`, `mask==0` matches all, and the batch kernel equals the single kernel element-wise + positionally — **3,627,225 runs, 0 crashes**; (3) `trading-core/fuzz/fuzz_pivot_fib` over `compute_pivot_levels` + `compute_fib_levels`: asserts no panic + the documented monotone ladder (`R4≥R3≥PDH`, `S4≤S3≤PDL`, `PDL≤P≤PDH`, `range≥0`, midpoint in band) — **31,164,014 runs, 0 crashes**; (4) `trading-core/fuzz/fuzz_evaluator` over `evaluate_atoms`: asserts no panic, only bits 0..=51 set (reserved 52-63 always clear), and every mutually-exclusive condition pair (above/below the same level, bullish/bearish, gap-up/gap-down, inside/outside day, upper/lower third, ≤1 time-of-day bucket) — **7,719,702 runs, 0 crashes**. **Honest domain (Golden Rule #10, matching `trading-core/src/lib.rs`):** the `trading-core` fuzzers stay inside the DOCUMENTED realistic envelope — prices capped at `MAX_PAISA`=₹100,000,000 (far below the `~10¹⁷`-paisa overflow bound), OHLC ordered, `PDH≥PDL`, `PDC∈[PDL,PDH]`, proximity bps `∈[0,10000]` — because the crate INTENTIONALLY panics on corrupt OHLC (always-on `assert!`, mirrors Python `ValueError`) and on absurd `i64`-scale magnitudes (release `overflow-checks`); 582. **DEC-INGEST-AUDIT-CHAIN-001 — wire the hash-chained AuditWriter into the spot ingest pull (Golden Rule #8)** (2026-06-08; closes the #1 finding of the deep data/reliability gap sweep — "spot ingest writes NO hash-chained audit"). **Gap (verified):** `brutex/adapters/dhan/run_ingest.py` + the `brutex fetch` CLI path emitted only `structlog` lines — `grep AuditWriter run_ingest.py` = 0 — so a spot data pull (a "material action" per CLAUDE.md Golden Rule #8) left NO hash-chained JSONL audit row, and the audit-replay oracle could not verify a pull. **What shipped (core capability, 100% line+branch under the EXISTING strict `--cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.run_ingest --cov-fail-under=100` ci.yml gate):** an optional injected `audit: AuditWriter | None = None` on `run_dhan_spot_ingest` + the `run_dhan_spot_ingest_with_retry` wrapper (default `None` = unchanged, so all 23 prior tests + every other caller are byte-identical). When wired, a new pure `_maybe_audit` helper appends a hash-chained trail — `INGEST_RUN_START` (worklist shape) → one `INGEST_PAIR_DONE` (bars/windows/still-failed) per succeeded pair OR one `INGEST_PAIR_FAILED` (error + `auth_failure`/`known_gap` classification) per quarantined pair → `INGEST_RUN_COMPLETE` (pairs ok/failed, total bars, auth_aborted). **Thread-safety (the key design constraint):** every append fires ONLY on the single controller thread that drains the parallel fan-out (`run_ingest.py` "single-threaded… need not be thread-safe"), so the not-thread-safe `AuditWriter` is never touched concurrently by the worker pool — no lock needed, no corruption possible. **Production activation:** `brutex fetch` (`cli.py:cmd_fetch`) now opens an `AuditWriter` at `<lake>/audit/spot-ingest.jsonl` (resume = append to the existing chain across runs) for LIVE pulls and threads it in; `--inspect`/`--dry-run` get a null context (no real data → no audit). 587. **DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 — PROVE the residual-B2 worst case is real: a Sharpe-only early-stop kill drops non-Sharpe top-K rankers (the leaderboard changes)** (2026-06-08; the honest conclusion of the Lane-G B2 investigation after DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 / PR #515). **TEST-ONLY — the early_stop module stays INERT.** **What shipped:** `tests/integration/test_stage2_5_b2_residual.py` — an adversarial counterpart to the benign A/B oracle. 588. **DEC-SPRT-INFEASIBLE-001 — feasibility review verdict: a provably leaderboard-preserving Stage-2.5 SPRT early-stop is INFEASIBLE; ABANDON it as a sweep accelerator and redirect to the exact Stage-1B prefilter + the bit-exact GPU path** (2026-06-08; the honest conclusion of Lane G after DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 proved the Sharpe-only kill unsafe). **Question investigated:** can the kill be made "composite-aware" to fix B2? **Verdict (structural, not a kill-statistic choice):** NO. (1) **No sound mid-flight bound for the non-Sharpe terms** — the leaderboard ranks on 8 full-backtest aggregates (`ranking/__init__.py:301-318`); `max_drawdown_pct` (`compute.py:262-307`), Calmar, and Risk-Efficiency (`ranking/__init__.py:165-177`) can be dominated by trades that have not happened at the 50-trade kill point, so none admits a sound bound from a prefix; the only mid-flight signal is the probabilistic PSR on Sharpe, already disproven (#587). (2) **The score is relative/pool-coupled** — z-scored across SURVIVORS (`ranking/__init__.py:180-193,285-291`) + DSR-deflated against pool `N`/`V` (`overfit.py:204-242`); pruning ANY combo perturbs every survivor's z-score AND the DSR bar; the only perturbation-free normalization (compute over the FULL pool) needs each killed combo's TRUE final metrics = the exact backtest early-stop exists to skip (closed circle). So a composite-aware kill is either UNSAFE (probabilistic) or NON-ACCELERATING (exact) — no safe-and-fast middle. This mirrors the only prune already proven safe: the EXACT Stage-1B `min_hits` prefilter (`sweep_driver.py:264-272`), safe precisely because it is exact not probabilistic. **Decision:** Stage-2.5 SPRT early-stop is **ABANDONED** as an accelerator (not merely blocked); **B4-wiring + B5 are CLOSED** (nothing safe to wire); the merged inert core (#511) + A/B oracle (#585/#515) + residual-B2 proof (#587/#516) STAY as documented building blocks + guardrails (not wired, must not be). **Redirect (leaderboard-safe, already in tree):** (a) the exact Stage-1B coarse prefilter (DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001) — the correct exact shape of the SPRT idea; (b) Phase-3.5 Metal GPU offload (`TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §3`, bit-exact parity + audit-replay gated). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the "~61% reduction / single overnight" SLA built on Stage-2.5 (`TRACK1_OPTIMIZATIONS.md §1`) is NOT safely achievable and is RETIRED; the achievable leaderboard-safe speedup is Stage-1B + the bit-exact GPU path. **What shipped:** ADR-0006 "FINAL VERDICT" section + a 🚫 ABANDONED banner on `TRACK1_BACKTEST_SPEC.md` §"Stage 2.5". **Scope:** docs only; the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE is UNCHANGED. **Builds on:** DEC-SPRT-B2-RESIDUAL-001 (#587), DEC-SPRT-AB-ORACLE-001 (#586), DEC-SPRT-EARLY-STOP-CORE-001 (#585), DEC-SPRT-SPEC-RECONCILE-001 (#584), DEC-SPRT-DESIGN-BLOCK-001 (#583), DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (the safe exact prefilter), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #9 / #10.
589. **DEC-STAGE1B-CONFLICT-FIX-001 — fix a leaderboard-corruption bug in the Stage-1B conflict prune (it WRONGLY pruned bullish/bearish-doji masks) + add 4 verified candle conflicts + prove the prune is EXACT** (2026-06-08; the operator-chosen "Lane A — safe Stage-1B speedup". While tightening the exact prefilter, a correctness bug was found). **Bug (verified, not theoretical):** `brutex/vocabulary/conflicts.py` `CONFLICT_PAIRS` listed `(BIT_BAR_BULLISH, BIT_BAR_DOJI)` and `(BIT_BAR_BEARISH, BIT_BAR_DOJI)` as conflicts — but the shared evaluator defines **DOJI as a SMALL body** (`body*10 < total_range`, `rust/trading-core/src/evaluator.rs:239`), NOT `open==close`. So a bar with a tiny POSITIVE body is **both BULLISH and DOJI** (tiny negative → BEARISH+DOJI). Empirically ~**9% of random bars** are bullish/bearish dojis (1871/1897 of 20k). The Stage-1B prefilter (`sweep_run.py:676` `has_conflict`) therefore **WRONGLY dropped every mask requiring (bullish AND doji) / (bearish AND doji)** — strategies that CAN fire + rank — silently corrupting the leaderboard (the exact failure class the SPRT lane was abandoned to avoid). **Fix:** REMOVED the two false pairs (a tiny-bodied directional bar is genuinely both). **Tightening (the safe speedup):** ADDED 4 UNCONDITIONAL candle conflicts, each provable from the evaluator's body/range + wick/range bounds (`evaluator.rs:233-256`) AND verified to never co-occur across 20k random bars: `(DOJI, LARGE_BODY)` (body/range <0.1 ⊥ >0.7), `(LONG_UPPER_WICK, LONG_LOWER_WICK)` (upper+body+lower==range ⇒ two halves can't both exceed range/2), `(LARGE_BODY, LONG_UPPER_WICK)`, `(LARGE_BODY, LONG_LOWER_WICK)` (a >0.7 body leaves <0.3 for either wick). Net CONFLICT_PAIRS: 24 − 2 + 4 = **26**. **New proof test (the real assurance):** `tests/property/test_conflict_pairs_exact.py` drives the REAL `evaluate_atoms` over 600 randomized realistic bars and asserts the load-bearing invariant `has_conflict(evaluate_atoms(bar)) is False` ∀ bars — i.e. NO conflict pair is ever co-set on a real bar ⟺ pruning conflict-masks can never drop a fireable mask ⟺ the Stage-1B prune is **EXACT (leaderboard-preserving)**. This test would have CAUGHT the bullish-doji bug (a real bar sets both → fails) and now regression-guards both the removed pairs (must co-occur) and the added pairs (must never). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** net mask-count effect is roughly neutral (un-prune 2 false / prune 4 new); the WIN is CORRECTNESS (the leaderboard no longer silently loses bullish/bearish-doji strategies) plus a slightly tighter exact prune. The degenerate zero-range bar/day edge (which can trip the pre-existing `(at_day_high, at_day_low)` pair) is out of scope (real bars have range >= 1 tick). **Verified locally:** 128 tests pass incl. the 400-case vocab golden (evaluator unchanged) + the sweep goldens (conflict_pruned counts unchanged for their fixtures); ruff + mypy clean. **Scope:** the EVALUATOR + the 52-condition golden are UNCHANGED — only the mask-generation prune set + a new test. **Builds on:** DEC-STAGE1B-WIRE-001 (the prefilter), DEC-SHARED-CORE-001 (the authoritative evaluator semantics), the SPRT-abandon redirect (DEC-SPRT-INFEASIBLE-001, which pointed here as the safe exact speedup), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #4 / #10.

The `AuditWriter` is **flush-per-entry** (every row persists without an explicit close), and the sink's existing single write-lock keeps the hash chain single-writer (no concurrency issue under the parallel option fan-out). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the change is the LIVE wiring only — `_build_live_options` is `# pragma: no cover` (needs real Dhan creds + network), consistent with the spot CLI wiring; the audit-WRITE core it activates is already 100%-tested. 592. **DEC-O1-BENCH-GAPS-001 — close the 3 un-benched O(1) hot-path gaps with isolated ratio gates: Bloom probe, BLAKE3 combo-hash, raw Parquet lake-write (G1 of the 4-gap audit)** (2026-06-08; the follow-on after DEC-DOC-STANDARDS-RECONCILE-001 / PR #528). **Gap:** the O(1) audit agent found that of the five Golden-Rule-#5 hot paths, three had NO dedicated bench: (a) the **Bloom probe** `BloomFilter.might_contain` was only exercised inside the composite option-dedup gate, never alone (`brutex/orchestrator/bloom.py:346`); (b) the **BLAKE3 combo-hash** `combo_hash`→`fno_math.blake3_hash` (`brutex/strategies/combo.py:91,180`) was architecturally O(1) per fixed-size identity but unbenched; (c) the **raw Parquet lake-write** `ParquetWriter.write` (`brutex/data/parquet_writer.py:224`) had only the in-memory results-store append gated, not the real file write. All three were YELLOW ("plausible, not proven"). **What shipped:** three new bench modules under `tests/bench/`, each a ratio gate routed through the existing two-tier `_o1_tiers.ratio_ceiling` (robust shared-CI ceiling, decreed 1.1× on the M4-Pro strict tier): `test_bloom_o1.py` (probe latency independent of inserts, 100k vs 1k, < 5×), `test_blake3_combo_hash_o1.py` (per-call latency independent of call count — guards against accidental growing state, 100k vs 1k, < 5×), `test_parquet_write_o1.py` (fresh-write latency independent of existing partition count, 500 vs 50, < 8×; each write targets a unique symbol → a new partition file, isolating the create-write from any merge). **Real-run proof (local .venv):** all 10 tests pass in ~10s; measured ratios Bloom 1.03×, hash ~1.0×, write ~1.0× — all far under their ceilings, and an O(n) regression (scan-on-probe / growing hash state / lake-scan-on-write) would blow the ratio and fail the gate. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** this does NOT force the decreed strict 1.1× on shared CI (that stays M4-Pro-tier only, per DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 / DEC-P0-020 shared-runner flake reality) — it converts three previously-unbenched O(1) claims into machine-checked regression gates at the same noise-tolerant ceilings the existing O(1) benches use. Test-only; no `brutex/` runtime code changed; CI scopes mypy to `brutex/` and jscpd to `brutex/`, so the new test modules add gates without touching either. **Builds on:** the 4-agent audit (this session), DEC-O1-STRICT-TIER-001 (the `_o1_tiers` two-tier helper), `test_lmdb_membership_o1.py` / `test_option_dedup_o1.py` (the sibling O(1) gates this mirrors), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #4 (reproducibility) / #5 (O(1) discipline) / #10 (honest limits).
592. **DEC-OPTION-429-RECOVERY-001 — make the rolling-option series ingest TRANSACTIONAL (resume-cursor in-run retry + commit-all-or-nothing) so a 429 mid-pagination never leaves a page-holed partition (closes audit Gap #2)** (2026-06-08; the option-path parity for the spot in-run 429 retry DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 + the `until_clean` recovery #571). **Gap (verified in code):** `ingest_rolling_option_series` (`brutex/adapters/dhan/option_ingest.py`) tiled a series into 30-day windows (the "cursors" of a multi-page option chain) and, on a RETRYABLE error (429 / 5xx / timeout), **DEFERRED** that cursor to the next pull (`continue`) while still fetching + WRITING the later cursors (the old `option_ingest.py:288-297` "a failed window is DEFERRED, NOT retried in-run as the spot path does"). So a 429 landing mid-pagination left the lake partition with a HOLE — a missing page between written pages. Keep-first dedup (`data/option_sink.py` + `data/option_dedup.py`) collapses a duplicate timestamp on a re-pull but can NEVER fill a missing page, so the partition could sit PARTIAL until a manual re-run (the audit's Gap #2). The spot path already had BOTH the in-run per-window 429 retry (DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 / `ingest.py`) AND the outer `until_clean` round loop (`until_clean.py`); the option path had neither. **What shipped (1 source file — `option_ingest.py`):** the series ingest is now **transactional** with two mechanisms: (1) **resume-cursor in-run retry** — a retryable cursor is re-fetched IN-RUN after a bounded seconds-scale exponential backoff (`_default_retry_backoff`, 1 s→2 s→…→8 s ceiling), up to `max_retry_passes` (default **2**) EXTRA attempts, paced by the SAME `≤ 5 r/s` bucket (Rule #6) so the retry waits the limiter out (mirrors the spot 429-retry rationale: the opening burst is over + the governor has stepped down by then); (2) **commit-all-or-nothing** — every cursor's session-filtered bars are STAGED in a phase-1 buffer and the sink is written + coverage marked only in a phase-2 COMMIT pass that runs AFTER every cursor has been fetched cleanly. If a cursor outruns its retry budget (or a TERMINAL error raises mid-fetch), the whole series ABORTS having committed NOTHING — the partition stays EMPTY and the un-committed windows are deferred to the next pull (coverage untouched ⇒ a re-pull re-fetches them). So the lake partition for a series is always WHOLE or ABSENT, **never a page-holed partial**. New `OptionIngestReport` fields `retried_windows` + `still_failed_windows` (mirroring the spot `IngestReport`) + a `complete` property (`still_failed_windows == 0`). The rate-feedback routing (429→`on_rate_limit`, 5xx/timeout→`on_timeout`, clean→`on_success`; DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001) is preserved per attempt. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** the staging buffer is **O(session-bars in the series) SPACE, NOT O(1)** — an all-or-nothing commit cannot be O(1) space without a sink-side rollback (out of this path's scope); the O(1) guarantees that DO hold are per-bar (the coverage probe, the dedup probe, the coverage-key build). The retry COUNT is bounded by `max_retry_passes` (never infinite) and every fetch is paced ≤ 5 r/s; a terminal / token-death error is non-retryable and raises straight out (quarantined upstream, partition empty). Behaviour change vs the old spine: a transient cursor now ABORTS the series (commit nothing) instead of deferring just that one window with the others written — that is the whole point (no more partial partitions). **Tests (100% line+branch on `option_ingest.py` — 110 stmts / 24 branch / 0 miss, verified locally in a 3.12 venv with the `fno_math`+`trading_core` kernels built):** `tests/unit/test_dhan_option_ingest.py` — the resume-heals-on-retry (partition COMPLETE), permanent-429-leaves-EMPTY (NOT even the already-fetched cursor 0 committed), abort-does-not-mark-coverage, complete-marks-every-window-in-one-commit, backoff-zero-based-indices, terminal-mid-series-commits-nothing, + the updated transient/feedback-routing cases (now assert clean abort, `sink.batches == []`) + the bounded-exponential backoff math (worst-case clamp, no real sleep via injected hook); a NEW property test `tests/property/test_dhan_option_429_recovery_properties.py` drives randomized chain length × failing-cursor position × heal-vs-permanent × retry budget and asserts the load-bearing invariant `committed_windows ∈ {0, N}` (never 1…N−1) ∧ `complete ⇔ failing cursor recovers within budget`; a NEW integration test `tests/integration/test_dhan_option_429_recovery.py` proves the guarantee against the REAL lake-write stack (real `OptionBarSink` + `OptionDedupIndex` + recording partition writer + a real hash-chained `AuditWriter`): a resumed 429 commits the whole partition with one audit row per window and `verify_chain` passes, a permanent 429 leaves ZERO writes / ZERO audit rows and the chain still verifies. Existing `test_dhan_option_universe_ingest` / `_parallel_wiring` / `option_pull_controller` / audit-chain tests pass unchanged (the universe fan-out calls the series spine with the defaults; its terminal-quarantine + success paths are unaffected). **Scope:** the Dhan option ingest path only — the BRUTE-FORCE ENGINE, the option sink/writer/dedup, and the spot path are UNCHANGED; `option_universe_ingest` / `option_pull_controller` signatures are untouched (the resume-cursor guard is fully contained in the series spine, default-on). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 / DEC-DHAN-WINDOW-RETRY-001 (the spot in-run retry this brings to options), DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 (#571) + `until_clean` (the outer round-loop recovery), DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger now advanced all-or-nothing), DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001 (#494, the per-attempt rate feedback), DEC-DHAN-PARALLEL-INGEST-001 (the single-writer sink the integration test exercises), CLAUDE.md Golden Rules #1 / #7 / #8 / #10 / #11.

## DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (2026-06-08)

592. **DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 — make the 12h `TokenKeepalive` the SINGLE token renewer (renews ONLY when <12h, learning expiry OFFLINE from the JWT `exp`), and DELETE the ungated per-pull `RenewToken` that rotated + then lost a healthy live token** (2026-06-08, operator: *"why always this renew token is hitting even in that case [>12h] ... it is wiping the current active token and trying to fetch the stale token ... one and only when the current active token is less than 12 hours alone right then this renew token should hit"*). Entry numbered **592** (renumbered 587→592 on the MIGRATION append collision with main's #587–#591; the decision ID is authoritative). **Root cause (two coupled defects, code-traced — distinct from #583 which only fixed reading the rotated `token` key):** (a) `pull_controller.py::_maybe_renew_adapter_token` fired a `RenewToken` at the START OF EVERY live pull / repull / retry (call sites `pull_all_spot` + `pull_candles`), with **NO <12h gate** — exactly the operator's "why is it always hitting" complaint. `RenewToken` **ROTATES** (mints a new token and INVALIDATES the presented one — DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 #583), so firing it on a healthy >12h token needlessly killed it. (b) On success the helper wrote the new token into `replace(adapter.client, access_token=...)` — but the live client reads its token from the shared `TokenHolder` via `token_provider` (`client.py:_headers`: `token_provider() if token_provider is not None else access_token`), so the rebuilt `access_token` field is **IGNORED** and the holder was **never updated**. Net effect: the pull kept reading the **just-invalidated** token from the holder → `HTTP 400 DH-906 "Invalid Token"` → the loud `auth_expired` verdict, on a token that was **never actually expired**. (The 11:37 full pull succeeded because the per-pull `RenewToken` was *refused* that time, a no-op; the 13:15 "Retry failed windows" *succeeded* at rotating and self-destructed the live token.) The correct renewer already existed: the background `TokenKeepalive` renews ONLY at the 12h half-life AND writes the fresh token into the holder the client reads. **What shipped:** (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_keepalive.py` — NEW pure `decode_jwt_expiry(token)`: reads the access-token JWT's standard `exp` claim (RFC 7519, base64url middle segment) **offline, with no network and no rotation**, so a freshly-pasted >12h token triggers **ZERO** `RenewToken` calls until it is genuinely inside the 12h window; returns `None` on ANY untrusted shape (not a 3-segment JWT / bad base64url / non-JSON / non-object claims / missing-or-non-numeric `exp`, `bool` rejected though it subclasses `int`) so a non-JWT token degrades to the prior learn-by-renew path — never a crash, never a guess. `_tick` now LEARNS expiry from the JWT on the first tick instead of an immediate rotating `RenewToken`; only a token actually <12h is renewed. (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — DELETE `_maybe_renew_adapter_token` + both call sites + the now-unused `replace` import; a breadcrumb comment at each former call site records WHY no per-pull renew exists. The keepalive is the sole renewer. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all four changed files; the FULL `pytest`/`mypy --strict`/`pyright`/strict-100%-coverage gate is enforced by CI (the dev container is Python 3.11 without the runtime deps, so the suite runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, NOT fabricated here). NEW tests: `TestDecodeJwtExpiry` ×9 (every decode branch) + `TestTick` ×2 (first-tick JWT >12h ⇒ 0 RenewToken calls, token untouched, `auth.keepalive.expiry_learned` logged; <12h ⇒ renews); the obsolete `TestMaybeRenewAdapterToken` removed with the helper. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ RenewToken now fires ONLY when the active token is genuinely <12h — never on a normal pull/repull/retry — and when it does fire (the keepalive) the fresh token propagates through the holder the client reads. 🟡 the keepalive keeps a token alive only while the PROCESS runs AND the first token is an ACTIVE web-generated JWT; a non-JWT/TOTP-minted or `exp`-less token degrades to one learn-by-renew at startup (best-effort, not a crash). The per-pull Telegram `auth_renew_failed` alert is removed with the per-pull renew; the keepalive still logs `auth.renew_failed`. 🚫 no change to the rate caps, ingest spine, or engine. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 · DEC-DHAN-AUTH-FAILFAST-RENEW-001 · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 · §6 · §10 · §11 COMMON.

## DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (2026-06-08)

593. **DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 — make the one-click "Pull spot" DRIVE ITSELF to a clean lake: turn the (already-built, already-100%-tested) re-pull-until-clean loop ON by default in the dashboard pull route** (2026-06-08, operator: *"once you finish the entire chunks then at last automatically retry until it fetched all the windows ... until every window gets finished this process should be repeated ... that too until or unless our quota is not yet exceeded ... until everything is clean it should always pull/retry, automated"*). Entry numbered **593** (renumbered 588→593 on the append collision; the decision ID is authoritative). **Root cause (capability existed but wired OFF):** `until_clean.run_until_clean` loops bounded re-pull rounds until `stop_clean` (every window fetched) / `stop_quota` (daily 100k Dhan quota spent) / `stop_dead` (token died) / `stop_no_progress` / budget, reusing the shared coverage ledger so each round re-fetches ONLY still-failed windows, rate-safe (DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001; `until_clean.py` is 100% line+branch + property + stress + O(1) bench tested). But `pull_all_spot(auto_retry=False, until_clean=False)` defaults it OFF, and the dashboard's main `POST /api/v1/universe/pull` route (`app.py::api_universe_pull._work`) passed NEITHER flag — so the one-click "Pull spot" ran a **single pass**, left whatever a transient 429/timeout storm failed (the operator's 125 residual windows), and STOPPED with the "⏳ Re-pull to finish" banner, requiring a MANUAL "Retry failed windows" click (which then independently died on the token-rotation bug fixed by DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 #592). The failures were never auto-retried-to-completion — not "tried and failed", but "never auto-tried". **What shipped (one wiring change):** `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — the main pull route's background `_work` now calls `pull_all_spot(..., auto_retry=True, until_clean=True)`, engaging `run_until_clean` with the persisted-quota hook (`_rate_controller.quota_exhausted`) + `stop_when_stuck=True` over the bounded `AUTO_RESUME_MAX_ROUNDS` (50) budget. The one-click pull now self-drives to a clean lake — zero manual "Re-pull" clicks (CLAUDE.md §11 AUTOMATED) — and stops cleanly on quota (resume after the IST-midnight reset) or token-death (re-auth), never an infinite or quota-burning loop. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** the changed `_work` route body is `# pragma: no cover — runs on the job thread` (the underlying `pull_all_spot(until_clean=True)` path, `run_until_clean`, the quota hook, and the no-progress guard are each already 100% line+branch covered by `tests/unit/test_dhan_until_clean.py` + `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` + `tests/property/test_until_clean_properties.py` + `tests/stress/test_until_clean_stress.py` + `tests/bench/test_dhan_until_clean_o1.py`); no route test pins the prior single-pass kwargs. `ruff` + `ruff format --check` clean; the full gate runs on CI. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the one-click pull retries every failed window automatically until the lake is clean OR the daily quota is spent, with the 50-round bound + the no-progress guard + the quota brake making it safe. 🟡 each round is O(failed_windows), NOT O(1)-total — a sustained throttle still costs wall-time; the loop pauses (not fails) on quota and resumes after IST midnight. This complements DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#588), which audits/alerts a per-symbol 100%-failure storm. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the ingest spine, or the engine; the `/retry-failed` button + its `?until_clean=` escalation are unchanged. **Builds on:** DEC-AUTO-RESUME-QUOTA-001 · DEC-INGEST-AUTO-RETRY-001 · DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (#592) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 · DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#588) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 6 · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 (2026-06-08)

594. **DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-SINGLE-SOURCE-001 — one durable source of truth for the live access token: a write-through `TokenHolder` so a mid-session credential SAVE and a keepalive RENEW both keep the persisted store + the in-memory holder in sync — fixing `auth_expired` on a freshly-saved valid token** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run` with a brand-new token: `auth.keepalive.expiry_learned remaining_hours=20.93 … no RenewToken fired` (proving DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 #592 works) yet the pull still `universe.pull_all.preflight_refused … verdict=auth_expired`; operator: *"why the fuck it failed again even with the new access token … better to have the db for this access token and always keep the latest token and have only one unique active token which is active and whenever even it gets renewed also it should be the updated one"*). **Root cause (code-traced, two divergent stores — the same token_provider/holder family as #592 but a different gap):** the live token lives in TWO places that drifted apart: the persisted `~/.brutex/credentials.json` (0600) and the in-memory `TokenHolder` every live `DhanClient` reads through `token_provider=holder.get`. (a) **Save gap:** `app.py::api_credentials_set` wrote the FILE (`save_dhan_credentials`) but NEVER updated the in-memory holder — which was seeded ONCE at startup. So saving a new token mid-session had ZERO effect on the running pull: it kept reading the stale startup token (already invalidated by a prior session's RenewToken rotation) → `DH-906` → `auth_expired`, even though the just-pasted token was valid (JWT `exp` ~21h out, decoded + confirmed). The only workaround was a full app restart (which re-seeds the holder from the file). (b) **Renew gap (latent):** the keepalive's `RenewToken` ROTATES (the new token invalidates the old), and `_renew_once` wrote the rotated token to the holder but NOT back to the file — so after any renewal the FILE held the now-DEAD pre-rotation token, and a restart re-loaded a dead token. **What shipped (the operator's "single latest active token" design):** the persisted creds file is the SINGLE durable store; the holder becomes a WRITE-THROUGH cache over it, so BOTH events keep them in sync. (1) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_holder.py` — `TokenHolder(token, *, on_set=None)`: `set()` updates the in-memory token under the lock, then (OUTSIDE the lock — it may do file I/O) calls the optional `on_set` persist hook; construction does NOT persist (only an explicit set propagates). (2) `brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` — `start_token_keepalive` builds the holder with an `on_set` that write-throughs the token to the 0600 creds file (preserving the client id), best-effort (logs `auth.token_persist_failed`, NEVER raises — a persist failure can't crash a renewal mid-pull). So a keepalive renewal now persists the rotated token → a restart re-loads the LIVE token (gap (b) closed). NEW `refresh_live_token(access_token) -> bool`: updates the installed holder in place (write-through) + tells the keepalive (NEW `set_live_keepalive` seam) to `forget_expiry()`; returns `False` when no live session is installed. (3) `brutex/adapters/dhan/token_keepalive.py` — NEW `TokenKeepalive.forget_expiry()`: drops the learned `_expiry_deadline` so the next `_tick` RE-LEARNS the new token's JWT `exp` offline (or renews if <12h) — no stale schedule after a save. (4) `brutex/dashboard/app.py` — `api_credentials_set` calls `refresh_live_token(body.access_token)` after the file save, so a saved token goes live with ZERO restart (gap (a) closed); the lifespan shutdown clears `set_live_keepalive(None)` alongside the holder. **Security (deliberate, no-illusion):** the single store stays the 0600 `credentials.json` file (never committed, never in the browsable DuckDB lake) — a secret token must NOT land in the `/db` tables the operator browses, or it leaks; the file is the durable single-source, not the DB. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all 4 source + 3 test files; `interrogate … --fail-under=100` PASSES on token_holder.py / token_keepalive.py / pull_controller.py locally; the full pytest/mypy/pyright/100%-coverage gate runs on CI (this dev container is Python 3.11 without the runtime deps). NEW tests: `test_dhan_token_holder.py::test_on_set_write_through_persists_each_set` (construction silent, every set persists in order — both `on_set` branches); `test_dhan_token_keepalive.py::test_forget_expiry_clears_learned_deadline`; `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py::TestRefreshLiveToken` ×3 (no-holder→False, holder+keepalive→updates+forget_expiry, holder-without-keepalive→updates — covering both `holder is None` and `keepalive is not None` arms + `set_live_keepalive`). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a saved token goes live without a restart; a renewed token is persisted so a restart re-loads the live token; one durable store, always the latest active token, synced on save AND renew. 🟡 the write-through persist is best-effort — a (rare) file-write failure logs `auth.token_persist_failed` and leaves the in-memory token live for the session but the file stale until the next successful set (a restart then would need a re-paste); the store is the 0600 file, not LMDB (a same-design swap if ever wanted). The keepalive's per-tick deadline is reset on save but the client_id captured at keepalive-start is reused by the persist hook (a mid-session client_id change is preserved because the handler writes the full creds first). 🚫 no change to the rate caps, the ingest spine, the engine, or the JWT-exp learning (#592). **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RENEW-SINGLE-OWNER-001 (#592, the JWT-exp learning + single-renewer this completes) · DEC-DHAN-TOKEN-KEEPALIVE-001 (the holder/keepalive seam) · DEC-DHAN-CREDS-WIRING-001 (the file resolver that reads the single store) · DEC-DHAN-RENEWTOKEN-ROTATE-001 (#583, why a rotated token must be persisted) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 · §11 COMMON (one source of truth) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 (2026-06-08)

595. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 — let the 429 ladder ease BELOW 3 r/s under a SUSTAINED storm + fix the `on_success` recovery bug that left the rate pinned at the floor for the rest of a pull** (2026-06-08, operator 90-min live log: `current_rps=3.0` with `recent_hits` pinned at ~179 for 3.5 min on a band of symbols (every call 429'd even at 3 r/s), and the rate then NEVER recovered above 3 for the remaining ~50 min of the pull). **Root cause (two coupled defects in `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`):** (a) **floor too high.** The 429 ladder hard-clamped at `FLOOR_RPS=3` (`if … and self._rps > FLOOR_RPS`) — "a quota breach is no reason to crawl" — but a RELENTLESS storm where Dhan rejects *every* call even at 3 r/s proves 3 is still too fast; the controller had nowhere lower to ease (unlike the TIMEOUT ladder, already allowed to reach `TIMEOUT_FLOOR_RPS=1` by DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001), so it spun pinned at 3 getting 100%-rejected. (b) **recovery permanently blocked.** `on_rate_limit` clears `_hits` ONLY inside its step-down branch, which cannot fire at the floor (`rps > FLOOR_RPS` False) — so `_hits` stayed pinned at its rolling-window count; and `on_success` evicted only `_timeouts`, NEVER `_hits`, so `not self._hits` was never True and the rate could never step back up to 5 once a storm reached the floor (the operator's "3 r/s for the whole run after one storm"). **What shipped:** (1) NEW constants `RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS = TIMEOUT_FLOOR_RPS (1.0)` + `STORM_HITS = 30`. `on_rate_limit` is now a TWO-TIER ladder: it reaches the SOFT `FLOOR_RPS` (3) quickly on a brief burst (`STEP_DOWN_HITS=3`), but eases BELOW it toward `RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS` (1) ONLY on the higher SUSTAINED-evidence `STORM_HITS` threshold (`threshold = STEP_DOWN_HITS if rps > FLOOR_RPS else STORM_HITS`; clamp `rps > RATE_LIMIT_STORM_FLOOR_RPS`). At 3 r/s, 30 hits ≈ 10 s of 100%-rejection — an unmistakable storm, not a quota nudge — so a transient burst still rests at 3 while a true cascade can finally back off. (2) `on_success` now evicts aged `_hits` AND `_timeouts` (was timeouts-only), so once a storm clears and its hits age out of the 60 s window, recovery proceeds 1→2→3→4→5 instead of staying stuck at the floor. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion):** `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `interrogate … --fail-under=100` PASSES on rate_control.py locally; the full pytest/100%-branch-coverage gate runs on CI (this dev container is Python 3.11 and CANNOT import the test chain — `brutex.orchestrator.retry` uses 3.12 `def retry_call[T]` generics — so the suite runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, NOT fabricated here). NEW/updated tests in `test_dhan_rate_control.py`: `test_brief_429_burst_clamps_at_soft_floor_3` (sub-storm burst rests at 3), `test_sustained_429_storm_eases_below_soft_floor_to_storm_floor` (3→2→1 on STORM_HITS each), `test_429_clamps_at_storm_floor_never_below_1` (the `rps > storm_floor` False arm), `test_recovery_unblocked_after_storm_hits_age_out` (the on_success `_hits`-evict True arm — the bug fix), and `test_on_success_blocked_by_recent_hit` rewritten so the blocking hit is genuinely IN-window (the eviction-False arm). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a sustained 429 storm now backs off to 1 r/s (room for Dhan to recover) instead of spinning pinned at 3, and the controller recovers to 5 after the storm clears instead of crawling for the rest of the pull. 🟡 easing to 1 r/s does NOT make Dhan accept the calls — it reduces the hammering + lets the vendor recover; a storm outlasting the window still defers windows to the next pull (no worse than before; the auto-resume #593 + the per-symbol watchdog #533 cover that). The in-run retry curb (defer instead of re-pile under a pinned-at-floor storm) is intentionally LEFT to the watchdog (#533) rather than duplicated here — out of scope. The `STORM_HITS=30` / deep-floor=1 values mirror the timeout ladder's relief-valve design; tunable. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s ceiling / 100k-day quota, the token bucket, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHEN/HOW LOW the 429 ladder eases + the recovery eviction. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001 (the timeout deep-floor this mirrors for 429s) · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the ladder this extends) · DEC-DHAN-RATE-SINGLE-BUCKET-001 (the single shared bucket the rate mutates) · DEC-RATE-STORM-WATCHDOG-001 (#533, the complementary give-up/alert this does not duplicate) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the retry-to-clean this composes with) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) hooks) · Rule 6 (≤5 r/s) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-RATE-RECOVERY-TRICKLE-001 (2026-06-08)

596. **DEC-DHAN-RATE-RECOVERY-TRICKLE-001 — let the rate RECOVER under a chronic MILD 429/timeout drip instead of staying pinned at the floor: gate `on_success` recovery on the step-down trigger, not a strictly-empty window** (2026-06-08, follow-up to the #595 4-agent hostile review, which flagged this as a pre-existing HIGH; operator chose to fix it now). **Root cause (residual of the #595 recovery bug, `brutex/adapters/dhan/rate_control.py`):** #595 fixed recovery for a storm that FULLY clears — `on_success` evicts aged `_hits`/`_timeouts`, so once the 60 s rolling window empties to ZERO the rate climbs 1→…→5. But the recovery gate was `not self._hits and not self._timeouts` — it required the window to be STRICTLY empty. Under a CHRONIC mild drip (a handful of 429s — or timeouts — per minute, far BELOW the step-down trigger, e.g. the vendor incidentally rejecting ~2 calls/60 s), the rolling window NEVER fully empties, so `not self._hits` is never True and the rate stays pinned at the floor FOREVER, never probing back toward the ceiling. This is the slow-drip twin of the operator's "never recovered above 3" log: #595 closed the burst-then-clear case; the persistent trickle remained a trap. **What shipped (one gate change):** the recovery condition is now `len(self._hits) < STEP_DOWN_HITS and len(self._timeouts) < STEP_DOWN_TIMEOUT_HITS` (plus the unchanged `_rps < CEILING_RPS` + `now - _last_step >= STEP_UP_WINDOW`). Recovery proceeds whenever NEITHER ladder shows step-down-LEVEL pressure — a mild drip probes up one rung, and if the higher rate genuinely storms, the ladder steps straight back down (self-correcting AIMD); genuine `>= STEP_DOWN_HITS` pressure still HOLDS the rate. The threshold bites only AT/BELOW the floor: above it `on_rate_limit`/`on_timeout` already clear their deque on every step (so at most `STEP_DOWN_HITS-1` ever sit in the window and recovery there is purely `STEP_UP_WINDOW`-timer gated); at/below the floor — where no further step clears the deque — a real drip is what holds recovery, giving correct hysteresis (a moderate sustained-rejection band holds; a faint incidental drip recovers). O(1): `len()` on a deque. The `on_success` aged-out eviction (#595) is unchanged. **Verified (HONEST — no illusion, REAL local run):** unlike #595 (run only on CI), this branch's tests were executed locally on **Python 3.12.3** (a throwaway venv with `pytest`+`structlog`+`lmdb`) — `tests/unit/test_dhan_rate_control.py` = **37 passed**, and `pytest --cov=brutex.adapters.dhan.rate_control --cov-branch` = **100.00% line + branch** on `rate_control.py`. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean; `interrogate --fail-under=100` PASS. The full mypy/pyright/mutation/property gate runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. NEW/updated tests: `test_mild_trickle_does_not_block_recovery` (a lone in-window 429 now recovers — the core fix, the True arm), `test_step_down_pressure_at_floor_blocks_recovery` (a `>= STEP_DOWN_HITS` drip at the floor with the timer met still HOLDS — the hit-gate False arm), `test_mild_timeout_drip_does_not_block_recovery` (timeout-side True arm; replaces the old `test_recent_timeout_blocks_then_clears_recovery` whose premise the fix inverts), `test_timeout_pressure_at_floor_blocks_recovery` (timeout-gate False arm), `test_recovery_unblocked_after_timeout_drip_ages_out` (the `on_success` `_timeouts`-eviction body — restores the line the replaced test covered). **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a chronic mild 429/timeout drip no longer pins the rate at the floor — the controller probes back to the ceiling once pressure drops below the step-down level, while a genuine sustained-rejection band still holds it down. 🟡 recovery is a probe: above the floor it steps up once per `STEP_UP_WINDOW` (300 s) whenever the in-window drip is below the step-down trigger, which can cause a slow bounded oscillation around the true sustainable rate (e.g. 4↔5) under borderline load — intended AIMD, never exceeds the 5 r/s ceiling, far better than a permanent pin. The `STEP_DOWN_HITS`/`STEP_DOWN_TIMEOUT_HITS` recovery thresholds reuse the step-down constants (tunable). 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s ceiling / 100k-day quota, the two-tier step-DOWN ladder (#595), the token bucket, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHEN recovery is allowed. **Builds on:** DEC-DHAN-RATE-STORM-FLOOR-001 (#595, the recovery-eviction this completes) · DEC-DHAN-OPTION-TIMEOUT-STORM-001 · DEC-DHAN-ADAPTIVE-RPS-001 (the ladder) · DEC-DHAN-TIMEOUT-BACKOFF-001 (the timeout deque this also gates on) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 5 (O(1) hooks) · Rule 6 (≤5 r/s) · §10.

## DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (2026-06-08)

597. **DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 — a Dhan `DH-905` "no data present" is a SETTLED known-gap, NOT a failed/pending window: stop it pinning every pull at `transient_residual` + the manual "Re-pull to finish" button** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run` over 783 instruments: `universe.pull_all.done … failed=1 pending_windows=1 verdict=transient_residual` on EVERY pull, the single offender being `NIFTY NEXT 50` **1-day**, whose daily history simply starts after 2021-01-01 so Dhan answers `HTTP 400 DH-905 "… no data present"`; operator: *"no data is fine … as long as Dhan returns the successful 200 we should retry; once it completes the chunk it should retry the failed windows and never stop until those alone succeed"*). **Root cause (`brutex/dashboard/pull_controller.py` + `brutex/adapters/dhan/run_ingest.py`):** a `DH-905` is a TERMINAL non-retryable 400, so `run_dhan_spot_ingest` quarantines the `(symbol, interval)` pair into `report.failures` (logged as INFO `ingest.known_gap`, "re-tried next pull, not masked"). But `pull_all_spot` counted EVERY `report.failures` key as a `failed` pair (`SymbolPullResult.failed`), so `total_failed=1` → `classify_pull` returns `transient_residual` (`needs_operator=True`) → the loud `universe.pull_all.action_required` WARNING + the dashboard's amber "⏳ Re-pull to finish" button. A re-pull just hits `DH-905` again → the SAME verdict → a permanent MANUAL loop. This is NOT an auto-retry failure: the in-run 429/timeout retries all succeeded (`still_failed_windows=0` on every symbol), and the auto-resume-until-clean loop correctly did not engage (it fires only on `still_failed_windows>0`, i.e. RETRYABLE transient leftovers). A `DH-905` can NEVER return a 200, so "retry until success" would never terminate — settling it is the correct behavior, exactly as the operator asked ("no data is fine"). **What shipped (one classification change):** in `pull_all_spot`'s per-symbol tally, split the `report.failures` keys into `known_gap_keys` (those whose error matches `is_no_data_message` — `DH-905` / "no data present") vs genuine `failure_keys`. Known-gap pairs are now counted as `no_data` (settled / EMPTY), NOT `failed`. So a symbol like `NIFTY NEXT 50` finishes `completed=1` (1-minute landed bars) + `no_data=1` (the 1-day gap) → `classify_pull` → **`clean`** (`needs_operator=False`); a universe whose ONLY misses are known-gaps → `known_gap_only` (grey, no action). A GENUINE terminal error (a real 400/404 — auth is handled separately by the fail-fast latch) still counts as `failed` → `transient_residual`, unchanged. The pair is still left un-marked (re-attempted next pull, never masked — DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 unchanged), but it no longer POISONS the verdict into a manual re-pull. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** executed on **Python 3.12.3** (venv with the runtime deps) — `tests/unit/test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` = **67 passed**. NEW tests: `test_dh905_no_data_is_settled_not_a_failure` (a `DH-905` on both intervals → `total_failed=0`, `total_no_data=2`, verdict `known_gap_only`, `pending_windows=0`) and `test_daily_gap_with_intraday_data_is_clean` (the EXACT operator case — 1-minute completes, 1-day is a `DH-905` gap → `completed=1`/`failed=0`/`no_data=1` → verdict `clean`, zero manual button). The existing `test_no_data_and_failure_branches` still asserts a GENUINE `DhanBadRequestError("boom …")` → `transient_residual` (genuine errors unaffected). `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ the one-click pull now finishes `clean` with ZERO manual "Re-pull" clicks when the only outstanding items are `DH-905` known-gaps (the operator's NIFTY NEXT 50 daily trap is gone); the auto-resume loop still drives every RETRYABLE transient window to success. 🟡 a `DH-905` pair is still re-attempted on the NEXT pull (1 wasted Dhan call/pull out of the 100k/day quota — negligible; the no-mask philosophy is preserved so a gap that later gains data is picked up). Permanently marking it settled in the coverage skip-ledger is a separate, larger follow-up (touches the daily-anchor %CHNG safety) — out of scope here. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the rate ladder, the token spine, the ingest spine, or the engine — only how a `DH-905` outcome is CLASSIFIED for the verdict. **Builds on:** DEC-PULL-VERDICT-001 (the verdict this corrects) · DEC-DHAN-NO-DATA-KNOWN-GAP-001 (the `ingest.known_gap` INFO log this aligns the tally with) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the retry-to-clean loop this clarifies fires on transient windows) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the no-mask re-attempt, unchanged) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (no hallucination — `DH-905` is the verified Dhan no-data marker) · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.

## DEC-FAILED-WINDOW-FORCE-REPULL-001 (2026-06-08)

598. **DEC-FAILED-WINDOW-FORCE-REPULL-001 — a `FAILED` window (always a retryable `DhanRateLimitError`/timeout) must be RE-PULLED until it succeeds, not skipped forever because the coarse span-enclosure reconcile marked its internal gap "complete"** (2026-06-08, operator live `make run`: `/coverage/windows` shows **63 FAILED windows** at `bars=0`, `attempts=3`, `last_error=DhanRateLimitError` — e.g. `JSWDULUX` 1-minute 2024-09→2025-09 FAILED while 2022 and 2025-09→2026 are SUCCESS — and they NEVER clear across pulls; the pull itself ends `failed=0 verdict=known_gap_only` (everything skipped). Operator: *"why still this is failed even though when it is dhan ratelimit error … it didn't retry"*). **Root cause (`brutex/dashboard/coverage_reconcile.py` `reconcile_windows` + the skip-ledger):** the lake span is the dataset's **min/max** date (`first_date`..`last_date`); a window that FAILED mid-history has stored bars BOTH before AND after it, so the span ENCLOSES it and the conservative `reconcile_windows` marks it complete in the skip-ledger (the documented "internal gap inside an enclosed span is not detected here" limitation). Once marked complete (and persisted to `fetch_coverage.json`), the ingest SKIPS it on every later pull — so the `DhanRateLimitError` window that exhausted its in-run retry budget on the first pull (correctly left un-marked + deferred to "next pull" by DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001) is on the NEXT pull wrongly marked complete by the enclosure reconcile and never re-fetched → stuck FAILED at 0 bars forever. This is also why the verdict reads `known_gap_only`: the 63 genuinely-missing windows are masked as complete, so nothing re-pulls and the residual looks clean while real data is missing. **Key correctness fact (code-traced, `brutex/adapters/dhan/ingest.py`):** a `FAILED` status row is ALWAYS a *retryable* transient — `status_log.record(..., error_type=type(exc).__name__)` is called ONLY on the `is_retryable(exc)` branch (rate-limit / timeout / transport / 5xx); a TERMINAL `DH-905` no-data is re-raised to the outer quarantine and NEVER recorded `FAILED` (it is a known-gap, settled by DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 #597). So every `FAILED` window is one that SHOULD keep being re-pulled until it succeeds — never a no-data window that would loop forever. **What shipped (the un-mark, NOT a status repaint):** (1) `FetchCoverage.unmark(key)` — O(1) `set.discard`, the idempotent inverse of `mark_complete`. (2) NEW pure `reconcile_failed_windows_for_repull(coverage, status_log)` in `coverage_reconcile.py`: for every window the status log records `FAILED`, `coverage.unmark(...)` it — overriding both the span-enclosure mark AND any stale persisted skip — and returns the count. (3) `pull_controller.py` calls it at pull start in BOTH pull paths, AFTER `reconcile_coverage_with_lake` (so the un-mark WINS) and after `begin_pull_status`. The un-marked windows are then re-fetched THIS pass; the auto-retry / until-clean loop (#593) drives the rate-limit ones to SUCCESS (status flips to SUCCESS naturally via the ingest's `record` on a 200), or — if Dhan genuinely has no data — settles them as a `DH-905` known-gap (#597). **Explicitly rejected (no-illusion):** an earlier draft FLIPPED the stale `FAILED` row straight to `SUCCESS` against the enclosing span. That was WRONG — it would PAINT OVER a genuine data gap (the window has 0 bars; the span only proves data exists *around* it, not *in* it) and hide missing data behind a green label. The screenshot proved the windows are genuinely empty (0 bars, only failed attempts), so the only correct fix is to RE-FETCH them, not relabel them. The un-mark self-heals in both cases (data missing → fetched + recorded SUCCESS; data somehow already present → re-fetch dedups keep-first + records SUCCESS) and can never hide a gap. **Verified (HONEST — REAL local run):** executed on **Python 3.12.3** (venv with the runtime deps) — `tests/unit/test_fetch_coverage.py` + `test_coverage_reconcile.py` + `test_window_status.py` + `test_window_status_store.py` = **46 passed**; `test_dashboard_pull_controller.py` = **67 passed**. NEW tests: `TestReconcileFailedWindowsForRepull` ×5 (a FAILED window un-marked → re-pulled; a SUCCESS/EMPTY row left complete — never needless re-fetch; un-marking an absent window is a safe no-op; empty log → 0) + `test_unmark_drops_a_completed_window` / `test_unmark_absent_window_is_a_noop` on `FetchCoverage`. `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files. The full mypy/pyright/100%-coverage/mutation gate runs on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. **Honest envelope (Golden Rule #10):** ✅ a `DhanRateLimitError`/timeout window is now RE-PULLED on the next pass instead of being skipped forever — the operator's 63 stuck FAILED windows get re-fetched until they succeed, so `/coverage/windows` reaches a true zero by FETCHING the data, not by relabeling it. ✅ the verdict becomes HONEST: while genuinely-missing windows remain, the pull reports `transient_residual` (work still to do) instead of a false `known_gap_only`. 🟡 a window that truly cannot be fetched (Dhan keeps rate-limiting it) is re-pulled every pass until it succeeds — by design ("never stop retrying a retryable window"); the `stop_when_stuck` brake bounds it WITHIN one `make run`, and the next run resumes it. The span-enclosure reconcile still cannot SEE an internal gap directly — this fix uses the per-window status log (the precise signal) to override it for known failures; a full per-window lake-completeness probe is a larger follow-up, not claimed here. 🚫 no change to the 5 r/s / 100k-day caps, the rate ladder, the token spine, the ingest spine, or the engine — only WHICH windows the skip-ledger lets through. **Builds on:** DEC-LAKE-RECONCILE-001 (`reconcile_windows`, whose internal-gap limitation this corrects) · DEC-DHAN-429-RETRY-001 (the in-run retry that leaves a failed window un-marked — this stops the next pull from re-masking it) · DEC-DHAN-NODATA-SETTLED-001 (#597, why a `DH-905` is NOT recorded `FAILED` and so is never force-re-pulled) · DEC-WINDOW-STATUS-001 (the per-window status log this reads) · DEC-AUTO-RESUME-DEFAULT-001 (#593, the loop that drives the re-pulled windows to success) · DEC-FETCH-COVERAGE-001 (the skip-ledger this un-marks into) · CLAUDE.md §2 Rule 1 (Correctness — never hide a gap) · §10 · §11 AUTOMATED.
